title: My First Rice Dumpling
connect: 課文談人生中各種「第一次」，這篇看一位學生第一次包粽子的失敗與收穫。
paragraphs: Last winter, my grandmother taught me to make [[traditional|T-0006]] rice dumplings for the first time. It became one of the most [[memorable|L4-0624]] days of my year. I wanted every dumpling to look [[perfect|T-0001]], so I watched her hands carefully and [[made sure|P-0005]] to wrap each leaf tightly.

My first dumpling was a [[failure|L0-0291]]. I [[accidentally|T-0002]] put in too much rice, and the leaf broke open in the hot water. Sticky rice floated everywhere, and my little brother began to laugh and [[yell|L3-0998]], "Rice soup!" I felt [[embarrassed|T-0003]]. I was also a little [[upset|L0-0342]], because I did not want to [[ruin|L4-0866]] the family dinner, and I was afraid I would [[let her down|P-0004]].

Grandma did not get angry. She smiled and told me that her own first dumpling was even worse. [[Fortunately|T-0007]], we still had [[the rest of|P-0001]] the rice and leaves, so I tried again. This time I used less rice and pulled the string tighter. When Grandma tasted my dumpling, her [[reply|L0-0324]] was short and warm: "Not bad at all!"

That night I [[realized|T-0005]] that a first try does not have to be good to be valuable. Even now, when I [[recall|L4-0803]] that broken dumpling, I smile instead of feeling ashamed. It taught me that mistakes are simply the first steps of learning.
zh: 去年冬天，奶奶第一次教我包傳統的粽子，那成了我這一年中最難忘的日子之一。我希望每個粽子都看起來完美，所以仔細看著她的手，並確認每片葉子都包得緊緊的。
我的第一個粽子是個失敗之作。我不小心放了太多米，葉子在熱水裡裂開，黏黏的米飯漂得到處都是，我弟弟一邊笑一邊大喊：「米湯！」我覺得很尷尬，也有點難過，因為我不想毀了這頓家庭晚餐，而且怕讓她失望。
奶奶一點也沒生氣。她笑著說她自己的第一個粽子還更糟。幸好我們還有剩下的米和葉子，我就再試了一次。這次我放比較少的米，繩子也綁得更緊。奶奶嚐了我的粽子之後，簡短又溫暖地回答：「一點也不差喔！」
那天晚上我領悟到，第一次嘗試不必做得好，也有它的價值。直到現在，每當我回想起那個裂開的粽子，我都是微笑，而不是覺得丟臉。它讓我明白，錯誤只是學習的第一步。

questions.stem: What went wrong with the writer's first dumpling?
options: The leaf was too small to hold any rice.
It broke open in the hot water because of too much rice.
Grandma forgot to give her the string.
The water was not hot enough to cook it.
questions.explain: 第二段說她不小心放了太多米，葉子在熱水裡裂開，故選 (B)。(A) 說葉子太小，是把「米太多」誤讀成「葉子太小」。
questions.evidence: I accidentally put in too much rice, and the leaf broke open in the hot water.

questions.stem: The word "ruin" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: ruin 是「毀掉、搞砸」，作者怕自己的失誤搞砸家人的晚餐，與 spoil 最接近，故選 (A)。finish 是「完成」，沒有破壞的意思。
questions.evidence: I was also a little upset, because I did not want to ruin the family dinner, and I was afraid I would let her down.

questions.stem: How did Grandma most likely feel about the writer's failed dumpling?
options: She was angry and asked the writer to stop.
She thought it was funny and wanted to tell the neighbors.
She was kind and wanted to encourage her granddaughter.
She was too busy to notice it.
questions.explain: 奶奶笑著說自己的第一個粽子更糟，第二次還稱讚「一點也不差」，可見她想鼓勵孫輩，故選 (C)。文中明說她「沒有生氣」，所以 (A) 不對。
questions.evidence: Grandma did not get angry.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Rice dumplings are the hardest food to make.
Younger brothers often laugh at their older sisters.
A good cook never makes any mistakes.
A first failure can be a happy and useful lesson.
questions.explain: 全文從失敗的第一個粽子，到奶奶的鼓勵與最後領悟「錯誤是學習的第一步」，主旨是失敗也能成為有價值的經驗，故選 (D)。(B) 弟弟的笑只是一個小情節。
questions.evidence: It taught me that mistakes are simply the first steps of learning.

vocab.stem: Our school trip was so ______ that I still remember every detail of it.
vocab.explain: 旅行「令人難忘」，所以連每個細節都還記得，memorable 最合語意，故選 memorable。crowded（擁擠的）、poisonous（有毒的）、sensitive（敏感的）都不能說明「還記得細節」。

vocab.stem: I did not mean to hurt her. I ______ stepped on her foot on the crowded bus.
vocab.explain: 不是故意傷到她，所以是「不小心」踩到，accidentally 最適合，故選 accidentally。eagerly（熱切地）與「不是故意」矛盾。

title: The Phone Basket
connect: 課文談過度使用手機，這篇看一個家庭如何用「手機籃」改善家人間的相處。
paragraphs: Last semester, I noticed that my phone was taking over my day. I checked it [[throughout|L0-0039]] breakfast, on the bus, and even at dinner. Every new [[message|T-0010]] made a small sound, and I would stop everything to look at it. [[In fact|P-0008]], I did not see how much it was costing me until my little sister said, "You never listen to me anymore."

Her words hurt, but she was right. When someone is talking and you keep looking at a screen, you [[ignore|T-0012]] that person without meaning to. Friends and family want your [[attention|T-0013]], and a screen can easily steal it. I felt [[disappointed|T-0014]] in myself. Good [[relationships|L0-0233]] need time and care, not just a quick glance.

So my family made a simple plan. During dinner, all phones go into a basket by the door. We [[focus|T-0011]] on the food and on one another. At first it was hard, but soon we began to talk about school, music, and funny things from the day. [[In addition|P-0011]], I started to [[respond|L0-0235]] to my sister's stories with real questions instead of one-word answers.

Phones are not bad. They help us [[communicate|L3-0173]] with friends far away and [[connect|L3-0183]] with people who share our interests. The problem is how we use them. [[Personally|T-0015]], I now find evenings more [[satisfying|T-0008]] when I [[hang out|P-0012]] with my family face to face. My sister's smile that night [[inspired|L4-0538]] me to keep the rule even on weekends.
zh: 上學期我發現手機正在佔據我的一整天。早餐時、公車上，甚至吃晚餐時我都在看手機。每則新訊息都會發出小小的聲音，我就會停下手邊所有事去看。事實上，直到我的小妹說「你都不再聽我說話了」，我才看出這件事讓我付出多大的代價。
她的話讓我受傷，但她說得沒錯。當有人正在說話而你卻一直看著螢幕，你就在無意間忽視了那個人。朋友和家人需要你的注意力，而螢幕很容易把它偷走。我對自己感到失望。好的人際關係需要時間和用心，而不只是匆匆一瞥。
於是我們家訂了一個簡單的計畫：晚餐時，所有手機都放進門邊的籃子裡。我們把心思放在食物和彼此身上。一開始很不容易，但很快我們就開始聊學校、音樂和當天的趣事。此外，我也開始用真正的問題回應妹妹的故事，而不是只用一兩個字敷衍。
手機並不壞。它幫助我們和遠方的朋友溝通，也讓我們和有共同興趣的人連結。問題在於我們怎麼使用它。就我個人而言，現在我覺得當我和家人面對面相處時，夜晚更讓人滿足。那天晚上妹妹的笑容激勵我，即使週末也要遵守這個規定。

questions.stem: What did the writer's family decide to do at dinner?
options: Put all the phones into a basket.
questions.explain: 第三段說晚餐時所有手機都放進門邊的籃子，故選 (B)。(A)、(C) 都是在使用手機，和規則相反。
questions.evidence: During dinner, all phones go into a basket by the door.

questions.stem: Why did the writer's sister say, "You never listen to me anymore"?
options: The writer often looked at the phone while she was talking.
The writer was angry with her every day.
The writer did not want to go home.
questions.explain: 第一、二段指出作者一直看手機而忽視別人，妹妹才會這樣抱怨，故選 (A)。文中沒有提到作者生氣或不想回家。
questions.evidence: When someone is talking and you keep looking at a screen, you ignore that person without meaning to.

questions.stem: The word "respond" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: respond to 是「回應」，作者開始用真正的問題回應妹妹的故事，與 answer 最接近，故選 (B)。
questions.evidence: In addition, I started to respond to my sister's stories with real questions instead of one-word answers.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why smartphones should be banned at school
How to choose a good smartphone
How a family used a simple rule to talk to each other more
How a younger sister taught her brother to play music
questions.explain: 全文講作者被妹妹提醒後，全家用手機籃的規則找回面對面的相處，故選 (C)。作者並不認為手機是壞的，(A) 過度延伸。
questions.evidence: Phones are not bad.

vocab.stem: Please do not ______ the teacher when she is explaining the homework.
vocab.explain: 老師在說明作業時不該「不理會」她，ignore 最合語意，故選 ignore。inspire（激勵）、introduce（介紹）、connect（連接）放進句中語意都不通。

vocab.stem: My mother looked ______ because I forgot to call her after the game.
vocab.explain: 我忘了打電話，媽媽看起來應該是「失望的」，disappointed 最合，故選 disappointed。satisfying 是「令人滿意的」，用來形容事物而非人的感受，且與忘記打電話的結果不合。

title: How Do Animals Sleep?
connect: 課文談動物的睡眠，這篇用一份學生報告看不同動物在海裡與野外怎麼睡。
paragraphs: Have you ever [[wondered|L0-0072]] how animals sleep? For a school report, I read about this and found some [[amazing|T-0016]] facts. People need about eight hours of sleep each night, but the [[average|L0-0181]] sleep time of animals varies a lot. Animals rest in a [[variety|L3-0953]] of ways. [[According to|P-0019]] one science book, some bats sleep [[up to|P-0020]] twenty hours a day, while horses need only a few hours.

Sleeping in the sea is harder. Sea otters [[float|L3-0328]] on the water [[surface|L0-0246]] while they rest. [[For example|P-0018]], they sometimes wrap themselves in seaweed so the water cannot carry them away. Dolphins must [[breathe|L3-0096]] air, so they cannot fall into a deep sleep like we do. Instead, they rest one half of the brain at a time. [[Therefore|T-0017]], they can keep swimming and come up for air whenever they need to.

Wild animals cannot sleep deeply in an open place, or a hungry hunter might find them. Many of them [[avoid|T-0018]] danger by taking short [[naps|L3-0564]] and staying light sleepers. Horses can even sleep standing up, so they can run quickly if something frightens them. It is a little strange to think that a quiet, sleepy [[creature|L3-0202]] may still be ready to run at any moment.

I showed my report to our biology teacher, who is an [[expert|L0-0202]] on animals. She said that all living things need rest, but they have found different ways to stay [[awake|L3-0049]] enough to be safe and sleep enough to stay healthy.
zh: 你有沒有想過動物是怎麼睡覺的？為了一份學校報告，我讀了這方面的資料，發現一些驚人的事實。人類每晚大約需要八小時睡眠，但動物的平均睡眠時間差異很大。動物以各式各樣的方式休息。根據一本科學書，有些蝙蝠一天最多睡二十小時，而馬只需要幾個小時。
在海裡睡覺更困難。海獺休息時漂浮在水面上。例如，牠們有時會把自己纏在海藻裡，這樣水就不會把牠們沖走。海豚必須呼吸空氣，所以不能像我們一樣陷入深層睡眠；牠們改成一次只讓一半的大腦休息。因此，牠們可以一邊游泳，一邊在需要時浮上來換氣。
野生動物不能在空曠的地方沉睡，否則飢餓的獵食者可能會找到牠們。許多動物靠短暫的小睡和淺眠來避開危險。馬甚至可以站著睡覺，所以只要有東西嚇到牠們，就能立刻奔跑。想到一隻安靜、昏昏欲睡的生物，隨時都可能起身奔逃，真有點奇妙。
我把報告拿給生物老師看，她是動物方面的專家。她說所有生物都需要休息，但牠們找到了不同的辦法，讓自己清醒到足以保持安全，又睡得夠多以保持健康。

questions.stem: Why do dolphins rest only one half of the brain at a time?
options: Because they like to swim in the morning.
Because they must breathe air and keep swimming.
questions.explain: 第二段說海豚必須呼吸空氣，不能深睡，所以一次只讓一半大腦休息，才能一邊游一邊浮上來換氣，故選 (C)。
questions.evidence: Dolphins must breathe air, so they cannot fall into a deep sleep like we do.

questions.stem: According to the passage, how can horses react quickly to danger?
options: They only sleep for twenty hours.
They can sleep while standing up.
questions.explain: 第三段指出馬可以站著睡，遇到驚嚇就能立刻奔跑，故選 (D)。「二十小時」是蝙蝠，不是馬，(B) 是混淆。
questions.evidence: Horses can even sleep standing up, so they can run quickly if something frightens them.

questions.stem: The word "float" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: float 是「漂浮」，指在水面上浮著，與 stay on top of water 相同，故選 (A)。dive deep（潛入深處）正好相反。
questions.evidence: Sea otters float on the water surface while they rest.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why cats sleep more than dogs
The different ways that animals sleep and stay safe
How scientists can wake up sleeping animals
Why people need eight hours of sleep
questions.explain: 全文介紹蝙蝠、海獺、海豚、馬等動物各有不同的睡法，並兼顧安全，故選 (B)。(D) 只在第一段當對照，不是主旨。
questions.evidence: Animals rest in a variety of ways.

vocab.stem: Our school has a wide ______ of clubs, from music to robots.
vocab.explain: 學校有各種社團，a wide variety of 是固定用法，故選 variety。distance（距離）、surface（表面）、journey（旅程）都不能和 wide ... of clubs 搭配。

vocab.stem: The doctor told him to ______ slowly and deeply to calm down.
vocab.explain: 要冷靜下來要慢慢深呼吸，breathe 最合語意，故選 breathe。avoid（避免）、float（漂浮）、survive（存活）都不合。

title: Heroes with Tiny Noses
connect: 課文談動物靈敏的嗅覺能幫人類做事，這篇看另一種動物：受訓的大鼠如何探測地雷與疾病。
paragraphs: Most people do not like rats, but in some countries these small animals are real heroes. African giant pouched rats have a very [[sensitive|L0-0162]] nose, and they can [[detect|L3-0235]] smells that humans cannot notice. When I [[came across|P-0024]] a video about them, I was surprised that rats could do such important work.

One job is to find buried landmines left over from old wars. A rat is light, so it usually does not set off a mine when it walks over it. Trainers teach each rat to [[locate|L3-0500]] the smell of one [[specific|L3-0819]] chemical and to scratch the ground to [[alert|L4-0031]] its human partner. A tasty snack is the [[reward|L4-0859]] each time the rat does the right thing. Rats can also check samples from patients who may be [[infected|T-0023]] with a lung [[disease|L0-0023]] called tuberculosis. [[Due to|P-0021]] their noses, they can check many samples in a short time, which helps doctors.

Training takes many months. The rats first learn to follow a small clicking sound that means food. Then they learn to [[perform|L3-0629]] simple tasks, and finally they are tested in real fields. Not every rat can [[manage|L0-0020]] to pass, but it [[turned out|P-0023]] that the friendly [[behavior|L4-0091]] of these animals makes them easy to work with.

I think this is a great example of how an animal's natural [[ability|L0-0011]] can help people. A rat may not look like a hero, but with a good nose and good training, it can make a field safer for farmers and children.
zh: 大部分的人不喜歡老鼠，但在某些國家，這些小動物是真正的英雄。非洲大頰囊鼠有非常靈敏的鼻子，能偵測到人類注意不到的氣味。當我偶然看到一支關於牠們的影片時，我很驚訝老鼠竟能做這麼重要的工作。
其中一項工作是找出戰爭遺留下來、埋在地下的地雷。老鼠很輕，所以走過地雷時通常不會觸發它。訓練員教每隻老鼠找出某種特定化學物質的氣味，並用抓地來通知牠的人類夥伴。每次老鼠做對，就會得到美味的點心當獎賞。老鼠也能檢查可能感染肺部疾病「結核病」的病人樣本。由於牠們的鼻子，牠們能在短時間內檢查很多樣本，這對醫生很有幫助。
訓練要花好幾個月。老鼠先學會跟隨一個代表有食物的小小喀噠聲，接著牠們學會執行簡單的任務，最後在真正的田地裡接受測試。不是每隻老鼠都能通過，但結果發現這些動物友善的行為讓牠們很容易合作。
我認為這是動物天生能力能幫助人類的好例子。老鼠看起來也許不像英雄，但靠著靈敏的鼻子與良好的訓練，牠能讓農民與孩子的田地更安全。

questions.stem: How do the rats tell their human partners that they have found a mine?
questions.explain: 第二段說老鼠會抓地來通知人類夥伴，故選 (C)。吃點心是找對之後的獎賞，不是通知方式，(D) 是混淆。
questions.evidence: Trainers teach each rat to locate the smell of one specific chemical and to scratch the ground to alert its human partner.

questions.stem: The word "reward" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: reward 是「獎賞」，老鼠做對就得到點心，故選 (A) 做得好得到的獎勵。
questions.evidence: A tasty snack is the reward each time the rat does the right thing.

questions.stem: Why are rats useful for finding landmines?
options: They are strong enough to dig up the mines.
They can fly over the fields.
They have good noses and are light enough not to set off mines.
questions.explain: 文中提到老鼠鼻子靈敏，且因為身體輕，走過時通常不會觸發地雷，故選 (D)。
questions.evidence: A rat is light, so it usually does not set off a mine when it walks over it.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Trained rats use their sense of smell to help people in important ways.
Rats are the most dangerous animals in the world.
Doctors should keep rats at home.
Every rat can be trained in a week.
questions.explain: 全文介紹受訓大鼠用嗅覺找地雷、檢查疾病樣本，主旨是 (A)。(D) 與文中「訓練要花好幾個月」矛盾。
questions.evidence: I think this is a great example of how an animal's natural ability can help people.

vocab.stem: Drivers must stay ______ when they drive at night, or they may not see danger in time.
vocab.explain: 夜間開車必須保持「警覺」才能及時看到危險，alert 最合語意，故選 alert。poisonous（有毒的）、crowded（擁擠的）、infected（被感染的）都不能形容駕駛人要保持的狀態。

vocab.stem: Please be ______. Tell me exactly which room you want to book.
vocab.explain: 要求對方說出確切的房間，所以要「具體的」，specific 最合語意，故選 specific。infected（被感染的）、romantic（浪漫的）不合；sensitive（敏感的）不是描述說話清不清楚。

title: The Beach Clean-up
connect: 課文談塑膠袋對環境的傷害，這篇看一個班級在海邊淨灘時的親身觀察。
paragraphs: Last Saturday, our class went to a small beach near our school for a clean-up day. I [[eagerly|T-0026]] agreed to [[come along|P-0026]] because I love the sea. But when we arrived, I was shocked. The sand was [[surrounded|L3-0871]] by trash that stretched along the shore.

Most of the garbage was [[plastic|L3-0645]]: bottles, straws, bags, and pieces too small to count. Some of it had [[drifted|L4-0318]] in from the sea, and some had been left by visitors. The beach was not [[crowded|T-0027]] that morning, but it was full of waste. We wore gloves and picked up everything we could find.

Plastic is a useful [[product|L3-0675]] because of its [[convenience|L4-0211]]: it is light, cheap, and strong. But that strength is also a problem, because plastic can stay in nature for hundreds of years. Fish and seabirds sometimes eat small pieces, and this can [[harm|L3-0383]] them. If we do not throw trash away [[properly|T-0031]], it may [[end up|P-0030]] in the ocean.

We worked for three hours. When we were done, we [[packed up|P-0027]] our gloves and carried the full bags to the truck. Our teacher showed us how to sort the waste for [[recycling|T-0029]]. [[Obviously|T-0028]], one class cannot clean the whole sea. Still, protecting the [[environment|T-0030]] begins with small actions like this one, and I will bring my own bag next time.
zh: 上星期六，我們班到學校附近的一個小海灘進行淨灘活動。我熱切地答應同行，因為我很愛海。但當我們抵達時，我嚇了一跳。沙灘被沿著海岸綿延的垃圾包圍著。
大部分垃圾是塑膠：瓶子、吸管、袋子，還有多到數不清的小碎片。有些是從海上漂來的，有些是遊客留下的。那天早上海灘並不擁擠，卻到處都是廢棄物。我們戴上手套，把能找到的東西都撿起來。
塑膠因為方便而成為好用的產品：它輕、便宜又堅固。但這種堅固也是問題，因為塑膠可以在自然界裡留存幾百年。魚和海鳥有時會吃進小碎片，這可能傷害牠們。如果我們不妥善處理垃圾，它就可能最後流入海洋。
我們工作了三小時。結束後，我們收好手套，把裝滿的垃圾袋搬到卡車上。老師還教我們如何分類以便資源回收。顯然，一個班級沒辦法清乾淨整片海。不過，保護環境就是從這樣的小行動開始，下次我會自備袋子。

title: The Tower in Paris
connect: 課文談自由女神像這座象徵性的地標，這篇看另一座地標：巴黎鐵塔如何從臨時建築變成城市的象徵。
paragraphs: My classmate Wendy just came back from a trip to Paris. She [[paid a visit to|P-0034]] the Eiffel Tower and showed us her photos in class. "It looks much bigger in person," she said. Her pictures made me want to learn more about this tower, so I went to the library after school.

Today the tower is a famous [[landmark|L4-0577]] and a top [[attraction|L4-0075]] for every [[tourist|L3-0919]] who goes to France. Yet it was built as part of a big [[celebration|L4-0129]], a world fair held in Paris in 1889. The builders were asked to make something that nobody had seen before. The iron tower rose to about three hundred meters, taller than any other building in the world at that time.

Many people did not like it at first. [[Even though|P-0031]] some artists called it ugly, the tower stayed. It was supposed to be [[removed|L0-0049]] after twenty years, but it proved useful for sending radio signals. [[Over time|P-0033]], people got used to it and even began to love it.

Now the tower stands [[firmly|T-0033]] above the city. It does not look like an [[ancient|T-0034]] [[monument|L4-0651]] or a [[statue|L3-0838]] of a famous person, but for many people it [[symbolizes|L6-0899]] Paris itself. To people around the [[globe|L4-0449]], it can [[represent|L3-0720]] a dream of traveling far from home.
zh: 我的同學 Wendy 剛從巴黎旅行回來。她去參觀了艾菲爾鐵塔，並在班上給我們看她的照片。她說：「實物看起來大多了。」她的照片讓我想多了解這座塔，於是放學後我去了圖書館。
今天，這座塔是著名的地標，也是每位到法國的觀光客必去的熱門景點。然而它當初是為了一場大型慶典而建，那是 1889 年在巴黎舉辦的世界博覽會。建造者被要求做出前所未見的東西。這座鐵塔高約三百公尺，在當時比世界上任何其他建築都高。
一開始許多人並不喜歡它。雖然有些藝術家說它很醜，這座塔還是留了下來。它原本預計二十年後拆除，但後來發現它對發送無線電訊號很有用。隨著時間過去，人們習慣了它，甚至開始愛上它。
現在這座塔穩穩地矗立在城市上空。它看起來不像古老的紀念碑，也不像某位名人的雕像，但對許多人來說，它象徵著巴黎本身。對全世界的人而言，它可以代表一個遠行的夢想。

The tallest buildings in the world today
questions.explain: 全文講艾菲爾鐵塔從為博覽會而建、受批評，到成為巴黎象徵的過程，故選 (B)。(D) 只是第二段提到當時最高，並非全文重點。
questions.evidence: Over time, people got used to it and even began to love it.

vocab.explain: 長城是每年吸引數百萬人造訪的熱門「景點」，attraction 最合，故選 attraction。freedom、treatment、slavery 都不能表示地點。

vocab.explain: 橋不再安全所以下個月會被「拆除」，removed 最通順，故選 removed。celebrated（慶祝）、symbolized（象徵）、represented（代表）不合橋被拆除的語意。

title: Music from a Bucket
connect: 課文談用回收物做樂器追求音樂夢，這篇看一位台灣國中生如何用舊水桶和水管組成樂隊。
paragraphs: Mei-ling joined the band at her junior high school, but the band had a big problem. It could [[barely|L3-0065]] pay for new [[instruments|T-0037]]. The old drums were broken, and one new flute cost more than her family spent on food in a month. Her teacher told the students to [[look for|P-0037]] other ways to make music.

[[Somehow|L3-0815]], Mei-ling had an idea. She asked her neighbors for old things they no longer needed, and soon the band had [[tons of|P-0036]] junk: plastic buckets, metal pipes, and empty bottles. A bucket became a drum. Long pipes of different sizes made deep, warm sounds when the students blew into them. At first the music sounded terrible, and some classmates laughed. Mei-ling felt tired, but her friends' [[encouragement|L0-0010]] kept her going. She had real [[determination|L4-0277]] and a quiet [[faith|L3-0309]] in her team.

In the spring, the band decided to [[apply|L0-0129]] for a place in the city's youth [[concert|L3-0178]]. A month later, they [[received|T-0038]] a letter saying they were in! On the night of the show, the hall was quiet at first, and then the audience clapped for a long time. One judge said the group had great [[potential|L4-0753]]. For the students, it was a small [[triumph|L4-0968]]. Mei-ling now hopes to [[pursue|L4-0792]] music at university, and the band [[looks forward to|P-0039]] next year's show.
zh: 美玲加入了國中的樂隊，但樂隊有個大問題：他們幾乎付不起買新樂器的錢。舊鼓都壞了，一支新長笛的價錢比她家一個月的伙食費還高。老師要同學們另外想辦法做音樂。
美玲不知怎麼地想到了一個點子。她向鄰居要不再需要的舊東西，很快樂隊就有了一大堆廢物：塑膠水桶、金屬管子和空瓶子。一個水桶變成了鼓。不同大小的長管子，被學生吹起來會發出低沉溫暖的聲音。一開始音樂聽起來很糟，有些同學還笑他們。美玲覺得很累，但朋友們的鼓勵讓她撐下去。她有真正的決心，也默默地相信自己的團隊。
春天時，樂隊決定申請參加市裡青少年音樂會的名額。一個月後，他們收到一封信，說他們入選了！演出當晚，大廳起初很安靜，接著觀眾鼓掌了很久。一位評審說這個團體很有潛力。對學生們來說，這是一個小小的勝利。美玲現在希望能到大學繼續追求音樂，而樂隊也期待著明年的演出。

questions.stem: Why did the school band need to find other ways to make music?
options: They did not have enough money for new instruments.
The teacher did not like the old drums.
Mei-ling's family did not allow her to play the flute.
The band had too many members.
questions.explain: 第一段說樂隊幾乎付不起新樂器的錢，所以老師要學生另找方法，故選 (A)。(B) 文中只說舊鼓壞了，並沒有說老師不喜歡。

questions.stem: What did the students use to make their instruments?
options: Wood and metal bought from a shop
Cheap drums from a city market
questions.explain: 第二段說美玲向鄰居要不需要的舊東西，樂隊因此有了水桶、水管和空瓶，故選 (B)。(A) 文中沒有說他們花錢買材料。
questions.evidence: She asked her neighbors for old things they no longer needed, and soon the band had tons of junk: plastic buckets, metal pipes, and empty bottles.

questions.stem: The word "potential" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: potential 指「潛力」，也就是未來可以發展得更好的能力，與 ability to grow 最接近，故選 (B)。評審是在稱讚樂隊，(A) 壞運氣不合。
questions.evidence: One judge said the group had great potential.

options: How to buy cheap flutes online
Why some classmates laughed at music

questions.explain: 全文從沒錢買樂器、用舊物做樂器、到登上音樂會，主軸是美玲把舊物變成樂隊並圓了小小的夢，故選 (C)。(B) 同學的笑聲只是第二段的小細節。

vocab.stem: A new bike is expensive, so he can ______ afford one with the money he saved.
vocab.explain: 新腳踏車很貴，他存的錢「幾乎」買不起，barely afford 是常見搭配，故選 barely。easily（輕易地）與「很貴」矛盾。
