title: Why Did I Buy That?
connect: 課文談便利商店的行銷策略，這篇看一位學生在超市做小調查，發現商品擺放如何影響顧客。
paragraphs: Jason went to a big supermarket with his sister to buy milk. He had a list in his hand, but at the checkout he found two bags of candy in the basket. "I did not plan to buy these," he said.

For a school project, Jason went back to the market with a notebook. The milk was at the very back of the store, so every [[customer|T-0042]] had to walk past many other things first. Snacks were [[visible|L3-0964]] at eye level, and the cheaper brands were on the bottom shelf, where they were hard to see. At the front, a long [[display|L0-0116]] of sweets stood beside the checkout. Some people were [[likely to|P-0042]] pick one up while they [[lined up|P-0044]]. Jason also saw signs like "Buy two, get one free," an [[offer|T-0041]] that made small things look like a great deal.

Jason learned that stores use a clever [[strategy|L3-0852]]. They want you to feel the [[urge|L4-0973]] to buy something you do not need. A sudden [[impulse|L5-0450]] can easily make a [[purchase|L5-0681]] feel like a good idea at the time. He felt a little angry, but he also found the idea [[familiar|L3-0311]]: his mother had often said, "Never go shopping when you are hungry."

Now Jason is more [[aware|L3-0052]] of these small tricks. He is [[eventually|T-0043]] able to leave the store with only what he needs. His classmates now ask him to teach them how to [[take advantage of|P-0045]] sales without wasting money.
zh: 傑森和姐姐去大超市買牛奶。他手上拿著購物清單，但到了結帳處卻發現籃子裡多了兩袋糖果。「我本來沒打算買這些。」他說。
為了學校的專題，傑森帶著筆記本又回到超市。牛奶放在店的最後面，所以每位顧客都得先經過許多其他商品。零食放在視線高度很顯眼，比較便宜的牌子則放在最底層的架子，很難看見。在店的前面，結帳櫃檯旁立著一長排甜食陳列。有些人在排隊時很可能會順手拿一包。傑森還看到「買二送一」之類的標語，這種優惠讓小東西看起來像是很划算。
傑森發現店家用了聰明的策略。他們想讓你產生想買不需要的東西的衝動。一時的衝動很容易讓買下去的當下覺得是個好主意。他有點生氣，但也覺得這個想法很熟悉：媽媽常說：「肚子餓的時候不要去買東西。」
現在傑森對這些小把戲更有警覺了。他最後總能只買需要的東西就離開商店。同學們現在也請他教大家如何利用特價又不浪費錢。

questions.stem: Why was the milk at the back of the store?
options: So customers would pass many other things first.
Because milk is heavier than candy.
Because the store had no room at the front.
So children could not reach it.
questions.explain: 第二段說牛奶放在最後面，所以顧客得先經過許多商品，意思是讓人順便看到、買到其他東西，故選 (A)。文中沒有提到重量或空間。
questions.evidence: The milk was at the very back of the store, so every customer had to walk past many other things first.

questions.stem: The word "strategy" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: strategy 是「策略」，指為了達成目標而擬定的計畫，與 a careful plan 最接近，故選 (A)。標語只是策略的一部分，(B) 不對。
questions.evidence: Jason learned that stores use a clever strategy.

questions.stem: What can we infer about Jason at the end of the passage?
options: He will never go to a supermarket again.
He thinks all stores are bad.
He wants to start his own store.
questions.explain: 最後一段說他現在對這些小把戲更有警覺，最後總能只買需要的東西就離開，可推論他購物變得更小心，故選 (B)。他只是變警覺，並沒有說再也不去超市。
questions.evidence: He is eventually able to leave the store with only what he needs.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why candy is bad for children
How store tricks can make people buy more, and how to avoid them
How a teacher gave Jason a high score
questions.explain: 全文從意外買了糖果，到研究超市擺放與優惠，最後學會避免衝動消費，主旨是店家的小把戲與因應之道，故選 (C)。(B) 並未討論糖果對健康的影響。
questions.evidence: Now Jason is more aware of these small tricks.

vocab.stem: The ______ asked the waiter for a menu and a glass of water.
vocab.explain: 向服務生要菜單和水的是「顧客」，故選 customer。其餘三者都不是人。

vocab.stem: When the sun came out, the rainbow became ______ in the sky.
vocab.explain: 太陽出來後彩虹在天空中變得「看得見」，be visible 最通順，故選 visible。familiar（熟悉的）不能形容彩虹出現的狀態。

title: A Wall That Tells a Story
connect: 課文討論塗鴉究竟是藝術還是破壞，這篇看一個社區如何讓學生合法地在牆上作畫。
paragraphs: On the way to school, Amy walked past a long gray wall every day. One morning someone had sprayed words and strange pictures on it without asking. Her neighbor said it was a [[mess|L3-0534]] and a [[criminal|L3-0206]] act. But Amy was not so sure. The pictures looked [[detailed|T-0046]], and she felt that the artist wanted to [[express|T-0047]] something.

At the next class meeting, students shared their [[opinions|T-0048]]. Some said such paintings were [[destructive|L5-0282]] because the owner had to pay to clean the wall. Amy's teacher listened and then said, "[[When it comes to|P-0052]] art, we should ask two questions: who owns the place, and did the artist have [[permission|L3-0631]]?"

The class decided to make a plan. With help from the city office, they found a wall that the owner was happy to give them. Over three weekends, forty students and their parents painted trees, fish, and birds on it. The strong [[contrast|L4-0208]] between the bright colors and the old gray bricks made the whole street look new. Many people thought the [[visual|L4-0985]] change was wonderful. Each picture [[stands for|P-0049]] a part of the town's history, so people can read the wall like a book.

Amy learned that a good painting needs both talent and [[effort|T-0049]]. It also needs respect for the [[community|L4-0163]]. Now when she hears the word "graffiti," she does not only [[associate|L4-0066]] it with trouble. She thinks about the stories that a wall can tell when everyone agrees to share it.
zh: 每天上學的路上，艾咪都會經過一道長長的灰色牆。有天早上，有人未經詢問就在牆上噴了字和奇怪的圖案。她的鄰居說這是一團亂，也是犯法的行為。但艾咪不太確定。那些圖畫看起來很細緻，她覺得作者想表達些什麼。
在下一次班會上，同學們分享了自己的看法。有些人說這種畫是破壞性的，因為屋主得花錢清洗牆壁。艾咪的老師聽完後說：「談到藝術，我們應該問兩個問題：這個地方是誰的？畫的人有沒有得到許可？」
全班決定擬定計畫。在市府的協助下，他們找到一面屋主樂意提供的牆。在三個週末裡，四十位學生和家長在牆上畫了樹、魚和鳥。鮮豔的顏色與老舊灰磚之間強烈的對比，讓整條街看起來煥然一新。許多人認為這個視覺上的改變很棒。每一幅圖都代表小鎮歷史的一部分，所以人們可以像讀書一樣讀這面牆。
艾咪學到，好的畫作既需要才華也需要努力，還需要尊重社區。現在當她聽到「塗鴉」這個詞，不再只把它和麻煩聯想在一起。她想到的是，當大家都同意共享時，一面牆能說出的故事。

questions.stem: Why did some students say the paintings were destructive?
options: The owner of the wall had to pay for cleaning.
The city did not like art.
questions.explain: 第二段說有些人認為這種畫有破壞性，因為屋主得花錢清洗牆壁，故選 (B)。(A) 文中沒有批評顏色。
questions.evidence: Some said such paintings were destructive because the owner had to pay to clean the wall.

questions.stem: Who helped the students find a wall for their painting?
questions.explain: 第三段寫在市府協助下，他們找到屋主願意提供的牆，故選 (B)。鄰居在第一段是批評的人，(C) 不對。
questions.evidence: With help from the city office, they found a wall that the owner was happy to give them.

questions.stem: The word "it" in "associate it with trouble" (paragraph 4) refers to ______.
questions.explain: 此處的 it 指前一句出現的 the word "graffiti"，意思是艾咪不再只把「塗鴉」這個詞和麻煩聯想在一起，故選 (D)。
questions.evidence: Now when she hears the word "graffiti," she does not only associate it with trouble.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to clean a wall quickly
How students made a legal wall painting and changed their view of graffiti
How a city made a new school
questions.explain: 全文從看到亂噴的牆、討論意見，到合法作畫並改變看法，主旨為學生合法創作並改變對塗鴉的看法，故選 (B)。(C) 文中並未說畫畫就是犯罪。
questions.evidence: She thinks about the stories that a wall can tell when everyone agrees to share it.

vocab.stem: Please ask for ______ before you use my camera.
vocab.explain: 用別人的相機前要先徵求「許可」，ask for permission 是固定說法，故選 permission。其餘選項都無法組成合理的句子。

vocab.stem: It took a lot of ______ to finish the large puzzle in one night.
vocab.explain: 一晚完成大型拼圖需要很多「心力」，take effort 最通順，故選 effort。mess 是「混亂」，不能表示所需的付出。

title: My First Week in Finland
connect: 課文談在羅馬遇到的文化衝擊，這篇看一位台灣交換學生在北歐學校適應新習慣。
paragraphs: Yu-ting is a Taiwanese student who spent a school year in Finland. On her first day, she was [[astonished|L5-0064]] by how quiet everyone was on the bus. In Taiwan, friends often talk loudly, but in Finland people seemed to enjoy the silence. She soon learned that each [[culture|T-0051]] has its own rules, and none of them is wrong.

[[For a start|P-0054]], people there do not use many words when they say hello. A short [[greeting|L4-0464]] and a handshake are enough. Her host mother also told her about an old [[custom|T-0050]]: you take off your shoes at the door, just like in Taiwan. That made Yu-ting smile, because it felt like home.

Another surprise was the school [[schedule|L0-0105]]. The school day starts early, and lunch is free for all students. Her [[daily|T-0054]] life also [[included|T-0055]] a long break in the middle of the morning, when students and teachers sat down to drink hot drinks and chat. She had never seen anything like it, and she thought it was a [[valuable|T-0052]] habit.

[[On the other hand|P-0055]], some things were hard for her. Teachers asked students to think for themselves and ask many questions, but Yu-ting was used to listening quietly. [[Afterward|L3-0015]] she felt shy. But slowly, she learned to [[embrace|L5-0326]] the new ways. By the end of the year, she did not see the [[difference|T-0056]] between the two countries as a problem. Instead, she knew she would carry these memories [[forever|L3-0337]].
zh: 雨婷是一位在芬蘭待了一學年的台灣學生。第一天，她就對公車上每個人那麼安靜感到非常驚訝。在台灣，朋友們常常大聲聊天，但在芬蘭人們似乎很享受安靜。她很快就明白，每個文化都有自己的規矩，而且沒有一種是錯的。
首先，那裡的人打招呼不太用很多話。一句簡短的問候和一次握手就夠了。她的寄宿媽媽還跟她提到一個古老的習俗：進門要脫鞋，就跟台灣一樣。這讓雨婷笑了，因為覺得就像回到家一樣。
另一個驚喜是學校的時間表。學校一天很早開始，所有學生的午餐都是免費的。她的日常生活也包含上午中間一段很長的休息，學生和老師會坐下來喝熱飲、聊天。她從沒見過這樣的事，並覺得這是個很有價值的習慣。
另一方面，有些事對她來說很困難。老師要求學生自己思考並多發問，但雨婷習慣安靜聽課。事後她覺得很害羞。不過慢慢地，她學會接納這些新方式。到了學年結束，她不再把兩個國家的差異看成問題。相反地，她知道自己會永遠帶著這些回憶。

questions.stem: What surprised Yu-ting on her first day in Finland?
options: People on the bus were very quiet.
Her host mother spoke too fast.
questions.explain: 第一段說她對公車上每個人那麼安靜感到驚訝，故選 (B)。文中沒有提到公車擁擠，(A) 是無中生有。
questions.evidence: On her first day, she was astonished by how quiet everyone was on the bus.

questions.stem: Which custom was the same in Finland and Taiwan?
options: Taking off shoes at the door
Sitting down for a morning chat
questions.explain: 第二段寫進門脫鞋的習俗與台灣一樣，故選 (A)。握手和免費午餐在文中是芬蘭的做法，不是兩地相同。
questions.evidence: Her host mother also told her about an old custom: you take off your shoes at the door, just like in Taiwan.

questions.stem: Why did Yu-ting feel shy after some classes?
options: She did not like her teachers.
She was used to listening quietly instead of asking questions.
questions.explain: 最後一段說老師要求學生思考、多發問，但她習慣安靜聽課，所以覺得害羞，故選 (B)。文中沒說她不喜歡老師或聽不懂英文。
questions.evidence: Teachers asked students to think for themselves and ask many questions, but Yu-ting was used to listening quietly.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a student learned to accept a different culture
How to find a good host family
Why schools should serve free lunch
questions.explain: 全文敘述雨婷在芬蘭遇到的各種新習慣，從驚訝到學會接納，主旨是學習接受不同的文化，故選 (A)。(B) 公車安靜只是開頭的一個例子。
questions.evidence: But slowly, she learned to embrace the new ways.

vocab.stem: My grandfather tells us stories about the old ______ of our village.
vocab.explain: 爺爺講的是村子的古老「習俗」，old custom 最合理，故選 custom。其餘三者都無法組成合理意思。

vocab.stem: It is hard to see the ______ between the twin brothers because they look so alike.
vocab.explain: 雙胞胎長得很像，所以難看出兩人的「差異」，故選 difference。include 是動詞，不能接在 the 後面。

title: The Hoop on the Trash Can
connect: 課文談用有趣的設計讓人養成好習慣，這篇看學生用投籃式垃圾桶改善校園亂丟垃圾的問題。
paragraphs: At Hill Junior High School, the yard was full of paper cups and snack bags after lunch. The student council made signs, but nobody read them. "People already know that dropping trash is bad," said Kevin, the council leader. "We need a new way to [[motivate|L4-0653]] them."

Kevin's science teacher once said that a small game can [[improve|T-0058]] a boring [[routine|L3-0746]]. So the council decided to run an [[experiment|L3-0299]]. They put a basketball hoop above each trash can and drew a score line on the ground. Their [[goal|T-0060]] was simple: to see whether students would throw trash into the cans if it felt like a game.

The idea worked better than they had imagined. At first a few students tried it just for fun, and a short [[activity|T-0062]] soon became a daily habit. The council kept a record for two weeks, and they found that the number of cups on the ground went down a lot. It was a [[positive|T-0057]] result. Kevin said, "The cans were [[actually|T-0059]] the same old cans. We just made them fun."

A small idea can be a [[spark|L4-0904]] for a big change. [[Thanks to|P-0059]] the hoops, the yard is now much cleaner. The school hopes to [[promote|L3-0678]] the idea in other places, such as the library and the sports field. They also want to [[take action|P-0057]] on other problems, [[rather than|P-0060]] only talking about them. Kevin smiles when he watches a quiet, [[ordinary|T-0061]] boy score a perfect shot into a trash can.
zh: 山丘國中的操場在午餐後總是滿地紙杯和零食袋。學生會做了標語，但沒有人看。學生會長凱文說：「大家本來就知道亂丟垃圾不對，我們需要用新方法來激勵他們。」
凱文的自然老師曾說，一個小遊戲可以改善無聊的日常。於是學生會決定做一個實驗。他們在每個垃圾桶上方裝一個籃框，並在地上畫了一條得分線。他們的目標很簡單：看看如果像玩遊戲一樣，學生會不會把垃圾丟進桶子裡。
這個點子比他們想像的更有效。一開始只有幾個學生為了好玩去試，很快這項小活動就變成每天的習慣。學生會記錄了兩個星期，發現掉在地上的杯子大幅減少。這是個正面的結果。凱文說：「垃圾桶其實還是原來的垃圾桶，我們只是讓它變得有趣。」
一個小點子可以引發大改變。多虧了籃框，操場現在乾淨多了。學校希望把這個點子推廣到其他地方，例如圖書館和運動場。他們也想對別的問題採取行動，而不是只有說說而已。凱文看到一個安靜、平凡的男生把垃圾精準投進桶子裡時，臉上露出了笑容。

questions.stem: What did the students put above the trash cans?
questions.explain: 第二段說他們在每個垃圾桶上方裝了一個籃框，故選 (B)。只有地上畫了得分線，並沒有計分板，(A) 不對。
questions.evidence: They put a basketball hoop above each trash can and drew a score line on the ground.

questions.stem: What did the student council find after two weeks?
options: Fewer cups were left on the ground.
questions.explain: 第三段寫他們記錄兩週後，發現地上的杯子大幅減少，故選 (A)。標語在第一段就說沒人看，(D) 不對。
questions.evidence: The council kept a record for two weeks, and they found that the number of cups on the ground went down a lot.

questions.stem: Why did Kevin say the cans were "actually the same old cans"?
options: He wanted to buy new cans.
He thought the cans were too old.
He meant that the change came from making them fun, not from new cans.
He did not like the idea.
questions.explain: 凱文是說垃圾桶沒有換，只是讓它們變得有趣，代表成功來自好玩的設計，故選 (C)。他並沒有想買新垃圾桶。
questions.evidence: We just made them fun.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a game idea helped keep a school yard clean
Why basketball is a good sport
Why students should not eat snacks
questions.explain: 全文從操場髒亂、設計投籃垃圾桶到成效，主旨是用遊戲點子讓校園變乾淨，故選 (A)。(B) 籃球只是工具，不是主題。
questions.evidence: Thanks to the hoops, the yard is now much cleaner.

vocab.stem: She made a good plan to ______ her little brother to read every day.
vocab.explain: 用好計畫「激勵」弟弟每天閱讀，motivate 最合語意，故選 motivate。bury（埋）、capture（捕捉）都不合。

vocab.stem: The class made a ______ to finish the project, and everyone worked hard to reach it.
vocab.explain: 全班訂了完成專題的「目標」，大家努力達成，reach a goal 是常見搭配，故選 goal。booth（攤位）無法被 reach 成為努力的對象。

title: Pictures from the Beach
connect: 課文談用影像記錄島嶼之美與受到的傷害，這篇看一位高中生用手機記錄海灘垃圾並推動淨灘。
paragraphs: Hui-wen lives near a beach in Penghu. When she grew older, she began to take pictures with her phone. She did not [[start out|P-0061]] to be a [[photographer|L3-0634]]; she only wanted to [[capture|L3-0124]] the beautiful [[scenery|L4-0873]] around her home.

But one summer, the beach changed. After a big storm, plastic bottles, nets, and bags covered the sand. It was a small [[disaster|L4-0294]] for the sea life there, and the sea was [[no longer|P-0062]] the place she remembered. Hui-wen took photos every day for a month. She wanted to [[record|T-0064]] how things changed, and the pictures became strong [[proof|L3-0680]] that the beach was in trouble. She showed them to her teacher, who said, "Seeing the [[damage|T-0063]] with your own eyes has a stronger [[effect|L0-0009]] than any speech."

Hui-wen posted her photos online and asked friends to join a beach clean-up. Thirty students came on the first weekend, and over a hundred people came the next month. The group kept working, and slowly the work began to [[pay off|P-0065]]. The beach became cleaner. The local government also promised to [[prevent|L3-0670]] more waste from reaching the sea.

Hui-wen knows that one clean-up will not end the problem. Still, she hopes her pictures will have an [[impact|L4-0517]] on people who see them. She now joins a group that works on ocean [[conservation|L5-0206]], and she is [[grateful|L4-0460]] to everyone who helped. She believes that protecting nature is the duty of the people who live there.
zh: 慧雯住在澎湖的一處海灘附近。長大後，她開始用手機拍照。她一開始並不是想成為攝影師，只是想把家附近的美麗風景拍下來。
但有一年夏天，海灘變了。一場大風暴過後，塑膠瓶、漁網和袋子蓋滿了沙灘。這對那裡的海洋生物來說是一場小小的災難，大海也不再是她記憶中的樣子。慧雯連續一個月每天拍照。她想記錄事情是如何變化的，這些照片成了海灘出問題的有力證據。她拿給老師看，老師說：「親眼看到損害，比任何演說的效果都更強。」
慧雯把照片貼上網，邀請朋友參加淨灘。第一個週末來了三十位學生，隔月來了一百多人。團隊持續努力，漸漸地成果開始出現。海灘變乾淨了。地方政府也承諾要防止更多垃圾進入大海。
慧雯知道一次淨灘不能解決所有問題。不過她希望她的照片能對看到的人產生影響。她現在加入一個海洋保育團體，並感謝所有幫忙的人。她相信保護自然是居住在那裡的人的責任。

questions.stem: What did Hui-wen do for a month after the storm?
options: She took photos of the beach every day.
She cleaned the beach by herself.
questions.explain: 第二段說她連續一個月每天拍照記錄海灘的變化，故選 (A)。淨灘是後來邀請朋友一起做的，不是一個人完成，(B) 不對。
questions.evidence: Hui-wen took photos every day for a month.

questions.stem: The word "proof" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: proof 是「證據」，照片證明海灘出了問題，與 evidence 意思最接近，故選 (A)。
questions.evidence: She wanted to record how things changed, and the pictures became strong proof that the beach was in trouble.

questions.stem: What can we infer about the clean-up group?
options: It was started by the local government.
It only had students from her school.
questions.explain: 第三段說第一週末有三十人，隔月超過一百人，可推論團體越來越大，故選 (B)。政府只是後來承諾防止垃圾，並非發起者，(C) 不對。
questions.evidence: Thirty students came on the first weekend, and over a hundred people came the next month.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a student used photos to help protect a beach
How to take better pictures with a phone
questions.explain: 全文從拍照記錄海灘、用照片發起淨灘，到持續保護自然，主旨是學生用照片守護海灘，故選 (A)。(B) 風暴只是事件的起因。
questions.evidence: She believes that protecting nature is the duty of the people who live there.

vocab.stem: The police found no ______ that he had taken the bag.
vocab.explain: 警方找不到他拿了袋子的「證據」，no proof 最通順，故選 proof。scenery（風景）與 impact（衝擊）都無法與 that 子句搭配。

vocab.stem: The heavy rain did great ______ to the crops in the field.
vocab.explain: 大雨對田裡作物造成嚴重「損害」，do damage to 是固定搭配，故選 damage。grateful 是形容詞，不能放在 great 後面當名詞。

title: Run to the Line
connect: 課文談冠軍的決心與毅力，這篇看一位高中女生在比賽中受傷卻堅持跑完全程。
paragraphs: Mei-ling had [[her heart set on|P-0066]] winning the 800-meter race at the city school games. For two years, she trained before sunrise, running alone around the empty track. Her coach often praised her [[dedication|L6-0223]], and her classmates already called her a future [[champion|L3-0134]]. She dreamed of standing on the podium with a gold [[medal|L3-0527]] around her neck.

On the day of the race, things went wrong. Halfway around the second lap, Mei-ling felt a sharp [[pain|T-0066]] in her ankle. It was an [[injury|L3-0434]] she had never had before, and she fell to the ground. The crowd became silent. A doctor [[immediately|T-0067]] ran onto the track to check her leg. Everyone expected her to stop.

But Mei-ling shook her head. She slowly [[rose to her feet|P-0068]] and began to walk, then to jog. She could not [[speed up|P-0067]], and each step was a [[struggle|L0-0150]]. The other runners had already crossed the line, yet the people in the stands stood up and clapped. Her teammates came onto the field and walked beside her, giving her their [[support|T-0069]]. When she finally crossed the line, many of them were crying. It was an [[emotional|L3-0286]] moment for the whole school.

Mei-ling did not win a medal that day, but she won something else. Her classmates talked about her [[courage|T-0068]] for weeks, and the coach said that true [[strength|L3-0854]] is not only about speed. Mei-ling felt [[pride|L0-0229]] in herself, and the [[respect|T-0070]] of others meant more to her than any prize. She learned that [[success|T-0065]] can be measured in more than one way.
zh: 美玲一心一意想在市內學校運動會的 800 公尺賽跑中奪冠。兩年來，她天還沒亮就起床訓練，獨自在空蕩蕩的跑道上跑步。教練常稱讚她的奉獻精神，同學也已經把她看作未來的冠軍。她夢想著站上頒獎台，頸上掛著金牌。
比賽當天，事情出了差錯。跑到第二圈一半時，美玲的腳踝傳來一陣劇痛。這是她從沒經歷過的傷，她摔倒在地。全場一片寂靜。一位醫生立刻跑上跑道檢查她的腿。大家都以為她會放棄。
但美玲搖了搖頭。她慢慢地站起來，開始走，然後慢跑。她無法加速，每一步都是掙扎。其他選手早已越過終點線，但看台上的人都站起來鼓掌。她的隊友們走進場內，陪在她身旁給她支持。當她終於跨過終點線時，許多人都哭了。那對全校來說是個令人動容的時刻。
那天美玲沒有贏得獎牌，卻得到了別的東西。同學們談論她的勇氣談了好幾個星期，教練也說，真正的力量不只與速度有關。美玲為自己感到驕傲，而別人對她的尊敬比任何獎項都重要。她學到，成功可以用不只一種方式來衡量。

questions.stem: What happened to Mei-ling during the race?
options: She lost her shoe on the track.
She hurt her ankle and fell down.
She got lost and ran the wrong way.
questions.explain: 第二段說她跑到第二圈一半時腳踝劇痛而摔倒，故選 (B)。文中沒有提到掉鞋或撞到別人，(A)(D) 皆是文中沒有的情節。
questions.evidence: Halfway around the second lap, Mei-ling felt a sharp pain in her ankle.

questions.stem: The word "dedication" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: dedication 指為目標投入的「奉獻、努力」，教練稱讚她每天清晨苦練，與 serious effort 最接近，故選 (C)。careless（粗心的）與長期苦練相反。
questions.evidence: Her coach often praised her dedication, and her classmates already called her a future champion.

questions.stem: The word "It" in the last sentence of paragraph 3 refers to ______.
options: the coach's talk with the doctor
questions.explain: 前一句說她終於跨過終點線，許多人哭了，所以 It 指的是「她終於跑完全程」這件事，故選 (A)。腳踝的痛發生在比賽中段，並不是令全校動容的時刻。
questions.evidence: It was an emotional moment for the whole school.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to train for a short race
Why doctors work at sports games
How a runner won a gold medal
How a hurt runner showed courage by finishing her race
questions.explain: 全文敘述美玲受傷後仍站起來跑完全程，並因此贏得尊敬，主旨是她的勇氣，故選 (D)。第四段明說她沒有拿到獎牌，(C) 與文意相反。
questions.evidence: Mei-ling did not win a medal that day, but she won something else.

vocab.stem: The football player missed the rest of the season because of a knee ______.
vocab.explain: 球員因膝蓋「傷」而缺席球季，injury 最通順，故選 injury。medal（獎牌）、pride（驕傲）、strength（力量）都不能接在 knee 後當作缺席的原因。

vocab.stem: It takes great ______ to speak in front of the whole school for the first time.
vocab.explain: 第一次在全校面前說話需要很大的「勇氣」，courage 最合理，故選 courage。injury（傷）、pain（痛）、medal（獎牌）都不符語意。

title: Does Noise Change Taste?
connect: 課文談在飛機上味覺為什麼變得不一樣，這篇看一位學生用小實驗測試噪音會不會影響食物的味道。
paragraphs: Wen's uncle works as a flight attendant, and he often tells her that the snacks on a plane taste plain to many [[passengers|L3-0615]]. At home, the same snack seems full of [[flavor|L3-0326]], but in the sky, he says, it is a different story. Wen was curious, so she decided to do some [[research|L4-0837]] for the school science fair.

She learned that taste is not only about the tongue. Our brain also uses smell, sound, and even the room around us to decide what we are eating. In a quiet kitchen, we can easily [[distinguish|L4-0303]] a sweet cookie from a salty one. On a plane, the loud engine noise creates a different [[condition|L0-0026]]. [[Believe it or not|P-0072]], loud sound can [[affect|T-0075]] how sweet food seems.

Wen [[came up with|P-0073]] a simple test. She asked twenty classmates to taste the same tomato soup twice. The first time, they ate it in a quiet room. The second time, they wore headphones that played loud noise. To make the test fair, she used the same soup made from the same [[ingredients|L4-0530]] each time. Wen asked each person to describe the taste [[accurately|T-0073]] on a score card. She also made sure nothing would [[distract|L5-0305]] them.

The results [[indicate|T-0076]] that most classmates found the soup less tasty with the noise. [[Regardless of|P-0075]] whether they liked tomatoes or not, the scores went down. Her uncle smiled and told her that some airlines look for a [[solution|L0-0175]] too: they add stronger spices to meals. [[Normally|T-0072]], Wen never thinks about sound when she eats, but now she knows that eating is a team effort between all our senses.
zh: 小文的叔叔是空服員，他常告訴她，飛機上的點心對許多乘客來說味道很淡。在家裡，同樣的點心充滿風味，但他說在空中就是另一回事。小文很好奇，於是決定為學校的科展做一些研究。
她得知味覺不只跟舌頭有關。我們的大腦還會利用氣味、聲音，甚至周遭的環境，來判斷自己在吃什麼。在安靜的廚房裡，我們很容易分辨甜餅乾和鹹餅乾。在飛機上，巨大的引擎聲形成了不同的條件。信不信由你，很大的聲音會影響食物嚐起來有多甜。
小文想出了一個簡單的測試。她請二十位同學把同一碗番茄湯嚐兩次。第一次在安靜的教室裡吃，第二次戴上播放著大噪音的耳機。為了讓測試公平，她每次都用同樣的材料做出同樣的湯。小文請每個人在評分卡上準確描述味道。她也確保沒有任何東西會讓他們分心。
結果顯示，大部分同學覺得有噪音時，湯比較不好喝。不管他們喜不喜歡番茄，分數都下降了。叔叔笑著告訴她，有些航空公司也在找解決辦法：他們在餐點裡加重香料。平常小文吃東西時從不會想到聲音，但現在她知道，進食是所有感官共同合作的結果。

questions.stem: What did Wen ask her classmates to do?
options: Cook tomato soup in the school kitchen.
Listen to music while writing a report.
Taste the same soup in a quiet room and then with loud noise.
Guess the names of different spices.
questions.explain: 第三段說她請同學把同一碗湯嚐兩次，一次安靜、一次戴著大噪音耳機，故選 (C)。她只是讓同學喝湯，並沒有要大家煮湯，(A) 不對。
questions.evidence: She asked twenty classmates to taste the same tomato soup twice.

questions.stem: The word "indicate" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: indicate 是「顯示、指出」，結果顯示多數同學覺得湯較不好喝，與 show 最接近，故選 (B)。
questions.evidence: The results indicate that most classmates found the soup less tasty with the noise.

questions.stem: Why did Wen use the same soup both times?
options: So that only the noise would be different.
Because she did not have time to cook more.
Because she wanted the soup to taste better.
So that her classmates would finish it quickly.
questions.explain: 文中說「為了讓測試公平」才用同樣的湯，可推知她想讓噪音成為唯一的差別，故選 (A)。文中沒有提到沒時間或想讓湯更好喝。
questions.evidence: To make the test fair, she used the same soup made from the same ingredients each time.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A simple way to cook tomato soup
A student's test on how noise can change the way food tastes
questions.explain: 全文從叔叔的話引出疑問，再說明小文如何設計實驗，主軸是噪音會不會改變味覺，故選 (D)。(A) 叔叔的工作只是開頭引子。
questions.evidence: The results indicate that most classmates found the soup less tasty with the noise.

vocab.stem: Before writing her report, Lisa did some ______ at the library.
vocab.explain: 寫報告前先去圖書館做「研究、查資料」，research 最合理，故選 research。flavor（味道）、pressure（壓力）、condition（狀況）都不能搭配 did some。

vocab.stem: Not getting enough sleep can ______ how well you do on a test.
vocab.explain: 睡眠不足會「影響」考試表現，affect 最通順，故選 affect。announce（宣布）、blame（責怪）、remain（保持）放進句中語意都不通。

title: The Face in the Mirror
connect: 課文談一個人執著於消除小小的缺點，這篇看一位高中女生如何學會接受自己臉上的胎記。
paragraphs: Ya-ting had a small, [[faint|L3-0306]] mark on her left cheek. She had it from birth, and most people could [[hardly|T-0083]] see it. But in every photo she posted online, she used an app to remove it. Her friend Hao often asked her why, and she always said it looked better that way. She was [[stubborn|L3-0857]] about it.

One weekend, her class took a group photo for the yearbook. Ya-ting [[desperately|T-0079]] wanted the photographer to hide the mark. He [[reluctantly|T-0080]] agreed, but the editing took a long time, and the final picture looked strange. Her face did not seem like her own. She felt [[frustration|L4-0426]] rising inside her, so she [[put aside|P-0076]] her phone and stared at the picture for a long while.

That evening, Hao came to visit. Ya-ting had to [[confess|L4-0179]] that she was unhappy with her own face. Hao tried to [[explain|T-0082]] how he saw her. When he had to [[describe|T-0081]] her to others, he never mentioned the mark, only her laugh and her jokes. Ya-ting felt her worry begin to [[fade|L3-0305]]. Looking at an old photo again, she could not find a [[trace|L3-0922]] of anything ugly. Nobody else saw the mark the way she did.

[[From then on|P-0077]], Ya-ting posted her pictures without editing them. At first it felt scary, but she received only kind comments. She felt no [[regret|L3-0709]]. Her friends liked her [[all the more|P-0078]] for being honest. She learned that trying to make everything perfect can hide what is truly lovely.
zh: 雅婷左臉頰上有一個小小的、淡淡的記號。那是她天生就有的，多數人幾乎看不出來。但在她上傳到網路的每張照片裡，她都用修圖軟體把它去掉。朋友阿豪常問她為什麼，她總說這樣比較好看。她在這件事上非常固執。
某個週末，班上拍畢業紀念冊的團體照。雅婷拚命希望攝影師把記號遮掉。他不情願地答應了，但修圖花了很久，最後的照片看起來很奇怪。那張臉不像是她自己的臉。她心中湧起挫折感，於是把手機擱到一旁，盯著那張照片看了好久。
那天晚上，阿豪來拜訪。雅婷不得不坦承自己對自己的臉不滿意。阿豪試著說明他眼中的她。每當他要向別人形容她時，從不提那個記號，只說她的笑聲和笑話。雅婷覺得心裡的煩惱開始淡去。她再看一次舊照片，找不到一絲難看的痕跡。別人根本不像她那樣看待那個記號。
從那時起，雅婷發佈照片時不再修圖。一開始她覺得有點可怕，但收到的全是善意的留言。她一點也不後悔。朋友們因為她的坦率而更喜歡她。她學到，想讓一切完美，可能反而遮住了真正可愛的地方。

questions.stem: Why did Ya-ting use an app on her photos?
options: She wanted her photos to look more colorful.
Her friend Hao asked her to.
She wanted to hide a mark on her cheek.
questions.explain: 第一段說她每張照片都用修圖軟體把臉頰上的記號去掉，故選 (C)。是她自己想這麼做，Hao 反而常問她為什麼，(B) 不對。
questions.evidence: But in every photo she posted online, she used an app to remove it.

questions.stem: The word "stubborn" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 她總是堅持這樣比較好看，不聽朋友的疑問，stubborn 指「固執的」，故選 (B)。她其實對臉不自在，所以 (D) proud 不對。
questions.evidence: She was stubborn about it.

questions.stem: What can we infer from Hao's words about her?
options: He thinks her mark is the most important thing about her.
He never talks to other people about her.
He wants her to edit her photos again.
He values her personality more than her looks.
questions.explain: 他向別人形容她時只提笑聲與笑話，不提記號，可推知他更重視她的個性，故選 (D)。
questions.evidence: When he had to describe her to others, he never mentioned the mark, only her laugh and her jokes.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A girl learns to accept a part of her face that she once wanted to hide
How to take a good group photo
A photographer who is not good at editing
Why friends should not visit each other at night
questions.explain: 全文從她修圖、對照片失望，到朋友開導後坦然發佈原圖，主旨是學會接受自己，故選 (A)。
questions.evidence: She learned that trying to make everything perfect can hide what is truly lovely.

vocab.stem: My grandfather is so ______ that he never changes his mind, even when he is wrong.
vocab.explain: 「從不改變心意、即使錯了也一樣」是固執，故選 stubborn。faint（微弱的）、scary（可怕的）、awful（糟糕的）都無法描述這種個性。

vocab.stem: After a long silence, Tom decided to ______ that he had broken the window.
vocab.explain: 沉默許久後決定「坦承」自己打破窗戶，confess 最合理，故選 confess。depart（離開）、fade（褪色）、shiver（發抖）都不能接 that 子句。

title: A Box of Books
connect: 課文談女孩爭取受教育的權利，這篇看一位台灣學生如何從一封信認識教育機會的不平等並採取行動。
paragraphs: Last autumn, the [[principal|T-0087]] of Hsiao-yu's school announced a book drive. Students could bring in old story books and school supplies to send to a small school in a mountain [[region|L0-0045]] far away. Hsiao-yu was one of the first to join. At first she only wanted to clean her bookshelf, but a letter from that school changed her mind.

The letter was written by a girl named Sana, who was thirteen. She wrote that in her village, many girls leave school early because their families cannot pay, or because they think [[female|T-0084]] students do not need school. Hsiao-yu was surprised. In Taiwan, the government's [[policy|L0-0102]] of free basic [[education|T-0086]] gives every child the chance to learn, and she had never thought of it as something special. She felt that boys and girls should have an [[equal|T-0088]] chance.

Hsiao-yu wanted to do more than send books. She decided to [[speak out|P-0086]] at the school assembly. She spent a week writing her speech and tried to [[persuade|L3-0633]] her classmates that sharing a book can change a life. She also asked them to [[sign|T-0091]] a card for Sana's class. Over two hundred students joined, and teachers began to [[call for|P-0087]] more help from parents.

Months later, a box arrived from Sana's school with drawings and thank-you notes. Sana wrote that she would [[continue|T-0085]] studying and hoped to become a teacher. Her school also planned to [[establish|L4-0360]] a small library. Hsiao-yu knows that a few boxes of books cannot [[ensure|L4-0353]] that every child has a place in school, yet she feels she has taken the first step.
zh: 去年秋天，筱瑜學校的校長宣布要舉辦圖書募集活動。學生可以帶來舊的故事書和學用品，寄給遙遠山區的一所小學校。筱瑜是最早加入的人之一。起初她只是想整理自己的書架，但那所學校寄來的一封信改變了她的想法。
那封信是一位名叫莎娜的十三歲女孩寫的。她寫道，在她的村子裡，許多女孩很早就離開學校，因為家裡付不起費用，或是認為女學生不需要上學。筱瑜很驚訝。在台灣，政府的免費基本教育政策讓每個孩子都有學習的機會，她從沒覺得這有什麼特別。她覺得男孩和女孩都應該有平等的機會。
筱瑜想做的不只是寄書。她決定在學校的集會上發聲。她花了一個星期寫講稿，試著說服同學，分享一本書可以改變一個人的人生。她也請大家在要給莎娜班上的卡片上簽名。超過兩百名學生參加，老師們也開始呼籲家長提供更多協助。
幾個月後，一個箱子從莎娜的學校寄來，裡面有圖畫和感謝卡。莎娜寫道她會繼續念書，希望成為老師。她的學校也計畫設立一間小圖書室。筱瑜知道，幾箱書無法確保每個孩子都有學校可念，但她覺得自己已經踏出了第一步。

questions.stem: What was the book drive for?
options: Sending books and supplies to a small school far away
Building a new library at Hsiao-yu's school
Raising money for the school principal
Selling old books to local students
questions.explain: 第一段說學生帶舊書和學用品寄給遙遠山區的小學校，故選 (A)。
questions.evidence: Students could bring in old story books and school supplies to send to a small school in a mountain region far away.

questions.stem: Why was Hsiao-yu surprised by Sana's letter?
options: She did not know Sana's age.
She thought the school was too far away.
She had never thought that going to school was not easy for every child.
She did not like writing letters.
questions.explain: 第二段指出她在台灣習慣了人人有受教育的機會，從沒覺得特別，所以得知別處女孩輟學才驚訝，故選 (C)。
questions.evidence: In Taiwan, the government's policy of free basic education gives every child the chance to learn, and she had never thought of it as something special.

questions.stem: The word "ensure" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: ensure 是「確保」，與 make certain 最接近，故選 (D)。作者說的是幾箱書「無法保證」每個孩子都能上學，並非只是猜測或希望。
questions.evidence: Hsiao-yu knows that a few boxes of books cannot ensure that every child has a place in school, yet she feels she has taken the first step.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a principal runs a school
How a student helped girls far away get books and hope for school
How to write a good speech
questions.explain: 全文從一封信開始，講筱瑜發起行動、寄書並收到回信，主旨是她幫助遠方孩子的行動，故選 (B)。
questions.evidence: Sana wrote that she would continue studying and hoped to become a teacher.

vocab.stem: My sister tried to ______ our parents to let her keep a puppy.
vocab.explain: 「說服」父母讓她養小狗，persuade 最通順，故選 persuade。sign（簽名）、ensure（確保）、control（控制）都不能接 parents to 的結構。

vocab.stem: The town plans to ______ a new library near the park.
vocab.explain: 城鎮計畫在公園旁「設立」新圖書館，establish 最合理，故選 establish。threaten（威脅）、recover（康復）、sign（簽名）都不合語意。

title: Pencils and Dreams
connect: 課文談一位創作者如何克服困難、實現夢想，這篇看一位喜歡畫卡通的學生如何面對失敗。
paragraphs: [[Ever since|P-0090]] he was a small child, Jun-hao has loved drawing cartoons. His notebooks are full of talking cats and flying fish. His art teacher calls him [[imaginative|L4-0511]], and Jun-hao hopes to build a [[career|L3-0125]] in animation one day. His [[passion|L3-0616]] for drawing is so strong that he often forgets to eat snacks after school.

Last year, he entered a school cartoon contest, but his work did not win anything. He felt sad and began to wonder whether he should [[dare|L3-0214]] to dream so big. His uncle, who works at a small animation studio, listened and told him that every artist meets a [[challenge|L0-0046]] at the start. [[For instance|P-0089]], many cartoon makers had their first ideas turned down several times before an audience ever saw their work.

Jun-hao decided to treat the failure as an [[obstacle|L4-0682]] to get past, not as the end of the road. [[In other words|P-0091]], he would look for a way around it. He asked his teacher for advice, studied how stories are told, and practiced every evening. His [[attitude|L3-0042]] changed: he no longer worried about winning, only about getting better. Slowly, he learned to [[overcome|L4-0702]] his fear of showing his drawings to others.

This year, Jun-hao made a one-minute film about a lonely robot who finds a friend. Many students watched it on the school website. It was not a great [[achievement|L3-0005]] by professional standards, but it made him proud. He knows the road is long and there will be [[hardship|L4-0475]] ahead. Still, he believes that with hard work he can [[fulfill|L4-0427]] his dream.
zh: 自從小時候起，俊豪就一直喜歡畫卡通。他的筆記本裡滿是會說話的貓和會飛的魚。美術老師說他很有想像力，俊豪希望有一天能以動畫為職業。他對畫畫的熱情之高，常常放學後忘了吃點心。
去年他參加學校的卡通比賽，但作品什麼獎都沒得。他很難過，開始懷疑自己該不該敢夢想那麼大。他的叔叔在一家小動畫工作室工作，聽了他的心事後說，每位創作者一開始都會遇到挑戰。例如，許多卡通創作者的第一個構想都被拒絕好幾次，才有觀眾看到他們的作品。
俊豪決定把失敗當成要跨過去的障礙，而不是路的終點。換句話說，他要找辦法繞過去。他向老師請教，研究故事怎麼說，每天晚上練習。他的態度改變了：他不再擔心得不得獎，只在意有沒有進步。慢慢地，他學會克服把作品拿給別人看的恐懼。
今年，俊豪做了一部一分鐘的短片，講一個孤單的機器人找到朋友的故事。許多同學在學校網站上看了它。以專業的標準來看，這不算很大的成就，但它讓他感到驕傲。他知道前路還很長，也會有艱難在前方。不過他相信，只要努力，就能實現自己的夢想。

questions.stem: What happened when Jun-hao entered the school contest?
options: His work did not win anything.
He was too late to join.
His teacher drew the cartoon for him.
questions.explain: 第二段明說他的作品什麼獎也沒得，故選 (B)。
questions.evidence: Last year, he entered a school cartoon contest, but his work did not win anything.

questions.stem: The word "obstacle" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: obstacle 是「阻礙、障礙」，文中把失敗看作要跨過去的東西，與 problem 最接近，故選 (C)。gift 與 prize 是正面的東西，不合。
questions.evidence: Jun-hao decided to treat the failure as an obstacle to get past, not as the end of the road.

questions.stem: What can we infer about Jun-hao's uncle?
options: He understands the difficulties of making cartoons.
He wants Jun-hao to stop drawing.
He is an art teacher at Jun-hao's school.
questions.explain: 叔叔在動畫工作室工作，並以創作者的經驗開導他，可推知他了解這一行的困難，故選 (A)。文中沒說他得過獎，也沒說他是學校老師。
questions.evidence: His uncle, who works at a small animation studio, listened and told him that every artist meets a challenge at the start.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to make a film with a robot
Why cartoons are better than real movies
How a student learned to face failure and keep following his dream
questions.explain: 全文從俊豪愛畫畫、比賽失敗、調整態度到完成短片，主旨是他面對失敗仍堅持夢想，故選 (D)。
questions.evidence: Still, he believes that with hard work he can fulfill his dream.

vocab.stem: A positive ______ can help you enjoy even difficult lessons.
vocab.explain: 正面的「態度」能讓人連困難的課都享受，attitude 最通順，故選 attitude。request（請求）、poverty（貧窮）、parade（遊行）都不合語意。

vocab.stem: Tom practiced every day to ______ his fear of swimming.
vocab.explain: 每天練習是為了「克服」對游泳的恐懼，overcome 最合理，故選 overcome。convey（傳達）、rescue（救援）、weave（編織）都不能搭配 fear。

title: The New Boy
connect: 課文談對外表與眾不同的人要有同理心，這篇看一位新同學如何被班上接納。
paragraphs: When Kai joined Mr. Chen's class in September, everyone noticed him. A long scar ran across the left side of his face from a surgery he had as a young child. Some students [[stared|L3-0836]] at him in the hallway. Others began to [[whisper|L0-0254]] behind their hands. Kai tried to [[pretend|L3-0669]] he did not see anything, but his shoulders dropped each time. He only wanted to [[fit in|P-0094]].

The worst [[incident|L4-0521]] happened in October. Two boys in the back row began to [[make fun of|P-0098]] Kai and liked to [[tease|L3-0892]] him about his scar. Their words were [[rude|T-0094]] and [[awful|L3-0053]], and Kai left the room with tears in his eyes. Mei, who sat next to him, felt angry. She stood up and [[defended|L4-0256]] him, telling the boys to stop.

After class, Mei decided to [[approach|L0-0114]] Kai gently. She did not know what to say, so she simply asked if he wanted to eat lunch together. Kai was surprised, but he agreed. [[At least|P-0099]] one person in the class was on his side, he thought. The next day, one of the boys came to [[apologize|L3-0030]]. He said he was [[genuinely|T-0096]] sorry, and Mei believed him.

[[Gradually|T-0097]], the class changed. People started to talk to Kai about games and music instead of his face. Kai laughed more often, and he began to raise his hand in class. He told Mei that kindness does not need to be big. Sometimes it is just sitting down next to someone.
zh: 九月凱加入陳老師的班級時，每個人都注意到他。他臉的左側有一道長長的疤，是小時候動手術留下的。有些學生在走廊上盯著他看。另一些人用手遮著嘴開始竊竊私語。凱努力假裝沒看到任何事，但每次他的肩膀都垂了下來。他只希望能融入大家。
最糟的事件發生在十月。後排的兩個男生開始嘲笑凱，還喜歡拿他的疤開玩笑。他們的話既無禮又糟糕，凱含著眼淚離開了教室。坐在他旁邊的小美很生氣。她站起來為他辯護，要那兩個男生住手。
下課後，小美決定溫和地接近凱。她不知道該說什麼，就只是問他要不要一起吃午餐。凱很驚訝，但答應了。他心想，至少班上有一個人站在他這邊。隔天，其中一個男生來道歉。他說他真心感到抱歉，小美相信他。
漸漸地，班上改變了。大家開始跟凱聊遊戲和音樂，而不是他的臉。凱笑得更多了，也開始在課堂上舉手發言。他告訴小美，善意不需要很大。有時它只是在某個人身旁坐下來。

questions.stem: How did Mei first approach Kai?
options: She told the teacher about the boys.
She asked him to eat lunch with her.
She invited him to a party.
questions.explain: 第三段說她不知說什麼，便問他要不要一起吃午餐，故選 (C)。
questions.evidence: She did not know what to say, so she simply asked if he wanted to eat lunch together.

questions.stem: The word "incident" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: incident 指「事件」，與 event 最接近，故選 (A)。
questions.evidence: The worst incident happened in October.

questions.stem: What can we infer about Kai at the beginning of the story?
options: He was angry at his teacher.
He felt uncomfortable and unhappy at school.
He enjoyed being the center of attention.
He did not care about the other students.
questions.explain: 他假裝沒看到、肩膀每次都垂下來，可推知他感到不自在又難過，故選 (B)。他希望融入大家，不是享受被注意，(C) 不對。
questions.evidence: Kai tried to pretend he did not see anything, but his shoulders dropped each time.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a boy changed schools in October
Why scars are hard to see
How to give a lunch invitation
How one student's kindness helped a new classmate feel accepted
questions.explain: 全文敘述凱被議論，小美挺身而出、主動邀請，班級慢慢改變，主旨是善意讓新同學被接納，故選 (D)。
questions.evidence: Sometimes it is just sitting down next to someone.

vocab.stem: The teacher was ______ happy to see her old student again after ten years.
vocab.explain: 十年後見到老學生，老師「真心地」高興，genuinely 最合適，故選 genuinely。rudely（無禮地）、reluctantly（不情願地）與開心矛盾。

vocab.stem: You should ______ to Amy for breaking her pen.
vocab.explain: 弄壞別人的筆應該「道歉」，apologize to 是固定搭配，故選 apologize。pretend、whisper、stare 都不能這樣接 to Amy 表示賠不是。

title: Ten Minutes on Stage
connect: 課文介紹演講平台，這篇看一位高中生在校內午休演講上分享蜜蜂主題的經驗。
paragraphs: Last spring, my school began a [[series|L5-0773]] of lunchtime talks, and I decided to [[give it a try|P-0105]]. Each speaker has only ten minutes to share an idea with a small [[audience|L3-0045]] of classmates. The students who join come from a [[broad|T-0101]] [[range|L0-0068]] of backgrounds, so the topics are never boring. Last month, one girl talked about old coins, and another boy showed us how to fix a bicycle.

My own topic was bees. I have had a [[fascination|L6-0338]] with them since my uncle let me watch his hives. I read [[numerous|L4-0674]] articles and watched short videos, and I also had to [[seek|T-0099]] advice from our biology teacher. I learned that bees help to grow fruit and vegetables [[as well as|P-0102]] flowers, and that without them, many of our favorite foods would be harder to find.

The hardest part was the [[method|T-0103]] of speaking. At first I read my notes word for word, and my friends said I sounded like a robot. So I practiced in front of a mirror for a week and learned to look at people's faces instead of my paper. I also used simple [[technology|L0-0074]], just three photos on one slide, so that nobody had to read small words from the screen.

On the day, my hands shook, but nobody laughed. Afterward, a teacher asked me to [[discuss|T-0102]] bees with a class of younger students, too. Talks like these are [[increasingly|T-0100]] popular in schools, and anyone can listen [[for free|P-0103]]. I think they are well [[worth|L0-0259]] your time. When you listen to different people, you [[broaden your horizons|P-0106]] without even leaving your school.
zh: 去年春天，我們學校開始舉辦一系列午休演講，我決定試試看。每位講者只有十分鐘，向一小群同學分享一個想法。來參加的學生背景各式各樣，所以題目從來不無聊。上個月，一個女生談舊硬幣，另一個男生則示範怎麼修腳踏車。
我自己的主題是蜜蜂。自從叔叔讓我看他的蜂箱之後，我就一直對蜜蜂很著迷。我讀了許多文章、看了短片，也向生物老師請教。我學到蜜蜂除了幫花授粉，也幫助水果和蔬菜生長；沒有牠們，我們愛吃的許多食物會更難取得。
最困難的部分是說話的方式。一開始我一字一句照著筆記唸，朋友說我聽起來像機器人。於是我對著鏡子練習了一個星期，學會看著人們的臉而不是我的紙。我也只用了簡單的科技，在一張投影片上放三張照片，這樣就沒有人得去讀螢幕上的小字。
演講當天我的手在發抖，但沒有人笑。事後，一位老師還請我向一班學弟妹談談蜜蜂。這類演講在學校裡越來越受歡迎，而且任何人都可以免費聽。我認為它們非常值得你花時間。聽不同的人說話，你不用離開學校就能拓展視野。

questions.stem: How did the writer get better at giving the talk?
options: By practicing in front of a mirror for a week.
By asking friends to give the talk for him.
By reading the notes faster and faster.
By using many photos on the screen.
questions.explain: 第三段寫他對著鏡子練習一星期，並學會看聽眾的臉，故選 (A)。(C) 剛好相反，他是改掉照著筆記唸的習慣；(D) 文中只用了三張照片。
questions.evidence: So I practiced in front of a mirror for a week and learned to look at people's faces instead of my paper.

questions.stem: The word "seek" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: seek advice 是「尋求建議」，與 ask for 意思最接近，故選 (C)。作者是去向生物老師請教，不是拒絕或忘記建議。
questions.evidence: I read numerous articles and watched short videos, and I also had to seek advice from our biology teacher.

questions.stem: What does the writer mean by saying his friends thought he "sounded like a robot"?
options: His voice was too loud for the room.
His speech was stiff and not natural.
questions.explain: 照著筆記一字一句唸，聽起來就會生硬、不自然，朋友才說像機器人，故選 (B)。文中的 technology 只是三張照片，與機器人的比喻無關，(C) 是被字面誤導。
questions.evidence: At first I read my notes word for word, and my friends said I sounded like a robot.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a student prepared for a short school talk and what he gained from it
Why bees are important to farmers
How to build a talk show for the whole school
Why students should stop reading notes
questions.explain: 全文談作者為午休演講選題、研究、練習，最後獲得經驗，故選 (A)。(B) 蜜蜂的重要性只是第二段的內容，不是全篇重點。
questions.evidence: Last spring, my school began a series of lunchtime talks, and I decided to give it a try.

vocab.stem: The singer thanked the ______ for clapping so loudly after the last song.
vocab.explain: 歌手感謝在最後一首歌後大聲鼓掌的「觀眾」，故選 audience。method（方法）、series（系列）、field（領域）都不能當作鼓掌的人。

vocab.stem: This TV ______ has ten episodes, and I have already watched all of them.
vocab.explain: 有十集的電視「系列／影集」是 series，故選 series。foundation（基礎）、conference（會議）、celebrity（名人）都不能用來指有很多集的節目。

title: Dinner in the Street
connect: 課文談臺灣的辦桌文化，這篇看一位學生參與社區街頭晚餐、從旁幫忙的經驗。
paragraphs: Every autumn, our [[neighborhood|L3-0571]] holds a big dinner in the middle of the street. The [[event|T-0106]] [[takes place|P-0108]] on the first Saturday of October, and nearly every family comes. When I was younger, I was [[curious|T-0105]] about why adults wanted to eat outside, since the street can be hot and noisy. After I helped last year, I finally understood.

Days before the dinner, the grown-ups [[arrange|T-0108]] everything carefully. The road is closed so that no [[vehicle|L3-0957]] can enter. Neighbors put up a large [[temporary|L3-0897]] tent as [[shelter|L4-0887]] in case it rains, and they borrow tables and chairs from the school. My job was to [[help out|P-0110]] in the kitchen, and my cousin and I had to [[hand out|P-0111]] paper bowls and chopsticks to everyone who arrived.

Each family brings a dish in a plastic [[container|L4-0200]], and the food is placed on one long table. People [[exchange|L3-0296]] recipes as they eat, and they tell funny stories about the street's past. Mr. Chen, an [[elder|T-0107]] who has lived here for fifty years, taught me that the best soup needs patience, not special tools.

When dinner is over, people [[relax|L3-0710]] on their chairs while the children play games under the lights. Nobody has to hurry home. The evening shows how a group of people can [[cooperate|L4-0217]] to make something warm and friendly. It is the [[spirit|T-0109]] of sharing that I remember most, and I hope our street will keep this habit for many years.
zh: 每年秋天，我們社區都會在街道正中央辦一場大型晚餐。活動在十月的第一個星期六舉行，幾乎每家都會來。我小時候很好奇，為什麼大人想在外面吃飯，畢竟街上又熱又吵。去年我親自幫忙之後，終於明白了。
晚餐前幾天，大人們就會仔細安排好一切。道路會封起來，不讓車輛進入。鄰居們搭起一頂大型臨時帳篷，萬一下雨可以遮蔽，還向學校借來桌椅。我的工作是到廚房幫忙，我和表弟則把紙碗和筷子發給每位來的人。
每個家庭都帶一道菜，裝在塑膠盒裡，菜被擺在一張長桌上。大家邊吃邊交換食譜，也說起這條街過去的趣事。陳先生是在這裡住了五十年的長輩，他教我最好喝的湯需要的是耐心，而不是特別的工具。
晚餐結束後，大人們靠在椅子上放鬆，孩子們在燈下玩遊戲，沒有人需要趕著回家。這個夜晚讓人看到一群人能如何合作，營造出溫暖友善的氣氛。我最難忘的是分享的精神，我也希望我們這條街能把這個習慣保持很多年。

questions.stem: What was the writer's job at the dinner?
options: Helping in the kitchen and giving out bowls and chopsticks
Cooking the soup for all the guests
questions.explain: 第二段說他的工作是到廚房幫忙，並和表弟發紙碗與筷子，故選 (A)。煮湯的是陳先生，不是作者，(B) 是常見的混淆。
questions.evidence: My job was to help out in the kitchen, and my cousin and I had to hand out paper bowls and chopsticks to everyone who arrived.

questions.stem: The word "temporary" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: temporary 指「暫時的」，帳篷只在活動期間搭起，與 lasting only a short time 相符，故選 (B)。文中沒有提到價錢或材質。
questions.evidence: Neighbors put up a large temporary tent as shelter in case it rains, and they borrow tables and chairs from the school.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3, "they" in "they tell funny stories about the street's past" refers to ______.
questions.explain: 前一句主詞是 People，they 指在晚餐上交換食譜的人，故選 (C)。recipes 雖然最靠近，但食譜不會「說故事」。
questions.evidence: People exchange recipes as they eat, and they tell funny stories about the street's past.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to cook soup for fifty people
Why streets should be closed every day
A teenager's first trip to another city
A neighborhood dinner in the street and the sharing it brings
questions.explain: 全文從準備工作到用餐、聊天，描寫社區街頭晚餐及其中的分享精神，故選 (D)。(B) 只有活動當天才封路，不是每天。
questions.evidence: It is the spirit of sharing that I remember most, and I hope our street will keep this habit for many years.

vocab.stem: Our ______ has a small park, a bakery, and a library, all within five minutes' walk.
vocab.explain: 公園、麵包店、圖書館都在步行五分鐘內，說的是居住的「社區、鄰近地區」，故選 neighborhood。container（容器）、elder（長者）、vehicle（車輛）都不能當作有公園和圖書館的地方。

vocab.stem: We stood under a big tree for ______ when it suddenly began to rain.
vocab.explain: 突然下雨而站在大樹下，是為了「遮蔽、躲雨」，for shelter 最通順，故選 shelter。exchange（交換）、spirit（精神）、event（活動）放入後語意不通。

title: Names That Became Words
connect: 課文談以人名命名的字詞，這篇從科學課的例子看電壓、溫度和點字背後的人物。
paragraphs: In science class, our teacher asked a [[general|T-0110]] question: why do we say "volt"? Many words [[derive|L5-0276]] from the names of people, and these words are called eponyms. I looked it up and found that "volt" comes from Alessandro Volta, an Italian scientist who built one of the first batteries. [[In the beginning|P-0114]], people simply wanted to honor him, but his name soon became part of everyday science.

Another example is the Celsius scale. Anders Celsius, a Swedish astronomer, [[thought up|P-0117]] a temperature scale based on water in the 1740s. [[Later on|P-0113]], other people turned his numbers around so that zero meant freezing. Today it is the [[standard|L0-0108]] way to measure temperature in Taiwan, and the name is [[widespread|L5-0990]] around the world, although some countries still use an [[alternative|L4-0033]] scale named after another scientist.

My favorite story is about Louis Braille. He was a French boy who lost his sight as a child. As a teenager, he made a reading system for blind people. The system [[combines|L0-0191]] six raised dots in different patterns to stand for letters, and the most useful [[feature|L0-0004]] is that readers can feel the words with their fingers. Braille's invention [[plays an important role|P-0116]] in the lives of blind people even today.

These stories [[reveal|L3-0730]] that the work of one person can stay in our language for centuries. The [[usage|L4-0975]] of an eponym is usually so natural that we forget there was ever a real person behind it. Language is [[constantly|T-0113]] changing, and I now enjoy looking at the [[existing|T-0114]] words around me and wondering whose names they hide.
zh: 自然課上，老師問了一個一般性的問題：為什麼我們說「伏特」？很多字源自人名，這類字叫做以人名命名的字。我查了資料，發現「伏特」來自亞歷山卓·伏打，一位製造出最早期電池之一的義大利科學家。起初，人們只是想紀念他，但他的名字很快就成了日常科學的一部分。
另一個例子是攝氏溫標。瑞典天文學家安德斯·攝爾修斯在一七四〇年代想出一種以水為基準的溫度標準。後來，其他人把他的數字顛倒過來，讓零度代表結冰。如今它是臺灣測量溫度的標準方式，這個名字也流傳到世界各地，雖然有些國家仍使用以另一位科學家命名的替代溫標。
我最喜歡的故事是關於路易·布萊葉。他是個法國男孩，小時候失去了視力。青少年時期，他為盲人設計了一套閱讀系統。這套系統把六個凸起的點排成不同的組合來代表字母，最實用的特色就是讀者能用手指摸出字句。布萊葉的發明直到今天，在盲人的生活中仍扮演重要的角色。
這些故事顯示，一個人的成就可以在語言中留存好幾個世紀。這類字的用法通常自然到我們忘了背後曾有一個真實的人。語言不斷在改變，而我現在喜歡看看身邊現有的字，想想它們藏著誰的名字。

questions.stem: What did other people do with Celsius's temperature scale later?
options: They changed it so that zero meant freezing.
They made it based on air instead of water.
They gave it a new name.
They stopped using it in Taiwan.
questions.explain: 第二段說後來有人把他的數字顛倒，讓零度代表結冰，故選 (A)。文中說這個溫標是以水為基準，並未改成空氣，(B) 是無中生有。
questions.evidence: Later on, other people turned his numbers around so that zero meant freezing.

questions.stem: The word "widespread" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: widespread 是「普遍的」，名字傳遍全世界，與 found in many places 最接近，故選 (B)。文中雖提到一七四〇年代，但 widespread 說的是範圍，不是年代。
questions.evidence: Today it is the standard way to measure temperature in Taiwan, and the name is widespread around the world, although some countries still use an alternative scale named after another scientist.

questions.stem: What does the writer suggest in the last paragraph?
options: New words should not come from names.
We often use people's names in words without noticing it.
questions.explain: 作者說這類字用起來太自然，我們忘了背後有真人，也就是常常用卻沒注意到，故選 (C)。他說語言「不斷改變」，所以 (D) 與原文相反。
questions.evidence: The usage of an eponym is usually so natural that we forget there was ever a real person behind it.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a French boy lost his sight
Why the Celsius scale is better than other scales
How to find the names of scientists online
Some everyday words come from the names of real people, and their stories are interesting.
questions.explain: 全文以 volt、Celsius、Braille 三個例子說明字詞源自人名，故選 (D)。(B) 只是第二段的例子之一，且文中並未說攝氏比較好。
questions.evidence: Many words derive from the names of people, and these words are called eponyms.

vocab.stem: Many English words ______ from Latin, such as "student" and "library".
vocab.explain: student、library 這類字「源自」拉丁文，many words derive from Latin 是常見用法，故選 derive。release（釋放）、chase（追逐）、reveal（揭露）都無法搭配 from Latin 表示來源。

vocab.stem: The weather in the mountains is ______ changing, so bring a coat just in case.
vocab.explain: 山區天氣「不斷地」變化，所以要帶外套，constantly changing 最通順，故選 constantly。never changing 會讓「帶外套」失去理由，digitally、quietly 也不合語意。

title: A Day on a Tea Farm
connect: 課文談英式下午茶的文化差異，這篇看一位學生到臺灣茶園參訪，了解一杯茶背後的功夫。
paragraphs: Last weekend, my class visited a tea farm in the hills near Taipei. I had never [[heard of|P-0118]] how much work goes into one cup of tea. The bus ride was long, so we were nearly [[starving|T-0119]] when we arrived. Fortunately, the owner, our [[host|T-0117]] for the day, welcomed us with warm snacks and a [[delightful|L4-0263]] smile.

Mr. Lin explained that growing tea is a kind of [[agriculture|L3-0016]] that depends on weather, soil, and patience. The leaves are picked by hand, left to dry for a while, shaken gently, and then heated. The [[quality|L0-0043]] of the tea depends on every one of these steps, and this careful process gives oolong its [[characteristic|L4-0132]] flavor. When I tasted a cup fresh from the pot, I could smell flowers.

He told us that tea [[typically|T-0115]] tastes best when the water is hot but not boiling, because water that is too hot can make it bitter. Some of my classmates began to [[disagree|L0-0134]] about how long to wait; one said thirty seconds, and another insisted on a full minute. Mr. Lin smiled and said that was part of the fun. Some tea sets are [[exquisite|T-0118]] and even [[luxurious|L4-0607]], but you really need only a simple pot and a quiet moment.

The [[fundamental|L4-0429]] lesson of the day was that good things take time. Before we left, I [[asked for|P-0120]] a small bag of leaves, because I want to [[invite my grandfather over|P-0121]] this weekend. I will make the tea [[as carefully as possible|P-0123]], and we will talk while we drink. A cup of tea also gives me [[energy|T-0120]] for studying afterward, and it reminds me to slow down.
zh: 上週末，我們班參觀了臺北近郊山上的一座茶園。我從來不知道一杯茶背後有這麼多工夫。車程很長，所以我們抵達時都快餓壞了。幸好，當天的主人，也就是茶園老闆，帶著愉快的笑容用熱呼呼的點心歡迎我們。
林先生解釋說，種茶是一種仰賴天氣、土壤與耐心的農業。茶葉由人工採摘，放置一段時間讓它變乾，輕輕搖動，再加熱。茶的品質取決於每一個步驟，而這套仔細的流程讓烏龍茶有了它獨特的風味。我喝到剛從壺裡倒出的一杯時，能聞到花香。
他告訴我們，茶通常在水熱但不滾燙時最好喝，因為太燙的水會讓茶變苦。我有些同學對該等多久意見不同，一個說三十秒，另一個堅持要整整一分鐘。林先生笑著說這就是樂趣的一部分。有些茶具精緻、甚至奢華，但其實你只需要一把簡單的壺和一段安靜的時光。
這天最根本的一課是：好東西需要時間。離開前，我要了一小包茶葉，因為我想在這個週末請爺爺來家裡。我會盡可能細心地泡茶，我們邊喝邊聊。一杯茶也能讓我在之後有精神讀書，並提醒我慢下來。

questions.stem: Why were the students very hungry when they reached the farm?
questions.explain: 第一段寫車程很長，所以到達時他們快餓壞了，故選 (A)。文中說老闆還端出點心歡迎他們，所以 (B) 與原文相反。
questions.evidence: The bus ride was long, so we were nearly starving when we arrived.

questions.stem: What did some classmates disagree about?
options: Which tea set was the most expensive
How long to wait before drinking the tea
Whether to buy a small bag of leaves
How to pick leaves by hand
questions.explain: 第三段說同學們對「該等多久」意見不同，有人說三十秒，有人說一分鐘，故選 (B)。茶具只是後面另外提到的話題，並不是爭論點。
questions.evidence: Some of my classmates began to disagree about how long to wait; one said thirty seconds, and another insisted on a full minute.

questions.stem: The word "exquisite" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: exquisite 是「精緻的」，用來形容做工漂亮的茶具，與 beautifully made 最接近，故選 (C)。後面的 but 表示不必依賴貴重茶具，並不是說它們壞了。
questions.evidence: Some tea sets are exquisite and even luxurious, but you really need only a simple pot and a quiet moment.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to grow tea at home
Why tea is better than other drinks
A farm owner who wants to sell more tea
A school trip to a tea farm that taught the writer to enjoy tea slowly
questions.explain: 全文寫參觀茶園、學到泡茶與品茶，最後體會到慢下來的道理，故選 (D)。文中並沒有比較茶與其他飲料，也沒有談老闆想賣茶。
questions.evidence: The fundamental lesson of the day was that good things take time.

vocab.stem: This shop is famous for the high ______ of its handmade shoes.
vocab.explain: 店以手工鞋的高「品質」聞名，high quality 是常見搭配，故選 quality。agriculture（農業）、host（主人）、energy（精力）都不能被形容為 high 的鞋子特性。

vocab.stem: After a long run, I ate a banana to get some ______ back.
vocab.explain: 跑完長跑後吃香蕉是為了補回「體力、精力」，get some energy back 最通順，故選 energy。affair（事務）、host（主人）、characteristic（特徵）都無法「補回來」。

title: My Mistake Notebook
connect: 課文談做筆記的學習技巧，這篇看一位學生用「錯題本」改變讀書方式。
paragraphs: I used to think that studying hard meant [[reciting|L5-0708]] the textbook again and again. My scores, however, hardly changed. Then a university [[professor|L3-0676]] visited our school and shared a simple [[technique|L3-0894]]: keep a notebook of your own mistakes. I was doubtful, but I decided to try it for one month.

The [[system|T-0123]] is easy. After each quiz, I write the question I got wrong in the left [[column|L3-0169]] of a page. On the right side, I [[fill in|P-0125]] the correct answer and one sentence about why I made the mistake. At the bottom, I leave a [[blank|T-0125]] space and later add a short [[summary|L3-0868]] of the whole lesson in my own words.

The [[process|L3-0673]] takes about ten minutes. When the [[information|L3-0433]] is long, I [[break up|P-0124]] a big topic into small parts so that it is easier to remember. I also use an [[abbreviation|T-0124]] for long words, such as "cw" for "cell wall", to save time. Writing it all in my own way forces me to think, not just copy.

Every Sunday, I [[review|T-0127]] the notebook from the first page. I [[gain|T-0122]] confidence when I see that old mistakes no longer appear. The method does not [[require|L0-0044]] any expensive tools, only a pen and some patience. I even [[make use of|P-0126]] the short time on the bus to read a few pages. Short and [[frequent|L3-0343]] practice works better than one long night before the exam, and after a month my science score went up by ten points.
zh: 我以前以為用功讀書就是一遍又一遍背課本，但我的成績幾乎沒有變化。後來有一位大學教授來我們學校，分享了一個簡單的技巧：準備一本自己的錯題本。我半信半疑，但還是決定試一個月。
這套方法很簡單。每次小考後，我把錯的題目寫在一頁的左欄，右邊則填上正確答案，並寫一句我為什麼會錯。頁面底部我留一塊空白，之後再用自己的話加上整堂課的簡短摘要。
整個過程大約花十分鐘。資訊很長的時候，我會把大主題拆成小段，這樣比較容易記住。我也會用縮寫代替長單字，例如用「cw」代表「cell wall」（細胞壁）來節省時間。照自己的方式全部寫下來，會逼我思考，而不只是抄寫。
每個星期天，我從第一頁開始複習這本筆記。看到舊的錯誤不再出現，我就更有自信。這個方法不需要任何昂貴的工具，只要一支筆和一點耐心。我甚至利用搭公車的短暫時間多看幾頁。短而頻繁的練習比考前熬一整晚更有效，一個月後我的自然成績進步了十分。

questions.stem: Where does the writer put the correct answer in the notebook?
options: On the right side of the page
At the top of the page
On the back of the quiz
questions.explain: 第二段寫錯題在左欄，右邊則填正確答案與犯錯原因，故選 (A)。左欄放的是錯誤的題目，(B) 是容易搞反的地方。
questions.evidence: On the right side, I fill in the correct answer and one sentence about why I made the mistake.

questions.stem: The phrase "break up" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: break up a big topic into small parts 是把大主題「分成」小段，與 divide 最接近，故選 (B)。作者目的是方便記憶，所以不可能是忘記或忽略。
questions.evidence: When the information is long, I break up a big topic into small parts so that it is easier to remember.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3, "it" in "so that it is easier to remember" refers to ______.
questions.explain: it 指前面被拆成小段的 a big topic，拆開是為了讓主題更容易記住，故選 (C)。(A) 筆記本不是被記憶的內容。
questions.evidence: When the information is long, I break up a big topic into small parts so that it is easier to remember.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why students should avoid taking quizzes
How a professor writes a science book
Why long study nights are the best way to learn
How a student studies better by keeping a notebook of mistakes
questions.explain: 全文說明作者用錯題本的做法與成效，故選 (D)。第四段明說短而頻繁的練習比考前熬夜更有效，(C) 剛好相反。
questions.evidence: Then a university professor visited our school and shared a simple technique: keep a notebook of your own mistakes.

vocab.stem: Our swimming coach taught us a new ______ for breathing in the water.
vocab.explain: 教練教的是呼吸的新「技巧」，故選 technique。column（欄）、summary（摘要）、system（系統）都不適合用來指一種呼吸的方法。

vocab.stem: Please ______ your notes tonight so that you are ready for tomorrow's quiz.
vocab.explain: 為了明天小考而「複習」筆記，review your notes 最通順，故選 review。gain（獲得）、blank（空白的）、guide（引導）放入句中語意不通。

title: Why Astronauts Grow Taller
connect: 課文談太空站上的生活，這篇從「太空人為什麼會變高」切入，看太空對身體的影響。
paragraphs: For my science project, I asked a simple question: why do [[astronauts|L6-0062]] come back from space a little taller? On Earth, [[gravity|L5-0415]] presses the bones of the back together all day. In space, that pressure is gone, so the spine can stretch. On the [[ISS|P-0127]], some astronauts grow by a few centimeters, but they return to their normal height soon after landing.

Space changes other parts of the body, too. Body fluids [[tend|L3-0898]] to move toward the head, which makes faces look puffy and can even change an astronaut's [[vision|L3-0965]]. Because muscles and bones do not have to hold up the body, they become weaker, and their strength can [[decrease|L3-0223]] quickly if nothing is done.

To [[maintain|L0-0032]] their health, astronauts [[work out|P-0129]] for about two hours almost every day. They use special machines with straps that hold them down, and many of them [[work up a sweat|P-0130]]. In space, [[sweat|L3-0878]] does not drip away; it stays on the skin in small balls. After the exercise, the station's machines [[gather|T-0131]] moisture from the air and clean it into drinking water.

Daily life is different, too. A [[liquid|T-0129]] cannot be poured into a cup because it would float away, so many drinks come as [[powdered|T-0128]] mixes in sealed bags. Living in space may sound [[out of this world|P-0128]], but astronauts [[sacrifice|L4-0869]] many comforts of home. Scientists study these changes so that they can [[limit|T-0132]] the damage to the human body on longer trips, perhaps even to Mars.
zh: 我的自然科專題問了一個簡單的問題：為什麼太空人從太空回來會變高一點？在地球上，重力一整天都把背部的骨頭壓在一起。在太空中，這股壓力消失了，所以脊椎可以伸展。在國際太空站上，有些太空人會長高幾公分，但他們著陸後不久就會恢復原本的身高。
太空也會改變身體的其他部分。體液傾向往頭部移動，讓臉看起來浮腫，甚至會改變太空人的視力。因為肌肉和骨頭不必撐住身體，它們會變弱，如果不處理，力量可能很快下降。
為了維持健康，太空人幾乎每天運動約兩小時。他們使用附帶束帶、能把身體固定住的特殊器材，很多人還會運動到流汗。在太空中，汗水不會滴落，而是變成小水珠留在皮膚上。運動之後，太空站裡的機器會收集空氣中的水氣，並把它淨化成飲用水。
日常生活也不一樣。液體不能倒進杯子，因為會飄走，所以許多飲料是裝在密封袋裡的粉狀沖泡包。住在太空聽起來好極了，但太空人其實犧牲了許多家裡的舒適。科學家研究這些變化，是為了在更長的旅程（甚至可能是去火星）中減少對人體的傷害。

questions.stem: Why can an astronaut's spine stretch in space?
options: Gravity is no longer pressing the bones together.
The ISS is warm all the time.
questions.explain: 第一段說在地球上重力壓著背部骨頭，太空中壓力消失，脊椎才能伸展，故選 (A)。文中沒有提到飲食、睡姿或溫度。
questions.evidence: In space, that pressure is gone, so the spine can stretch.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 3, what happens to sweat in space?
options: It stays on the skin in small balls.
questions.explain: 第三段明說汗水不會滴落，而是變成小水珠留在皮膚上，故選 (B)。「powder」是第四段飲料包的內容，與汗水無關。
questions.evidence: In space, sweat does not drip away; it stays on the skin in small balls.

questions.stem: Why do astronauts exercise almost every day?
options: They have nothing else to do.
They need to keep their muscles and bones from getting weak.
They must make drinking water by running.
questions.explain: 第二段指出肌肉骨頭不必撐住身體會變弱，第三段說為了維持健康每天運動，由此可推論是為了防止肌力與骨質衰退，故選 (C)。長高只是太空中脊椎伸展的結果，不是運動的目的。
questions.evidence: Because muscles and bones do not have to hold up the body, they become weaker, and their strength can decrease quickly if nothing is done.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to build a space station
A student's trip to a space museum
How life in space changes the human body and how astronauts deal with it
questions.explain: 全文從長高、體液、肌肉說到運動與飲食，主軸是太空對身體的影響與因應，故選 (D)。(C) 作者是做科學專題，文中沒有提到參觀博物館。
questions.evidence: Scientists study these changes so that they can limit the damage to the human body on longer trips, perhaps even to Mars.

vocab.stem: An apple falls from a tree to the ground because of ______.
vocab.explain: 蘋果往地面掉是因為「重力」，故選 gravity。vision（視力）、liquid（液體）、sweat（汗）都無法解釋物體下墜。

vocab.stem: Doctors tell us to ______ the time we spend looking at screens every day.
vocab.explain: 醫生要我們「限制」每天看螢幕的時間，limit the time 最通順，故選 limit。gather（收集）、tend（傾向）、maintain（維持）放進句中都不合語意。

title: A Video Call in Ward 7
connect: 課文談一次打破規則的探病，這篇看一位學生如何用視訊讓年幼的表弟陪伴生病的奶奶。
paragraphs: Last winter my grandmother was [[confined|L5-0199]] to a hospital bed because of a serious [[illness|T-0134]]. She had always been strong, but now she looked [[frail|T-0136]] and tired. The doctors said her condition was [[terminal|L5-0890]], so the family wanted to spend every day with her. However, the hospital did not allow children under twelve to visit, because [[germs|L4-0443]] spread easily in winter. My little cousin Ming cried about it, and I felt sorry for him.

One Saturday I brought a tablet to the ward. I was [[about to|P-0135]] ask a nurse where I could find a quiet corner when I saw my grandmother's tired eyes. She whispered that she missed Ming more than anything. I did not [[hesitate|L3-0398]]. I asked the nurse if I could use the tablet to [[contact|L0-0122]] him by video. She thought for a moment and then smiled. "This is not a crowded room," she said, "and a patient who is happy often gets better faster." She helped me set up the call.

When Ming's face appeared on the screen, my grandmother's eyes began to [[sparkle|L5-0814]]. Her [[laughter|L3-0478]] filled the room, and for the first time in weeks she sat up straight. Ming held up a drawing of the whole family and sang a silly song to [[cheer her up|P-0133]]. She clapped along and wiped her eyes. I felt a [[warmth|L3-0975]] in my chest that I will never forget, even though I wished I could give her a [[hug|L3-0416]] on his behalf.

A few months later, my grandmother [[passed away|P-0137]] peacefully. We were sad, but we were also thankful for that afternoon. I am glad I did not [[refuse|T-0137]] to ask for help. Sometimes a small act, like one phone call, can [[make a difference|P-0138]] to a person who is waiting for the people she loves.
zh: 去年冬天，我的奶奶因為一場重病被限制在醫院的病床上。她一向很堅強，但現在看起來虛弱又疲倦。醫生說她的病情已經到了末期，所以全家人都想每天陪著她。不過，醫院不准十二歲以下的孩子探病，因為冬天病菌很容易傳播。我的小表弟阿明為此哭了，我也替他難過。
某個星期六，我帶著一台平板電腦到病房。我正要問護理師哪裡有安靜的角落，就看見奶奶疲倦的雙眼。她小聲說，她最想念的就是阿明。我沒有遲疑，問護理師能不能用平板和他視訊聯絡。她想了一下，然後笑了。她說：「這裡人不多，而且病人心情愉快通常會好得比較快。」她幫我把視訊接好。
當阿明的臉出現在螢幕上時，奶奶的眼睛開始閃閃發亮。她的笑聲充滿了整個房間，好幾週來第一次坐得直直的。阿明舉起一張全家人的畫，還唱了一首好笑的歌來逗她開心。她跟著拍手，並擦了擦眼睛。我胸口湧起一股我永遠不會忘記的溫暖，雖然我多希望能替他給奶奶一個擁抱。
幾個月後，奶奶平靜地過世了。我們很難過，但也很感謝那個下午。我很高興當時沒有拒絕開口求助。有時候，一個小小的舉動，像是一通電話，就能對一位等待著心愛之人的人帶來改變。

questions.stem: Why couldn't Ming visit his grandmother in the hospital?
options: The hospital did not let young children visit.
He was sick with a cold.
questions.explain: 第一段指出醫院不准十二歲以下的孩子探病，因為冬天病菌易傳播，故選 (B)。文中沒說阿明怕醫生或生病，(A)(C) 皆屬無中生有。
questions.evidence: However, the hospital did not allow children under twelve to visit, because germs spread easily in winter.

questions.stem: What did the narrator do on Saturday?
options: She wrote a long letter to Ming.
She asked to use a tablet for a video call.
She asked the doctor for new medicine.
questions.explain: 第二段說她問護理師能否用平板和阿明視訊，故選 (C)。(B) 寫信文中沒有提到，是以視訊代替，不是寫信。
questions.evidence: I asked the nurse if I could use the tablet to contact him by video.

questions.stem: The word "frail" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: frail 指「虛弱的、體弱的」，與前後的 tired 呼應，意思最接近 weak，故選 (A)。(D) quiet 指安靜，不是身體狀況。
questions.evidence: She had always been strong, but now she looked frail and tired.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a hospital builds a new ward
How a video call brought joy to a sick grandmother
Why children should not visit hospitals
How the narrator learned to use a tablet
questions.explain: 全文敘述作者用視訊讓表弟陪伴生病的奶奶，帶給她快樂，主旨是 (B)。(C) 文中只提到醫院規定，並未主張孩子不該去醫院。
questions.evidence: Sometimes a small act, like one phone call, can make a difference to a person who is waiting for the people she loves.

vocab.stem: The movie was so funny that the whole class burst into ______.
vocab.explain: 電影很好笑，全班爆出「笑聲」，burst into laughter 是常見搭配，故選 laughter。warmth（溫暖）、illness（疾病）、germ（細菌）都無法與 burst into 搭配。

vocab.stem: Please wash your hands often to stop the ______ from spreading.
vocab.explain: 勤洗手是為了防止「細菌」擴散，故選 germs。hugs（擁抱）、sparkles（閃光）、terminals（終點站）都不合語意。

title: The Newspaper Tower
connect: 課文談團隊合作搭高塔的挑戰，這篇看一個物理課小組如何用報紙搭塔、從失敗中修正。
paragraphs: Our physics teacher, Mr. Chen, [[promised|T-0138]] a surprise for Friday's class. When we arrived, each team of four found only newspaper, tape, and a pair of scissors on the desk. Our task was to [[construct|L4-0193]] the tallest tower that could hold a small apple at the top. We were not allowed to use any other [[materials|L0-0007]], and we had only twenty minutes. Everyone laughed. How could paper hold up an apple?

At first, our team did nothing but argue. Everyone had a different idea, and no one wanted to be [[in charge|P-0140]]. Then Lily, who dreams of becoming an [[architect|L5-0051]], reminded us that a tall [[structure|L3-0856]] needs a wide base. We agreed to [[collaborate|T-0139]]: two people rolled the paper into tubes, one person taped them together, and one checked the height. It was a lot of [[trial and error|P-0139]]. Our first tower fell down before the apple even touched it.

After that, we sat down and tried to [[figure out|P-0141]] what went wrong. The tubes were too thin, and the base was too narrow. So we made them [[slightly|T-0140]] fatter and added triangles to the sides, because triangles give a tower more [[stability|L5-0834]]. Mr. Chen walked by and gave us some [[feedback|L4-0394]]. He told us to push the tower gently with a finger before we put the apple on top. Each small [[adjustment|L4-0021]] made it stronger.

In the end, our tower stood ninety centimeters tall and [[ranked|L3-0694]] third in the class. The winning team had a [[unique|L3-0946]] design shaped like a spiral. We were not the champions, but we learned something important. Good ideas often grow when people listen to one another, and failure is only one step on the road to a better answer.
zh: 我們的物理老師陳老師答應星期五的課會有個驚喜。我們到教室時，每組四個人只在桌上找到報紙、膠帶和一把剪刀。我們的任務是搭出最高的塔，而且塔頂要能放一顆小蘋果。我們不能使用任何其他材料，只有二十分鐘。大家都笑了。紙怎麼撐得住一顆蘋果呢？
一開始，我們這組只顧著爭論。每個人都有不同的想法，也沒人想當負責人。後來夢想成為建築師的莉莉提醒我們，高的結構需要寬的底座。我們同意合作：兩個人把紙捲成管子，一個人用膠帶黏起來，一個人檢查高度。這是大量的嘗試與錯誤。我們的第一座塔在蘋果還沒碰到之前就倒了。
之後，我們坐下來努力找出哪裡出了錯。管子太細，底座也太窄。於是我們把管子做得稍微粗一點，並在側邊加上三角形，因為三角形能讓塔更穩固。陳老師走過來給了我們一些回饋。他叫我們在放蘋果之前，先用手指輕輕推一推塔。每一次小小的調整都讓它變得更堅固。
最後，我們的塔有九十公分高，在班上排名第三。冠軍那組有一個獨特的設計，形狀像螺旋。我們不是冠軍，但學到了重要的一課。好點子常常在人們彼此傾聽時產生，而失敗只是通往更好答案路上的一步。

questions.stem: In paragraph 2, what does "It" in "It was a lot of trial and error" refer to?

questions.evidence: It was a lot of trial and error.

title: Life Before Fire
connect: 課文透過神話談人類如何得到火，這篇從歷史課出發，看火如何真實地改變早期人類的生活。
paragraphs: In history class, our teacher asked us to imagine life before fire. At first, I thought it would be only a little uncomfortable, but then she described the long, dark nights. Early people had no thick [[fur|L3-0348]] like other animals, and in winter they could easily [[freeze|L3-0341]]. Without light or heat, they could [[fall victim to|P-0147]] cold, hunger, and wild animals. Life must have been truly [[miserable|L4-0643]].

Fire changed everything. It [[enabled|L3-0288]] people to cook food, and cooked meat was softer and easier to eat. At night, a fire could [[banish|T-0144]] the darkness and keep dangerous animals away. Many scientists believe fire was one of the greatest [[benefits|L3-0075]] in the history of [[mankind|L3-0517]]. People could now sit [[underneath|L6-0941]] the stars and stay warm.

Some historians think that fire also helped to [[set the stage for|P-0149]] the growth of [[civilization|L4-0144]]. People gathered around the warm light to share food and stories. A [[generous|T-0142]] hunter would give meat to those who had none, and the habit of sharing made groups stronger. [[As a result|P-0146]], families could live together, learn from each other, and later make tools from clay and metal, which they could shape only with fire. A tree trunk could even be burned and scraped into a [[hollow|L3-0404]] boat.

I never thought about this until last summer, when our scout camp [[ran out of|P-0144]] dry wood on a rainy night. We could not make a fire, and we sat in the cold with only cold sandwiches for dinner. That night I understood why people valued fire so much. Today we press a button to get warmth and light, but for most of history, a single small flame was a treasure.
zh: 在歷史課上，老師要我們想像沒有火的生活。一開始我以為只是有點不舒服，但當她描述漫長又漆黑的夜晚時，我的想法改變了。早期人類沒有像其他動物那樣厚厚的毛皮，冬天很容易就凍僵。沒有光和熱，他們可能成為寒冷、飢餓和野獸的受害者。生活一定真的很悲慘。
火改變了一切。它讓人類能夠煮熟食物，而煮熟的肉更軟、更容易吃。夜裡，火可以驅走黑暗，並讓危險的動物遠離。許多科學家相信，火是人類歷史上最大的好處之一。人們現在可以坐在星空下仍保持溫暖。
有些歷史學家認為，火也為文明的發展鋪好了路。人們圍著溫暖的火光分享食物和故事。慷慨的獵人會把肉分給沒有東西吃的人，而分享的習慣讓群體更強大。因此，家人可以一起生活、互相學習，後來更用火塑形，做出黏土和金屬的工具。一根樹幹甚至可以被燒過、刮空做成中空的船。
直到去年夏天，我的童軍營在一個下雨的夜晚用完了乾木柴，我才真正想過這件事。我們生不了火，只能坐在寒冷中，晚餐只有冷三明治。那一晚我明白了為什麼人們如此珍惜火。今天我們只要按個按鈕就有溫暖和光，但在歷史的大部分時間裡，一小簇火焰就是珍寶。

questions.explain: generous 是「慷慨的」，文中獵人把肉分給沒有的人，與 kind 意思最接近，故選 (D)。brave（勇敢）雖可形容獵人，但與「分享」無關。
questions.evidence: A generous hunter would give meat to those who had none, and the habit of sharing made groups stronger.

vocab.explain: 池塘一夜之間「結冰」，freeze 最符合，故選 freeze。enable（使能夠）、punish（處罰）、banish（驅逐）都無法描述池塘的變化。

vocab.stem: Regular exercise has many ______ for your health.
vocab.explain: 運動對健康有許多「好處」，故選 benefits。victims（受害者）、thefts（竊盜）、conflicts（衝突）都不能和 for your health 搭配。

title: Remembering Grandpa
connect: 課文介紹墨西哥人如何紀念逝去的親人，這篇改看臺灣家庭在掃墓日如何用故事與家人團聚來懷念祖先。
paragraphs: Every spring, my family travels to my grandfather's hometown for the [[annual|L4-0043]] tomb-sweeping holiday. It is an [[occasion|L3-0579]] for a big family [[reunion|L4-0853]], and my cousins and I [[participate|L0-0100]] by cleaning the grave and placing flowers. When I was little, the quiet hillside used to [[scare me to death|P-0150]]. I thought it was a place only for sadness.

Last month my teacher asked us to interview an elder about how our family remembers people who have died. I spoke with my grandmother. She explained the [[concept|L4-0174]] in a simple way. Life is a [[cycle|L0-0132]], and death is [[inevitable|L5-0458]] for everyone. We do not only [[mourn|L6-0576]]; we also tell stories and share the foods that Grandpa loved. Every year my aunts prepare the dishes [[in advance|P-0153]], and we eat together, as if he were still sitting at the table.

We leave home at [[dawn|L3-0218]] to avoid the heat. The family places Grandpa's favorite tea, fruit and sweet cakes in front of the stone [[in honor of|P-0152]] his memory. My grandmother tells us how he fixed bicycles in the village and taught her to ride one. Everyone laughs, and for a moment the hillside is no longer a silent place. Hearing these small stories, I began to [[recognize|L3-0704]] how much love a family can keep alive through memories.

My grandmother worries that young people are too busy and that the tradition may [[die out|P-0154]] one day. I told her I would continue it. The visit can [[transform|L4-0960]] a quiet slope into a [[joyous|L6-0484]] place full of voices. When I have my own children, I want to bring them there, too, so they can meet their great-grandfather through our stories.
zh: 每年春天，我的家人都會回到祖父的家鄉，參加一年一度的掃墓節日。這是全家大團聚的場合，我和堂表兄弟姊妹會參與清理墳墓、獻上鮮花。小時候，那安靜的山坡總是把我嚇得半死。我以為那只是個悲傷的地方。
上個月老師要我們訪問一位長輩，了解我們家如何紀念已逝的人。我訪問了奶奶。她用簡單的方式解釋這個概念。生命是一個循環，而死亡對每個人來說都是無可避免的。我們不只是哀悼；我們也說故事，並分享爺爺愛吃的食物。每年阿姨們都會事先準備好菜餚，我們一起吃，就像他仍坐在餐桌旁一樣。
我們天剛亮就出門，以避開炎熱。家人把爺爺最愛的茶、水果和甜糕點擺在墓前，向他的記憶致敬。奶奶告訴我們他以前怎麼在村裡修腳踏車，又怎麼教她騎車。大家都笑了，那一刻山坡不再是個寂靜的地方。聽著這些小故事，我開始體會到一個家庭能透過回憶讓多少愛延續下去。
奶奶擔心年輕人太忙，這個傳統有一天可能會消失。我告訴她我會繼續下去。這趟拜訪能把安靜的山坡轉變成充滿聲音的歡樂之地。等我有了自己的孩子，我也想帶他們去，讓他們透過我們的故事認識曾祖父。

options: She cooked dinner on the hill.
She sang old songs to the family.
questions.explain: 第三段說奶奶講爺爺修腳踏車、教她騎車的故事，故選 (B)。清理墳墓是作者與堂表兄弟姊妹做的，不是奶奶獨自做。

questions.evidence: Life is a cycle, and death is inevitable for everyone.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes how the narrator's feelings changed?
questions.explain: 作者小時候覺得山坡可怕、只有悲傷，後來聽了故事，體會到家人用回憶傳遞愛，由害怕轉為珍惜，故選 (C)。
questions.evidence: Hearing these small stories, I began to recognize how much love a family can keep alive through memories.
