questions.explain: 全文說明家人藉由說故事、一起吃飯來懷念祖先，主旨是 (B)。(C) 只是奶奶的擔心，不是全文重點。
questions.evidence: When I have my own children, I want to bring them there, too, so they can meet their great-grandfather through our stories.

vocab.stem: My family has a big ______ every summer, and even my uncle from abroad comes home.
vocab.explain: 每年夏天的「團聚」連國外的叔叔也回來，故選 reunion。reception（接待會）、dawn（黎明）、concept（概念）皆不合語意。

vocab.stem: Seeing the old photos can ______ a sad afternoon into a happy one.
vocab.explain: 老照片能把悲傷的下午「轉變」成快樂的下午，transform A into B 最通順，故選 transform。mourn（哀悼）、anticipate（預期）、recognize（認出）都無法接 into。

title: Tainan, the Old Capital
connect: 課文介紹古都京都，這篇換成臺南這座曾經的首府，看一位學生如何在老街與古蹟間慢慢走。
paragraphs: Last May, my class took a school trip to Tainan, a city that [[previously|T-0146]] served as the [[capital|L4-0121]] of Taiwan. Many tourists see it as a food [[destination|L5-0280]], but our teacher wanted us to explore its history. The city [[boasts|L4-0101]] many [[historic|L3-0402]] buildings, and some of them are more than three hundred years old.

Our guide led us through the [[entrance|L0-0199]] of an old fort, and we climbed up its walls. The view was [[breathtaking|T-0147]]. Red flowers from the flame trees covered the streets like a carpet, and leaves [[rustled|T-0145]] in the warm wind. Then we took a [[leisurely|L4-0587]] walk through narrow lanes. There was no hurry. We stopped to look at old doors, listen to shopkeepers' stories, and taste small cakes.

The old streets had a [[distinctive|L5-0304]] charm. The roofs of the old temples looked [[elegant|L4-0336]], with curved lines and bright colors. An old warehouse had been [[turned into|P-0155]] a small art gallery, and inside, I saw some [[stunning|T-0148]] photographs of the city from a hundred years ago. In the afternoon, we visited a quiet garden where bright paper lanterns seemed to [[stand out|P-0158]] against the grey brick walls. My classmates took photos of everything.

On the bus home, I thought about the day. Some places are famous for a single landmark, but Tainan is a place you must feel with your feet, not only your eyes. I [[fell in love with|P-0159]] its slow pace, and I hope to return with my family one day. Next time, I will try to [[feast my eyes on|P-0156]] the night lights, too.
zh: 去年五月，我們班到臺南校外教學，這座城市曾經是臺灣的首府。許多觀光客把它當作美食景點，但老師希望我們探索它的歷史。這座城市擁有許多古蹟，有些已有三百多年的歷史。
導遊帶我們穿過一座古堡的入口，爬上它的城牆。景色令人屏息。鳳凰木的紅花像地毯一樣鋪滿街道，葉子在暖風中沙沙作響。接著我們在窄巷裡悠閒地散步。沒有人趕時間。我們停下來看老門、聽店家說故事，還嘗了小糕點。
老街有種獨特的魅力。老廟的屋頂看起來很優雅，線條彎曲、色彩鮮明。一間舊倉庫被改造成小小的藝廊，我在裡面看到幾張一百年前這座城市的驚人照片。下午，我們去了一座安靜的庭園，鮮豔的紙燈籠在灰磚牆的襯托下特別顯眼。同學們什麼都想拍。
回程的公車上，我回想這一天。有些地方因為一個地標而出名，但臺南是個需要用腳去感受、不只是用眼睛看的地方。我愛上了它緩慢的步調，也希望有一天能和家人再來。下次，我要好好飽覽夜晚的燈光。

questions.stem: What did the students do in paragraph 2?
options: They rode bicycles around the city.
They climbed the walls of an old fort and walked through lanes.
They listened to a concert in a temple.
They cooked a meal with local people.
questions.explain: 第二段說他們穿過古堡入口、爬上城牆，又在窄巷漫步，故選 (B)。其他活動文中沒有提到。
questions.evidence: Our guide led us through the entrance of an old fort, and we climbed up its walls.

questions.stem: The word "leisurely" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: leisurely 是「悠閒的」，後面緊接 no hurry，與 relaxed 最接近，故選 (A)。
questions.evidence: There was no hurry.

questions.stem: What does "it" refer to in "Many tourists see it as a food destination"?
questions.explain: it 指第一句提到的城市 Tainan，故選 (B)。老堡壘在後面才出現。
questions.evidence: Many tourists see it as a food destination, but our teacher wanted us to explore its history.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The history of a famous fort
How to take good photos of a city
A student's slow and enjoyable trip to an old city
Why tourists visit Tainan for food
questions.explain: 全文敘述作者在臺南的老街、古蹟和庭園間悠閒走訪並愛上這座城市，故選 (C)。(D) 只在第一段提到，是對比而非重點。
questions.evidence: I fell in love with its slow pace, and I hope to return with my family one day.

vocab.stem: The view from the mountain top was so ______ that everyone stopped to take photos.
vocab.explain: 山頂的景色令人屏息，大家才停下來拍照，故選 breathtaking。previous（先前的）、delicate（精緻的）、deliberate（故意的）都不合句意。

vocab.stem: Our town ______ a beautiful old library that was built a hundred years ago.
vocab.explain: 我們鎮「擁有」一座百年老圖書館，boast 作「擁有（值得自豪的東西）」，故選 boasts。rustles（沙沙響）、stuns（使震驚）、blossoms（開花）都不合句意。

title: A Walk with My Eyes Closed
connect: 課文以一個盲人國度的故事談視角與適應，這篇看一場蒙眼體驗活動如何讓學生學會尊重視障者。
paragraphs: Last week our class joined a strange activity. Each of us put on a blindfold and tried to cross the schoolyard with a partner who could see. I [[set off|P-0160]] confidently, but within seconds I [[tumbled|L4-0970]] down a small [[slope|L3-0811]] by the garden and ended up with a [[bruised|T-0149]] knee. My classmates laughed, but I felt nervous and a little ashamed.

Our guest, Ms. Hsu, has been blind since birth. She smiled at us and told us that she did not [[pity|L3-0644]] herself. Every morning she walks the same [[path|T-0152]] to work, and she [[navigates|L6-0586]] by sounds, smells and the feel of the ground under her feet. "I know this neighborhood [[intimately|T-0150]]," she said. She uses her cane [[skillfully|T-0151]], like a musician with an instrument. People who cannot see often [[adapt|L4-0018]] by relying more on their other senses, she explained.

The activity filled me with [[awe|L5-0073]]. I [[clung to|P-0163]] my partner's arm all the way back, and my heart was beating fast. Ms. Hsu said that being blind is not the hardest part of her life. It is how people treat her. Strangers often [[gaze|L4-0435]] at her or talk to her friend instead of to her. [[Worst of all|P-0165]], some people think she cannot do anything alone. [[Nevertheless|L4-0668]], she said, most people are kind when they understand.

At the end, she asked us to [[envision|L5-0335]] a school where everyone can move freely: with smooth sidewalks, clear signs, and classmates who ask before helping. We should do these things not out of pity but [[for the sake of|P-0167]] respect. When I walked home that day, I listened carefully to the street. For the first time, I noticed how much a person can hear.
zh: 上星期我們班參加了一個奇特的活動。每個人戴上眼罩，並由一位看得見的同伴帶著穿過校園。我信心十足地出發，但幾秒鐘內就在花園旁的小斜坡滾了下去，膝蓋還瘀青了。同學們笑了，但我既緊張又有點難為情。
我們的來賓徐女士從出生就看不見。她笑著對我們說，她並不可憐自己。她每天早上走同一條路去上班，靠聲音、氣味和腳下地面的觸感來辨別方向。她說：「我對這一帶非常熟悉。」她用手杖的技巧純熟，就像音樂家使用樂器。她解釋說，看不見的人常常藉由更依賴其他感官來適應。
這個活動讓我充滿敬畏。我一路緊緊抓著同伴的手臂走回來，心跳得很快。徐女士說，看不見並不是她生活中最困難的部分，而是別人怎麼對待她。陌生人常常盯著她看，或是對她的朋友說話而不是對她。最糟的是，有些人以為她什麼事都不能獨自完成。不過，她說，大部分的人在理解之後都很和善。
最後，她請我們想像一所人人都能自由行動的學校：有平整的人行道、清楚的標示，以及會先問過再幫忙的同學。我們做這些不是出於同情，而是為了尊重。那天走路回家時，我仔細聽著街上的聲音。我第一次發現，一個人能聽到這麼多。

questions.explain: 全文透過蒙眼體驗與徐女士的分享，說明學生學會理解與尊重視障者，故選 (B)。(D) 文中最後只是作者發現能聽到很多，並未比較重要性。
questions.evidence: We should do these things not out of pity but for the sake of respect.

vocab.stem: The little boy could not ______ the cold, so his mother gave him a warm coat.
vocab.explain: 男孩無法「適應」寒冷，adapt to 常見搭配，故選 adapt to。envision（想像）、gaze at（凝視）、flee from（逃離）都不合句意。

title: What Her Hands Said
connect: 課文談肢體語言如何傳達訊息，這篇看一位高中生在演講比賽中觀察別人的姿勢與手勢。
paragraphs: Mei-ling joined the [[psychology|L4-0787]] club because she wondered why people sometimes say one thing but show another. At the first meeting, the club advisor explained a simple [[theory|L3-0904]]: much of what we communicate comes not from words but from the face, the voice, and the body. To [[demonstrate|L4-0265]] this, he asked a volunteer to say "I'm fine" in three different ways, and the class had to [[interpret|L4-0556]] each one. Everyone agreed that the same words could mean very different things.

For homework, the members had to [[observe|L3-0578]] people quietly for a week. Mei-ling chose the school speech contest. [[Initially|T-0154]], she listened only to the words. Then she saw that one nervous speaker had [[stiff|L3-0844]] shoulders and kept his hands in his pockets. Another student used big, open [[gestures|L3-0356]] and looked at the judges, and the audience seemed to trust her more. Mei-ling learned that even a quick [[glance|L3-0357]] at someone's posture can tell you a great deal.

Of course, body language is not a secret code. Crossed arms may mean that a person is cold, not angry. The advisor reminded the club that one sign alone is rarely [[significant|L3-0793]], so we should look at the whole picture. [[Under the circumstances|P-0171]], it is wiser to ask a question than to guess. Mei-ling wrote this rule on the first page of her notebook.

Now Mei-ling is more [[conscious|L3-0184]] of her own habits. Before she speaks, she takes a slow breath and relaxes her arms, and her hands then move [[automatically|T-0155]] in a calm way. [[Aside from|P-0173]] giving better speeches, she has changed how she talks with friends. She looks up from her phone, nods, and listens with her eyes [[as well|P-0169]] as her ears. [[Best of all|P-0174]], their talks have become more [[meaningful|L3-0525]].
zh: 美玲加入心理學社，因為她好奇為什麼人們有時說的是一回事，表現出來的卻是另一回事。第一次聚會時，社團指導老師說明了一個簡單的理論：我們傳達的訊息，很大一部分不是來自言語，而是來自臉部、聲音和身體。為了示範這一點，他請一位志願者用三種不同的方式說「我沒事」，全班則要解讀每一種說法。大家都同意，同樣的話可以有非常不同的意思。
作業是要社員安靜地觀察人們一星期。美玲選了學校的演講比賽。起初她只聽內容。後來她發現，有位緊張的講者肩膀僵硬，雙手一直插在口袋裡。另一位同學則做出大方開放的手勢，並看著評審，聽眾似乎更信任她。美玲學到，就算只是快速瞥一眼別人的姿勢，也能得知許多訊息。
當然，肢體語言不是什麼祕密密碼。雙臂交叉可能只是這個人覺得冷，而不是生氣。老師提醒社員，單一個訊號很少具有重大意義，所以我們應該看整體情況。在這種情況下，提問比猜測更明智。美玲把這條規則寫在筆記本的第一頁。
現在美玲更能察覺自己的習慣。開口之前，她會緩緩吸一口氣、放鬆手臂，接著雙手就會自然而然地以沉穩的方式擺動。除了演講變好之外，她和朋友的談話方式也改變了。她會從手機上抬起頭、點點頭，不只用耳朵，也用眼睛傾聽。最棒的是，他們的談話變得更有意義。

title: A Day at the Elephant Sanctuary
connect: 課文談大象被虐待的問題，這篇看一位學生參觀不讓人騎象的保護園區，了解大象真正需要什麼。
paragraphs: During summer vacation, Ting's family visited northern Thailand. Elephants are a big part of the country's tourist [[economy|L4-0332]], and the [[demand|L4-0264]] for rides and shows is high. Ting had read online that some camps cause [[abuse|L5-0007]], so her father chose a sanctuary that does not allow riding. The guide [[highlighted|L5-0431]] this rule at the start of the tour, and she asked every visitor to keep a safe distance from the animals.

The guide explained that elephants are [[intelligent|L3-0440]] animals with [[complex|L0-0064]] feelings. They live in a [[herd|L4-0484]], take care of the young, and seem to remember friends for many years. Ting watched a mother gently help her baby out of the mud with her trunk. "They are not toys," the guide said. "Carrying tourists all day can [[lead to|P-0175]] back pain and [[exhaustion|T-0159]]."

The guide also said that young elephants taken from the wild [[illegally|T-0156]] are especially [[vulnerable|L5-0980]] because they still need their mothers. [[What's more|P-0176]], an animal that lives alone does not get [[adequate|L4-0020]] rest, food, or company. Many elephants at the sanctuary arrived with old injuries, and some will need care for the rest of their lives, so the sanctuary gives them a [[permanent|L4-0725]] home. Workers there [[deal with|P-0178]] these problems patiently, one animal at a time.

In the afternoon, Ting helped prepare fruit and watched the herd walk down to the river. She understood that tourists have power. When visitors choose kind places, the business has a reason to treat animals well. On the bus ride home, she wrote in her journal, "Next time I travel, I will ask one question first: how do they treat their animals?"
zh: 暑假時，婷婷一家人去了泰國北部。大象是這個國家觀光經濟的重要一環，騎象和表演的需求很高。婷婷在網路上讀到，有些營地會虐待大象，所以爸爸選了一個不准騎象的保護園區。導覽員在行程一開始就特別強調這條規定，並要求每位遊客與動物保持安全距離。
導覽員說明，大象是聰明的動物，感情複雜。牠們成群生活、照顧幼象，似乎還能記住朋友很多年。婷婷看到一頭象媽媽用鼻子輕輕把小象從泥巴裡推出來。導覽員說：「牠們不是玩具。整天載遊客可能導致背痛和筋疲力盡。」
導覽員還說，被非法從野外帶走的幼象特別脆弱，因為牠們仍然需要媽媽。此外，獨自生活的動物得不到足夠的休息、食物或同伴。園區裡有許多大象來的時候身上帶著舊傷，有些終其一生都需要照顧，所以園區給牠們一個永久的家。那裡的工作人員耐心地一隻一隻處理這些問題。
下午，婷婷幫忙準備水果，看著象群走向河邊。她明白了遊客其實有力量：當遊客選擇友善的地方，業者就有理由好好對待動物。在回程的巴士上，她在日記裡寫道：「下次旅行，我會先問一個問題：他們怎麼對待自己的動物？」

questions.stem: Why did Ting's father choose this sanctuary?
options: It did not allow people to ride elephants.
It was the cheapest camp in Thailand.
It had the largest herd of elephants.
It offered elephant shows every afternoon.
questions.explain: 第一段說婷婷讀到有些營地會虐待大象，所以爸爸選了不准騎象的園區，故選 (A)。(D) 的表演是園區所反對的，文中並未提供。

questions.stem: The word "vulnerable" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: vulnerable 指「脆弱的、易受傷害的」，文中說幼象還需要媽媽，所以最容易受傷，與 easy to hurt 最接近，故選 (A)。(B) 與「需要媽媽」的意思相反。
questions.evidence: The guide also said that young elephants taken from the wild illegally are especially vulnerable because they still need their mothers.

questions.stem: What does the guide suggest about carrying tourists all day?
options: It is good exercise for elephants.
It is a harmful way to treat elephants.
It is the only job elephants can do.
questions.explain: 導覽員說整天載遊客可能導致背痛和筋疲力盡，表示這對大象有害，故選 (C)。(B) 把傷害說成運動，與導覽員的警告相反。
questions.evidence: Carrying tourists all day can lead to back pain and exhaustion.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Elephants are the most dangerous animals in Thailand.
Visitors can help elephants by choosing places that treat them kindly.
Thailand has too many tourists every summer.
Baby elephants should be kept away from their mothers.
questions.explain: 全文從參觀園區、認識大象，到婷婷領悟遊客的選擇能影響業者，主旨是選擇善待動物的地方就能幫助大象，故選 (B)。(D) 與文中「幼象需要媽媽」相反。
questions.evidence: When visitors choose kind places, the business has a reason to treat animals well.

vocab.stem: The price of oil is high because the world's ______ for it keeps growing.
vocab.explain: 石油價格高是因為全世界對它的「需求」持續增加，故選 demand。herd（牛群）與 abuse（虐待）都不能說明價格上升的原因。

vocab.stem: A tiny bird that has just left its nest is very ______ to cold weather and hungry cats.
vocab.explain: 剛離巢的小鳥對寒冷天氣和飢餓的貓「很脆弱、容易受傷」，故選 vulnerable。permanent（永久的）和 adequate（足夠的）都無法與 to cold weather 搭配。

title: Festival Season in Grandma's Town
connect: 課文談媽祖遶境的盛況，這篇看一位學生跟著奶奶參加家鄉的春季廟會，體會人情味與文化傳承。
paragraphs: Every spring, Grandma's small town in central Taiwan holds a big temple festival. For a week, a [[throng|T-0161]] of visitors fills the streets, and many of them come on a [[pilgrimage|T-0160]] that families have walked for generations. Last year, I went to see it for myself. My grandmother woke me at dawn. "We must [[set out|P-0181]] early," she said, "or we will miss the start."

As the sun rose, a decorated sedan chair [[emerged|L4-0342]] from the temple gate, and the drums began. I could not guess the [[exact|L0-0287]] number of people, but there were thousands. The local [[authorities|L4-0078]] closed several roads, and volunteers in bright vests guided the walkers. [[Undoubtedly|L5-0943]], it was the loudest morning of my life, but it was also the most exciting.

What surprised me most was the [[hospitality|L6-0422]]. Neighbors set up tables along the road and [[enthusiastically|T-0163]] offered tea, rice balls, and cold water to strangers, with no charge at all. [[In the meantime|P-0183]], the primary school next door opened its gym, and the teachers there prepared simple [[accommodation|L5-0011]] and basic [[facilities|L4-0383]], such as showers and a first-aid corner, for people who had walked all night.

Grandma says the festival is part of our cultural [[heritage|L5-0430]]. Each [[ritual|L5-0744]] has a meaning, and the whole town takes part, from children to the elderly, selling [[all manner of|P-0184]] snacks or carrying flags. I used to think it was only noise and crowds. Now I see that it brings neighbors together and tells young people where they come from.
zh: 每年春天，奶奶位在台灣中部的小鎮都會舉辦盛大的廟會。一整個星期，大批遊客擠滿街道，其中許多人是來進行一趟家家戶戶走了好幾代的朝聖之旅。去年我親自去看了。奶奶天一亮就叫醒我。她說：「我們一定要早點出發，不然會錯過開頭。」
太陽升起時，一頂裝飾華麗的轎子從廟門出現，鼓聲隨即響起。我猜不出確切的人數，但肯定有好幾千人。地方當局封閉了好幾條道路，穿著鮮豔背心的志工則引導著步行的人。毫無疑問，那是我這輩子最吵的早晨，但也是最興奮的早晨。
最讓我驚訝的是人們的好客。鄰居們在路邊擺好桌子，熱情地請陌生人喝茶、吃飯糰、喝冰水，完全不收費。同時，隔壁的小學開放了體育館，老師們為走了一整夜的人準備了簡單的住宿和基本設施，像是淋浴間和急救角落。
奶奶說，這個廟會是我們文化遺產的一部分。每一個儀式都有它的意義，全鎮的人從孩子到老人都會參與，有的賣各式各樣的小吃，有的扛著旗子。我以前以為那只是吵鬧和人擠人。現在我明白，它把鄰居們凝聚在一起，也讓年輕人知道自己從哪裡來。

questions.stem: Why did the narrator's grandmother wake her at dawn?
options: They had to go to school early.
The festival would start soon and they did not want to miss it.
The grandmother wanted to cook breakfast.
The town closed the roads at noon.
questions.explain: 第一段奶奶說要早點出發，否則會錯過開頭，故選 (B)。(D) 文中沒有提到中午封路，封路是第二段由地方當局處理的事。
questions.evidence: "We must set out early," she said, "or we will miss the start."

questions.stem: The word "hospitality" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: hospitality 是「好客、款待」，後面描述鄰居免費請陌生人喝茶、吃飯糰，正是對客人的親切款待，故選 (A)。(C) 人群是第一段的 throng，不是這個字的意思。
questions.evidence: Neighbors set up tables along the road and enthusiastically offered tea, rice balls, and cold water to strangers, with no charge at all.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3, "people who had walked all night" most likely refers to ______.
options: the teachers at the primary school
the neighbors who set up tables
the visitors taking part in the walk
questions.explain: 第三段說學校為走了一整夜的人提供住宿和設施，這些人就是參加步行的訪客，故選 (D)。老師和鄰居是提供協助的一方，(A)(C) 不合。
questions.evidence: In the meantime, the primary school next door opened its gym, and the teachers there prepared simple accommodation and basic facilities, such as showers and a first-aid corner, for people who had walked all night.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to travel safely in central Taiwan
Why festivals are too noisy for young people
How a student came to value a local festival and its community spirit
How schools should be used as hotels
questions.explain: 全文敘述作者參加廟會的所見所聞，最後從覺得吵鬧轉為體會它凝聚鄰里、傳承文化，故選 (C)。(B) 是作者「以前」的想法，結論已經改變。
questions.evidence: Now I see that it brings neighbors together and tells young people where they come from.

vocab.stem: The old temple is an important part of the town's cultural ______, so the town works hard to protect it.
vocab.explain: 古老的廟是小鎮文化「遺產」的重要部分，所以鎮民努力保護它，故選 heritage。exaggeration（誇張）和 throng（人群）都無法與 cultural 搭配。

vocab.stem: The hotel offers free parking and other ______ such as a swimming pool and a gym.
vocab.explain: 飯店提供免費停車位，以及游泳池和健身房等「設施」，故選 facilities。rituals（儀式）、blessings（祝福）都不是飯店提供的設備。

title: Printing a Home for Fish
connect: 課文介紹3D列印的各種用途，這篇看海洋社的學生如何用3D列印做出給魚類藏身的人工礁塊。
paragraphs: Our marine club wanted to help [[protect|T-0169]] the sea life near Taiwan's coast. Our teacher explained that fish need a safe [[habitat|L5-0424]], and that when natural reefs are damaged, scientists sometimes place [[artificial|L4-0057]] structures in the water to give animals a place to hide. Buying such structures can [[cost an arm and a leg|P-0186]], though, so we looked for a cheaper way.

Our teacher found a 3D printer in the science room. It builds an object one thin [[layer|L5-0502]] at a time, following a design made on a computer. At first, the idea of printing a reef sounded [[ridiculous|L5-0737]] to us, but a short video showed that scientists really do this. We had to [[map out|P-0189]] every step on a big sheet of paper: the shape, the size, the number of holes, and the time needed for each block.

The printer is an [[electronic|L3-0282]] machine, so we needed some special [[equipment|L4-0357]], such as a power supply and a tray for the clay-like material. The printer also works best at the right [[temperature|T-0168]]. Each [[individual|L0-0050]] block was [[relatively|T-0167]] small, so we could [[assemble|L4-0062]] them like toy bricks into a larger shape. We were able to [[build on|P-0188]] the design from last year's club, which saved us a lot of time.

Printing only the pieces we need can also [[reduce|L3-0707]] waste, and every attempt, even a failed one, taught us something. Our teacher says that our small model will be tested in a tank before it goes anywhere near the sea. We do not know yet whether fish will like it, but we are proud. Our time and patience are [[precious|L3-0666]], and we have chosen to spend them on something useful.
zh: 我們的海洋社想幫忙保護台灣海岸附近的海洋生物。老師說明，魚類需要安全的棲息地，而當天然珊瑚礁受損時，科學家有時會在水中放置人工結構物，讓動物有地方躲藏。不過，購買這類結構物可能貴得嚇人，所以我們想找比較便宜的方法。
老師在科學教室找到一台3D印表機。它依照電腦上做好的設計，一次堆疊一層薄薄的材料來做出物體。起初我們覺得列印珊瑚礁這個想法聽起來很荒謬，但一部短片顯示科學家真的這麼做。我們得在一大張紙上把每個步驟規劃出來：形狀、大小、孔洞的數量，以及每個礁塊所需的時間。
印表機是電子機器，所以我們需要一些特別的設備，像是電源供應器和一個放類似黏土材料的托盤。印表機在適當的溫度下也運作得最好。每一個礁塊都相對較小，所以我們可以像積木一樣把它們組裝成較大的形狀。我們能在去年社團的設計上繼續發展，這替我們省下很多時間。
只列印需要的零件也能減少浪費，而每一次嘗試，即使是失敗的，都讓我們學到東西。老師說，我們的小模型在靠近大海之前會先在水槽裡測試。我們還不知道魚是否會喜歡它，但我們很驕傲。我們的時間與耐心很珍貴，而我們選擇把它們花在有用的事情上。

questions.stem: Why did the club look for a cheaper way to make artificial structures?

Buying ready-made ones could be very expensive.
The structures were too heavy to carry.
questions.explain: 第一段說購買這類結構物可能貴得嚇人，所以他們想找便宜的方法，故選 (B)。(D) 與文意不符，文中是說天然礁受損時才需要人工結構。

questions.stem: The word "ridiculous" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: ridiculous 是「荒謬的」，學生起初覺得用印表機做礁塊太離譜，與 very silly 最接近，故選 (A)。他們後來看了影片才相信，所以 (D) 不合。

questions.stem: Why will the model be tested in a tank first?
options: The club wants to be sure it works before using it in the sea.
The tank is cheaper than the sea.
The model is made of metal.

questions.evidence: Our teacher says that our small model will be tested in a tank before it goes anywhere near the sea.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to use a 3D printer to make toys
Why fish are disappearing from Taiwan

vocab.stem: My mother wears a warm coat because the ______ drops quickly at night in the mountains.
vocab.explain: 山上夜晚「氣溫」降得很快，所以媽媽穿暖外套，故選 temperature。texture（質地）和 balance（平衡）都無法說明「降得很快」的對象。

vocab.stem: It will take about an hour to ______ the new bookshelf because there are so many small parts.
vocab.explain: 書櫃有很多小零件，所以需要一個小時來「組裝」，故選 assemble。protect（保護）、reduce（減少）都不能接 bookshelf 表達這個動作。

title: The Bees on Our Roof
connect: 課文探討蜜蜂減少的原因，這篇看學校屋頂花園的養蜂經驗，認識蜜蜂為何重要、我們能怎麼幫忙。
paragraphs: Our school has a small garden on the roof, and last spring a beekeeper visited us to set up two hives. He explained that bees [[pollinate|T-0172]] flowers by carrying pollen from one flower to another, and that many of the fruits and vegetables on our plates depend on this work. Without bees, some crops would be harder to grow and more expensive to buy. Bees truly [[deserve|L4-0272]] our respect.

Yet beekeepers around the world have faced a [[mystery|L3-0562]]: in some places, large numbers of bees have suddenly disappeared. Scientists have collected [[evidence|L4-0366]] for years, and they believe there is no single cause. Several [[factors|L0-0123]] seem to work together. Many bee deaths [[result from|P-0192]] a mix of disease, tiny mites, and some [[pesticides|T-0171]] sprayed on crops. As cities grow, wild flowers also disappear, so the food [[supply|L0-0075]] for bees [[shrinks|L3-0790]]. [[On top of|P-0194]] that, hot summers and sudden storms make life harder for them.

This [[phenomenon|L4-0730]] may sound far away, but ordinary people can help. Our science club planted lavender, mint, and sunflowers around the hives, and we put out a shallow dish of water with small stones so that bees can drink without falling in. We hope the bees will [[thrive|L5-0905]] in our garden. The beekeeper told us that a healthy hive can even [[reproduce|L6-0755]] when part of the colony leaves with the old queen to start a home somewhere else.

Each of us can [[contribute|L4-0209]] a little. We can plant flowers on balconies, ask farmers about how they protect crops, and avoid spraying chemicals at home. [[In the long run|P-0195]], these small choices may keep both bees and our food safe. When I look at the roof garden now, I no longer see only flowers. I see a small team at work.
zh: 我們學校的屋頂上有一座小花園，去年春天，一位養蜂人來替我們架設了兩個蜂箱。他說明，蜜蜂把花粉從一朵花帶到另一朵花，為花授粉；我們盤子上的許多水果和蔬菜都仰賴這項工作。沒有蜜蜂，有些作物會更難種，買起來也會更貴。蜜蜂真的值得我們尊敬。
然而，世界各地的養蜂人卻遇到了一個謎：在某些地方，大量蜜蜂突然消失了。科學家蒐集了多年的證據，他們認為原因不只一個，而是好幾個因素似乎共同作用。許多蜜蜂的死亡是由疾病、微小的蟎蟲，以及一些噴灑在作物上的農藥混合造成的。隨著城市擴大，野花也消失了，所以蜜蜂的食物供應縮減。除此之外，炎熱的夏天和突如其來的暴風雨也讓牠們的生活更艱難。
這個現象聽起來也許很遙遠，但一般人也能幫上忙。我們的科學社在蜂箱周圍種了薰衣草、薄荷和向日葵，並放了一個淺水盤，裡面放著小石頭，讓蜜蜂喝水時不會掉進去。我們希望蜜蜂能在我們的花園裡茁壯。養蜂人告訴我們，一個健康的蜂群甚至能繁殖：當蜂群的一部分跟著原本的蜂后離開，到別處建立新家。
我們每個人都可以貢獻一點力量。我們可以在陽台種花、詢問農夫如何保護作物，並避免在家裡噴灑化學藥劑。長遠來看，這些小選擇也許能同時保住蜜蜂和我們的食物安全。現在我看著屋頂花園，看到的不只是花，而是一個正在工作的小團隊。

options: They help many fruits and vegetables grow.
They clean the water in the garden.
questions.explain: 第一段說蜜蜂替花授粉，許多水果和蔬菜都仰賴這項工作，故選 (B)。其他選項文中都沒提到，(D) 暴風雨反而是第二段說對蜜蜂不利的因素。
questions.evidence: He explained that bees pollinate flowers by carrying pollen from one flower to another, and that many of the fruits and vegetables on our plates depend on this work.

questions.stem: The word "shrinks" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.

questions.evidence: As cities grow, wild flowers also disappear, so the food supply for bees shrinks.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a possible cause of bee loss?
options: Too many beekeepers in the city
questions.explain: 第二段列出疾病、蟎蟲、農藥、野花減少、炎熱夏天與暴風雨，沒有提到養蜂人太多，故選 (D)。其餘三項都在文中出現。
questions.evidence: On top of that, hot summers and sudden storms make life harder for them.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Bees are in trouble for several reasons, and ordinary people can help them.
Scientists have found one simple cause for the bee mystery.
School gardens should be built only on roofs.
questions.explain: 全文先說蜜蜂的重要，再談消失的多重原因，最後說明學生能做的事，故選 (A)。(B) 與文中「沒有單一原因」相反。
questions.evidence: Scientists have collected evidence for years, and they believe there is no single cause.

vocab.stem: Without enough water and sun, these young plants will not ______ in the garden.
vocab.explain: 沒有足夠的水和陽光，這些幼苗無法在花園裡「茁壯成長」，故選 thrive。deserve（應得）和 pollinate（授粉）都不能以 plants 為主詞表達這個意思。

vocab.stem: The detective found no ______ that the stranger had been in the room that night.
vocab.explain: 偵探沒有找到陌生人那晚在房間裡的「證據」，故選 evidence。mystery（謎）、phenomenon（現象）都不適合與 found no 和 that 子句搭配。

title: The Day We Swapped Clothes
connect: 課文討論快時尚的代價，這篇看一位學生舉辦校內舊衣交換日，讓衣服有第二次生命。
paragraphs: Last month, my friend Yu-hsuan [[made her way to|P-0196]] the school gym carrying two heavy bags of clothes. She had planned a clothing swap, and students could bring in old shirts and jackets and take home something new for free. Over the past [[decade|L3-0220]], cheap clothes have become easy to find. Shops copy the latest [[trend|L3-0928]] and put new [[fashion|L0-0037]] on the shelves every few weeks.

Many people love [[affordable|T-0173]] clothes that look [[stylish|L6-0874]], but Yu-hsuan wanted to see the other side. She learned that making one shirt uses a lot of water, and that some factories let [[toxic|L5-0915]] [[dye|L4-0323]] flow into rivers. Workers who [[manufacture|L4-0614]] clothes in some places earn very low pay. Many shoppers buy a new shirt [[at the drop of a hat|P-0197]], wear it only a few times, and then [[discard|L6-0254]] it, so a huge pile of unwanted clothing grows every year.

Yu-hsuan did not want to blame anyone. She simply thought that students could be more [[responsible|T-0175]] if they had a better choice. She asked classmates to bring clothes that were still clean and in good shape. On swap day, the gym looked like a small shop with no price tags. Everyone had free [[access|L4-0008]] to the racks, and a few students were happy to find an almost new sweater that fit them well.

By the end of the afternoon, more than two hundred pieces had found new owners. Yu-hsuan hung a sign near the door: "Buy less, choose well, wear it longer." She explained that the swap was held [[so as to|P-0199]] show that a closet can be refreshed without spending any money. Perhaps we cannot change the whole industry, but we can learn to dress [[sustainably|T-0176]], one shirt at a time.
zh: 上個月，我的朋友玉萱提著兩大袋衣服走進學校體育館。她規劃了一場衣物交換，同學們可以帶來舊襯衫和外套，再免費帶走新的衣服。在過去十年裡，便宜的衣服變得很容易買到。商店模仿最新的流行，每隔幾週就把新的時裝擺上貨架。
許多人喜歡價格實惠又時髦的衣服，但玉萱想看看另一面。她得知，做一件襯衫要用掉很多水，有些工廠還會讓有毒的染料流進河裡。在某些地方，製造衣服的工人領的薪水非常低。許多消費者一時衝動就買下一件新襯衫，只穿幾次就丟掉，所以每年都有一大堆不要的衣服越堆越高。
玉萱不想責怪任何人。她只是認為，如果學生有更好的選擇，就可以更負責任。她請同學帶來仍然乾淨、狀況良好的衣服。交換日當天，體育館看起來像一間沒有標價的小店。每個人都能自由使用衣架上的衣服，有幾位同學很開心地找到一件幾乎全新又合身的毛衣。
下午結束時，有兩百多件衣服找到了新主人。玉萱在門邊掛了一塊牌子：「少買、買好、穿久一點。」她解釋說，舉辦交換日是為了證明：不花一毛錢也能讓衣櫃煥然一新。也許我們無法改變整個產業，但我們可以學著永續地穿衣，一次一件。

Learn to sew their own shirts.
Buy cheap clothes from a shop.

questions.stem: The word "discard" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: discard 是「丟棄」，文中說人們穿幾次就丟掉，所以堆起大量不要的衣服，與 throw away 最接近，故選 (B)。(D) 修理與「一堆不要的衣服」不符。

questions.stem: Why did Yu-hsuan hold the swap instead of blaming shoppers?
options: She wanted to give students a better choice.
She did not believe clothes cause problems.
She wanted to open a shop at school.
She thought cheap clothes were always good.
questions.explain: 第三段說她不想責怪任何人，認為學生有更好的選擇就能更負責任，所以辦交換日，故選 (A)。(B) 與第二段她了解到的問題相反。
questions.evidence: She simply thought that students could be more responsible if they had a better choice.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How cheap clothes are made in factories
How a student's clothing swap offers a more responsible way to dress
Why students should stop wearing new clothes
How to start a shop at school
questions.explain: 全文從快時尚的問題談到玉萱辦交換日，提供更負責任的穿衣方式，故選 (B)。(C) 太極端，文中並沒有要同學完全不穿新衣。
questions.evidence: Perhaps we cannot change the whole industry, but we can learn to dress sustainably, one shirt at a time.

vocab.stem: Many young people follow the latest fashion ______ and buy the same kind of shoes.
vocab.explain: 許多年輕人追隨最新的流行「趨勢」，買同樣款式的鞋子，故選 trend。decade（十年）和 wage（工資）都不能與 fashion 搭配成這個語意。

vocab.stem: Wearing a helmet is the ______ thing to do when you ride a bike on the road.
vocab.explain: 騎車上路時戴安全帽是「負責任」的做法，故選 responsible。toxic（有毒的）與 stylish（時髦的）都不是對這個行為的合理評價。

title: A Week Without My Phone
connect: 課本談一場關乎自由與慾望的打賭，這篇改看一位高中生和表哥為「一週不用手機」打賭，從中學到什麼。
paragraphs: Last winter, my cousin Jason and I had a long [[debate|T-0177]] about smartphones. He [[claimed|L0-0016]] that nobody could live without one for a week, but I [[insisted|T-0178]] that anyone with a strong will could do it. Our argument went [[back and forth|P-0200]] for an hour, so we decided to settle it with a bet. If I kept my phone in a drawer for seven days, Jason would give me his comic book collection, his most precious [[property|L3-0681]]. If I failed, I would do his chores for a month. That was the [[penalty|L4-0720]] we agreed on, and we wrote every rule on paper.

The first days were hard. My room felt like a [[prison|L0-0318]], and the hours seemed to [[wear on|P-0201]] slowly. My phone had always been my constant [[companion|L4-0164]], and I had never noticed how often I reached for it. On the third night, the idea of [[surrender|L4-0928]] was very tempting. However, I looked at the paper on my desk and kept going.

Then something changed. I picked up the first [[volume|L3-0970]] of a long adventure novel and finished it in two evenings. I rode my bike along the river, and I sat with my grandfather while he told me stories about his childhood. I even [[acquired|L4-0017]] a new hobby, drawing, because I finally had time to look at things carefully. My [[mental|L3-0532]] state improved, too. I slept better and felt calmer in the morning.

On the seventh day, Jason knocked on my door with a serious face. It had never [[crossed my mind|P-0205]] that he would look so nervous, but he had lost the bet and he knew it. I took the comic books, but they were [[by no means|P-0204]] the best part of the week. The experience taught me a [[profound|L5-0666]] lesson: being alone with your own thoughts is not always bad. Now I use my phone with a clear [[intention|L4-0551]], and I put it away when I do not need it.
zh: 去年冬天，我和表哥傑森針對智慧型手機展開一場很長的辯論。他聲稱沒有人能在沒有手機的情況下生活一週，但我堅持只要意志堅強，誰都做得到。我們的爭論來來回回持續了一個小時，所以決定用打賭來分出高下。如果我把手機收在抽屜裡七天，傑森就要把他的漫畫收藏送給我，那是他最珍貴的財產。如果我失敗了，就得幫他做一個月的家事。這就是我們約定的懲罰，而且每一條規則都寫在紙上。
頭幾天很難熬。我的房間像是一座監獄，時間好像過得特別慢。手機一直是我形影不離的同伴，我卻從沒發現自己有多常伸手去拿它。第三天晚上，投降的念頭非常誘人。不過，我看了看桌上那張紙，還是繼續撐下去。
接著情況改變了。我拿起一部長篇冒險小說的第一冊，兩個晚上就讀完了。我沿著河邊騎腳踏車，也陪爺爺坐著聽他講小時候的故事。我甚至培養了一個新嗜好──畫畫，因為我終於有時間仔細觀察事物。我的心理狀態也變好了，睡得更好，早上也覺得更平靜。
第七天，傑森一臉嚴肅地來敲我的房門。我從沒想過他會那麼緊張，但他輸了這場賭，他自己也知道。我拿走了漫畫書，但那絕不是這一週最棒的部分。這次經驗教了我深刻的一課：獨自面對自己的想法並不總是壞事。現在我帶著明確的目的使用手機，不需要時就把它收起來。

questions.stem: What did Jason say about living without a smartphone?
options: Nobody could do it for a whole week.
Anyone with a strong will could do it.
It would make people healthier in a month.
It was easy if you had a hobby.
questions.explain: 第一段說傑森聲稱沒有人能一週不用手機，故選 (A)。(B) 是「我」的主張，和傑森的立場相反，是容易混淆的選項。

title: Libraries on the Move
connect: 課本介紹船上學校如何把教育帶給淹水地區的孩子，這篇改看「行動圖書館」怎麼把書送到偏遠地區的讀者手上。
paragraphs: In my English class, I gave a short talk about libraries that travel to their readers. Many people think a library must be a big building, but for children in remote places, distance is often the biggest [[barrier|L4-0087]]. A heavy storm can [[flood|L3-0330]] a road, and a [[muddy|L4-0656]] path can take hours to cross on foot. For these children, books can seem as far away as the moon.

A mobile library solves the problem by bringing books to the readers. In many countries, a small truck or bus is turned into a library, and in parts of Kenya, librarians have even used camels to carry books across dry land. Each visit is a short reading [[session|L5-0775]], and the librarian lets only a few children come in [[at a time|P-0207]]. Some vehicles carry [[solar|L4-0901]] [[panels|L4-0708]] on the roof. Once the panels are [[installed|L4-0539]], the lights and computers can work even when there is no power plant nearby.

Mobile libraries are not only about stories. Many of them offer [[practical|L3-0665]] help, such as simple books about health and [[nutrition|L5-0575]]. A farmer can learn how to protect his crops, and a parent can learn how to read with a child. When families have more knowledge, they can make better choices, and their [[financial|L4-0401]] situation may slowly improve. Children who live in areas [[at risk of|P-0209]] floods or [[severe|L4-0881]] storms often miss many school days, so a library that comes to them is a great help.

Of course, the system is not perfect. Fuel is expensive, and the vehicles need regular repairs. Still, I think the idea is [[promising|L4-0775]] because it is [[based on|P-0208]] a simple belief: every child deserves an [[opportunity|L3-0586]] to learn. After my talk, a classmate asked how she could help. I told her we could start by collecting used books for a mobile library in our own county.
zh: 在英文課上，我做了一場短講，主題是會移動到讀者身邊的圖書館。許多人以為圖書館一定是一棟大建築，但對偏遠地區的孩子來說，距離往往才是最大的障礙。一場大雨就可能淹沒道路，泥濘的小徑要走上好幾個小時。對這些孩子來說，書本彷彿遠在月球。
行動圖書館把書直接送到讀者面前，解決了這個問題。在許多國家，小貨車或巴士被改造成圖書館，在肯亞的部分地區，圖書館員甚至用駱駝馱書穿越乾燥的土地。每次到訪就是一段簡短的閱讀時間，館員一次只讓幾個孩子進來。有些車輛在車頂裝了太陽能板，板子裝好之後，即使附近沒有發電廠，燈和電腦也能運作。
行動圖書館不只提供故事書。許多館藏還提供實用的協助，例如關於健康與營養的簡單書籍。農夫可以學到如何保護作物，家長可以學到如何陪孩子閱讀。當家庭擁有更多知識，就能做出更好的選擇，經濟狀況也可能慢慢改善。住在有淹水或嚴重暴風雨風險地區的孩子，常常缺很多天課，所以一座會來找他們的圖書館幫助很大。
當然，這套做法並不完美。燃料很貴，車輛也需要定期維修。不過我認為這個點子很有前景，因為它建立在一個簡單的信念上：每個孩子都應該有學習的機會。演講結束後，有位同學問我能怎麼幫忙。我告訴她，我們可以先從為本縣的行動圖書館蒐集二手書開始。

title: Saving the Old Market
connect: 課本談埃及古神殿在建水壩時如何兼顧發展與保存，這篇改看一群台灣高中生如何為社區老市場爭取保留。
paragraphs: Every Saturday morning, I walk with my grandmother to the old market near our home. She is [[fond|L3-0336]] of it, and so am I. The stalls sell fresh vegetables, handmade noodles, and cheap breakfast, and many [[residents|L5-0726]] have shopped there for sixty years. Last spring, a notice appeared on the wall: the market would be torn down to [[make way for|P-0218]] a tall shopping center and a wider road.

Some neighbors welcomed the plan. They said that [[urban|L3-0949]] [[development|T-0183]] would bring better [[transport|L3-0925]] and shorter trips to work. Others disagreed. To them, the market was a [[treasure|T-0184]] that gave the neighborhood its [[identity|L0-0141]]. A shopping center could [[replace|L3-0719]] the shops, my grandmother said, but it could not replace the friendships built over a counter.

My class decided to start a [[campaign|L4-0116]]. We talked with vendors, took photos, and collected signatures from almost everyone who walked by. Our teacher reminded us that we were not against [[progress|T-0182]]; we only wanted the city to listen. Some of the market's roofs were [[in need of|P-0213]] repair, and we admitted this honestly in our letter. Time was short, so we worked after school every day.

A few weeks later, the city invited us to a public meeting. Planners, vendors, and students all had a chance to speak. [[In the end|P-0212]], the city chose a new plan. The main hall of the market will stay and be repaired, while the new road will be built behind it. The plan is not perfect, but it shows that a city can [[strike a balance|P-0211]] between keeping its history and building for the future. Change does not have to [[endanger|L4-0347]] the places we love. It is [[crucial|L5-0245]] to ask the people who live in a place what they need.
zh: 每個週六早上，我都會陪奶奶走到家附近的老市場。她很喜歡那裡，我也是。攤位賣著新鮮蔬菜、手工麵條和便宜的早餐，許多居民在那裡買菜已經六十年了。去年春天，牆上貼出一張公告：市場將被拆除，為一座高樓購物中心和一條更寬的馬路讓路。
有些鄰居歡迎這項計畫。他們說都市發展會帶來更好的交通，上班的路程也會縮短。其他人不同意。對他們來說，市場是一項珍寶，賦予這個社區獨特的特色。奶奶說，購物中心可以取代那些店面，卻無法取代隔著攤位建立起來的情誼。
我們班決定發起一場活動。我們訪問攤商、拍照，並向幾乎每一位經過的人收集連署。老師提醒我們，我們不是反對進步，只是希望市政府能傾聽。市場有些屋頂確實需要修繕，我們也在信裡誠實地承認這一點。時間很緊迫，所以我們每天放學後都在忙。
幾週後，市政府邀請我們參加公聽會。規劃人員、攤商和學生都有機會發言。最後，市政府選擇了新的方案：市場的主廳會保留並加以修復，而新道路則蓋在它的後方。這個方案並不完美，但它顯示城市可以在保存歷史與為未來建設之間取得平衡。改變不必危及我們所愛的地方。詢問住在那裡的人他們需要什麼，是很關鍵的事。

title: Fish for Tomorrow
connect: 課本介紹蘭嶼飛魚季中人與海洋共生的傳統，這篇改看一位都市學生在東海岸漁村學到的永續捕魚觀念。
paragraphs: During our school trip to a small fishing village on Taiwan's east coast, I felt like [[a fish out of water|P-0223]]. I grew up in a big city, where fish come from the supermarket in plastic boxes. Here, about three hundred [[inhabitants|L6-0451]] live beside the sea, and every family seems to know the weather, the waves, and the moon like an old friend.

On our first morning, an old fisher named Mr. Lin showed us his boat and explained his rules. He uses nets with large holes so that young fish can swim out, and he never fishes in the season when some [[species|L4-0906]] lay their eggs. He said these [[guidelines|L5-0422]] were not written in any law book; his father had taught them to him. The [[consequence|L4-0186]] of taking too many fish is simple, he explained: one day the sea will be empty. Every seafood meal [[comes with|P-0221]] a choice.

That evening, a local family let us [[sample|T-0188]] fresh fish cooked in their kitchen. The sea was [[plentiful|L4-0741]] that week, but the cook told us she never asks the boats to bring in more than people need. A good [[harvest|L3-0385]] must follow nature's rhythm. Many [[indigenous|L5-0455]] communities along the coast have followed seasonal rules for a long time, and their [[wisdom|L3-0994]] teaches us how to live in [[harmony|L4-0477]] with the ocean.

Before we left, our teacher asked us not to [[disturb|L4-0308]] the fishing boats on the beach, and we all agreed. Back at school, I realized that we are all [[in the same boat|P-0224]]: the ocean belongs to everyone. No one can [[guarantee|L4-0467]] that fish will always be there, but each of us can choose seafood from careful fishers and ask where the fish came from. If we do, there may still be fish for generations [[to come|P-0222]].
zh: 在學校旅行到台灣東海岸一個小漁村時，我覺得自己像離開水的魚，格格不入。我在大城市長大，那裡的魚是裝在塑膠盒裡從超市買來的。在這裡，大約三百位居民住在海邊，每一戶人家似乎都像熟識的老朋友一樣了解天氣、海浪和月亮。
第一天早上，一位姓林的老漁夫帶我們看他的船，並說明他的規矩。他用網眼很大的漁網，讓小魚可以游出去，而且在某些物種產卵的季節，他絕不出海捕魚。他說這些準則並沒有寫在任何法律書裡，是他父親教他的。他解釋，捕太多魚的後果很簡單：有一天海會被捕空。每一餐海鮮都伴隨著一個選擇。
那天晚上，一戶當地人家讓我們試吃他們在廚房煮的新鮮魚料理。那週海裡的魚很豐富，但煮飯的阿姨告訴我們，她從不要求漁船帶回超過大家需要的量。好的收成必須順著大自然的節奏。海岸沿線許多原住民社群長久以來遵循季節性的規則，他們的智慧教我們如何與海洋和諧共處。
離開前，老師請我們不要打擾海灘上的漁船，大家都答應了。回到學校後，我體會到我們都在同一條船上：海洋屬於每一個人。沒有人能保證魚永遠都在，但我們每個人都可以選擇來自謹慎漁民的海鮮，並詢問魚是從哪裡來的。如果我們這麼做，未來世世代代或許仍有魚可吃。

title: A Diplomat's Pen
connect: 課本談一位波蘭女子冒險救出許多孩子，這篇改看一位日本外交官如何用簽發簽證幫助逃難的人。
paragraphs: On a school trip to Japan, my class visited a small memorial hall in Gifu. I must [[admit|L0-0260]] that I knew almost nothing about the man it honors, Chiune Sugihara. Our guide explained that in 1940 he was a Japanese diplomat working in Lithuania, a country in northern Europe. War was spreading across the continent, and many families were trying to escape.

These refugees needed visas to travel through Japan, but they could not [[obtain|L4-0683]] them easily. Each day, a growing crowd waited outside the consulate. Sugihara asked his government for permission several times, and each time the answer was no. He talked with his wife and with a [[colleague|L4-0155]], and then he made a hard decision. He began to write visas by hand, one after another, pressing his official [[seal|L3-0773]] onto each [[document|L5-0307]]. Some accounts say he was still writing when his train was about to leave.

It took a [[courageous|L4-0228]] and [[compassionate|L5-0172]] person to do that, because he risked his career. When the families, far from home and feeling [[isolated|T-0190]], held the papers in their hands, they [[breathed a sigh of relief|P-0226]]. Officials usually [[keep a record|P-0229]] of every visa they issue, and today a list of names helps families learn about their past. Our guide said that Sugihara never spoke much about his [[selfless|T-0191]] act.

Many of the people he helped later built new lives in other countries. [[To this day|P-0230]], their children and grandchildren remember his name. Standing in the quiet hall, I tried to [[take in|P-0228]] everything I had learned. Not everyone has the chance to change history, but his [[bravery|L3-0093]] showed me that one signature can change a family's future. I may not be able to [[convince|L4-0216]] everyone to act like him, but I can start by asking how I can help someone near me.
zh: 在一次日本校外旅行中，我們班參觀了岐阜一座小型紀念館。我得承認，我對館中紀念的這位人物杉原千畝幾乎一無所知。導覽員解釋說，1940 年他是日本外交官，派駐在北歐的立陶宛。戰爭正在歐洲大陸蔓延，許多家庭都想逃離。
這些難民需要簽證才能經由日本前往他處，但他們不容易取得。每天都有越來越多人在領事館外等候。杉原多次向政府請求許可，每次得到的答覆都是不行。他和妻子以及一位同事商量後，做了一個艱難的決定。他開始一張接一張手寫簽證，在每份文件上蓋上官方印章。有些說法指出，直到火車快要開走時，他仍在寫。
要這樣做需要勇敢又有同情心的人，因為他是拿自己的職涯冒險。當這些離鄉背井、感到孤立無援的家庭把文件握在手中時，他們鬆了一口氣。官員通常會保存所簽發每一張簽證的紀錄，如今一份名單能幫助家庭了解自己的過去。導覽員說，杉原很少談起自己這項無私的舉動。
他幫助過的許多人後來在其他國家重建了生活。直到今天，他們的子孫仍記得他的名字。站在安靜的紀念館裡，我努力消化所學到的一切。不是每個人都有機會改變歷史，但他的勇氣讓我明白，一個簽名就能改變一個家庭的未來。我或許無法說服每個人都像他那樣行動，但我可以從問問自己能怎麼幫助身邊的人開始。

questions.stem: What did Sugihara do after his government refused his requests?
options: He wrote visas by hand for the refugees.
He told the refugees to go home.
He asked his wife to take his place.
questions.explain: 第二段說政府拒絕後，他開始一張接一張手寫簽證，故選 (B)。(A) 文中說到他最後搭火車離開，但那不是他在被拒絕之後的決定。
questions.evidence: He began to write visas by hand, one after another

questions.stem: The word "obtain" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: obtain 是「獲得」，they could not obtain them easily 指難民不容易拿到簽證，與 get 最接近，故選 (B)。(A) lose 是失去，語意相反。
questions.evidence: These refugees needed visas to travel through Japan, but they could not obtain them easily.

questions.stem: Why does the writer say it took a courageous person to do what Sugihara did?
options: He risked his career by going against his government's answer.
He had to travel across the sea alone.
He did not know how to write visas.
He was afraid of the refugees.
questions.explain: 文中說他在政府一再拒絕下仍簽發簽證，並提到他拿自己的職涯冒險，所以說這需要勇氣，故選 (A)。其他選項文中都沒有根據。
questions.evidence: It took a courageous and compassionate person to do that, because he risked his career.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a diplomat's brave choice helped many refugees
How to travel to Japan by train
Why governments should stop issuing visas
What a memorial hall in Gifu looks like
questions.explain: 全文講述杉原千畝違背政府指示、冒險為難民簽發簽證，並讓後人記得他的勇氣，故選 (A)。(D) 紀念館只是敘事的場景，並非重點。
questions.evidence: Not everyone has the chance to change history, but his bravery showed me that one signature can change a family's future.

vocab.stem: The club wants to ______ ten new members before the school festival starts.
vocab.explain: 社團想在校慶前招募十位新成員，recruit members 是常見搭配，故選 recruit。seize（奪取）、burst（爆裂）都不合語意。

vocab.stem: The police found out that the passport was ______, so the man could not use it to travel.
vocab.explain: 警方發現護照是假的，所以那名男子不能用它旅行，故選 fake。courageous（勇敢的）無法形容護照。

title: Behind Every Parcel
connect: 課本介紹孟買便當送餐員靠編碼與分工準確配送，這篇改看郵件處理中心如何用同樣的團隊合作把包裹送到正確地點。
paragraphs: Last month, my class visited a mail center in a [[suburb|L3-0862]] of our city. Every day, it must [[handle|T-0195]] a [[massive|L5-0526]] number of letters and parcels. Our guide told us that the whole system depends on one simple idea: every item must go to the right place, and it must get there quickly.

The process starts when trucks bring bags of mail to the center. Workers and machines [[sort|L0-0107]] the items by area. Each address has a postal [[code|L4-0153]], and a machine reads it in a moment and sends the parcel down the correct belt. Then workers [[load|L0-0215]] the parcels onto smaller trucks. These trucks are part of a [[network|L0-0048]] that reaches every town and village on the island, and a parcel can travel [[swiftly|T-0193]] from one end to the other.

I asked the guide how the center avoids mistakes. He said that [[accuracy|L4-0013]] matters as much as speed, because one wrong digit can send a gift to the wrong city. Good [[efficiency|L4-0333]] comes from careful training and from checking the machines every day. He also said that online shopping has changed the work: each [[transaction|L5-0918]] on a website turns into a parcel that someone must deliver. They are not [[merely|T-0192]] moving boxes, he added; they are keeping promises to people.

Of course, no system is [[flawless|T-0196]]. Sometimes a label is damaged, or the address is unclear. When that happens, workers search for the owner so that the parcel can be [[brought back|P-0232]] to its sender. Even so, almost every parcel arrives [[on time|P-0233]], and this is [[in large part|P-0231]] because thousands of people do their small jobs carefully. I left the center with new respect for them. [[Without a doubt|P-0234]], I will think of them the next time I click the buy button.
zh: 上個月，我們班參觀了市郊的一座郵件處理中心。每天，它得處理大量的信件與包裹。導覽員告訴我們，整套系統仰賴一個簡單的概念：每一件物品都必須送到正確的地方，而且要送得快。
流程從卡車把一袋袋郵件運到中心開始。工作人員和機器依地區把物品分類。每個地址都有郵遞區號，機器瞬間就能讀取，並把包裹送上正確的輸送帶。接著工作人員把包裹裝上較小的卡車。這些卡車是一個網絡的一部分，能通到島上每個城鎮和村落，包裹可以快速地從一端送到另一端。
我問導覽員這個中心如何避免出錯。他說準確度和速度一樣重要，因為只要錯一個數字，禮物就可能被送到錯的城市。高效率來自嚴謹的訓練，以及每天檢查機器。他還說網路購物改變了這份工作：網站上的每一筆交易都會變成一個必須有人遞送的包裹。他補充說，他們不只是搬運箱子，而是在實現對人的承諾。
當然，沒有任何系統是完美無瑕的。有時標籤破損，或地址不清楚。這時工作人員會設法找出包裹的主人，好讓包裹能被退回給寄件人。即便如此，幾乎每個包裹都準時送達，這在很大程度上是因為成千上萬的人細心做好自己的小工作。離開中心時，我對他們有了新的敬意。下次我按下購買鍵時，無疑會想起他們。

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, what does a machine do with the postal code?
options: It prints the code on a label.
It reads the code and sends the parcel down the correct belt.

questions.explain: 第二段說機器瞬間讀取郵遞區號，並把包裹送上正確輸送帶，故選 (B)。(A) 文中並沒有說機器印標籤。
questions.evidence: Each address has a postal code, and a machine reads it in a moment and sends the parcel down the correct belt.

questions.stem: The word "massive" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: massive 是「巨大的」，a massive number of letters and parcels 指數量非常龐大，故選 (B)。(A) tiny 是極小，意思相反。
questions.evidence: Every day, it must handle a massive number of letters and parcels.

questions.stem: Why does the guide say accuracy matters as much as speed?
options: Because a small mistake can send a parcel to the wrong place.
Because workers want to finish early.
questions.explain: 導覽員說只要錯一個數字，禮物就可能被送到錯的城市，所以準確和速度一樣重要，故選 (A)。(C) 文中沒有提到工作人員想提早下班。
questions.evidence: He said that accuracy matters as much as speed, because one wrong digit can send a gift to the wrong city.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a mail center and its workers get parcels to the right place
Why trucks are better than trains
How to write an address on a parcel
questions.explain: 全文介紹郵件中心如何靠分類、編碼、路線網絡與人員細心把包裹送到正確地點，故選 (B)。(A) 網路購物只是第三段順帶提到的原因。
questions.evidence: Even so, almost every parcel arrives on time, and this is in large part because thousands of people do their small jobs carefully.

vocab.stem: Many people who live in the suburbs ______ to the city by train every morning.
vocab.explain: 住在郊區的許多人每天早上搭火車「通勤」到市區，故選 commute。install（安裝）、harvest（收割）都不合語意。

vocab.stem: The school gave the student an award for ______ in science after she won the national contest.
vocab.explain: 學生在全國比賽中獲勝，學校因其科學上的卓越表現頒獎，故選 excellence。penalty（處罰）不會是獎項的理由。

title: Fairness Begins at Home
connect: 課文談冰島如何推動性別平等，這篇看一位台灣高中生從自己家裡的家事分工，發現日常生活中的不平等。
paragraphs: Mei-ling's class was asked to write about fairness at home and at work. At first she thought the topic was dull, but then she looked at her own family. Her mother works full time and still does most of the [[domestic|L0-0282]] work. Her father is kind, yet he rarely touches a [[chore|L5-0135]]. Mei-ling realized that a [[gender|L4-0437]] [[gap|L3-0352]] can exist even in a loving home.

She decided to ask her classmates what they thought. The [[majority|L3-0515]] of them said that girls were expected to clean and cook while boys were left alone. Some students laughed, but others felt it was an [[injustice|L6-0452]]. Her teacher explained that this kind of unequal treatment is a form of [[discrimination|L5-0300]], even when nobody means to be cruel.

Mei-ling then read about how people have changed their societies. In some places, women organized a [[protest|L4-0784]] and [[took to the streets|P-0237]] to ask for equal rights. Over time, laws were written to [[ban|L5-0076]] unfair hiring, and city [[councils|L4-0226]] listened more carefully. Change was never quick. It took [[tough|L3-0917]] and [[bold|L3-0085]] people many years, and they could succeed only because they lived in a [[democratic|L3-0228]] society where citizens may speak up.

After the project, Mei-ling made a simple chart for her family. Every person, young or old, picked a task for the week. At first her brother complained, but he soon admitted that the house looked better. Her parents said they should [[take small steps|P-0239]] to share the work more fairly. Mei-ling knows one chart will not solve every problem. Still, her school is doing well [[in this regard|P-0240]], and she feels proud that a small change at home began with one question.
zh: 梅玲的班上被要求寫一篇關於家裡與職場公平的作文。起初她覺得這個題目很無聊，但接著她看了看自己的家。她的母親全職工作，卻仍然做大部分的家務。父親人很好，卻很少碰任何一件雜事。梅玲發現，即使在充滿愛的家裡，也可能存在性別差距。
她決定問問同學的想法。大多數同學說，女生被期待要打掃和煮飯，而男生則可以不用管。有些同學笑了，但也有人覺得這是一種不公不義。老師解釋說，這種不平等的對待是歧視的一種，即使沒有人是存心刻薄。
梅玲接著讀到人們如何改變自己的社會。在某些地方，女性組織抗議並走上街頭，爭取平等的權利。隨著時間過去，人們制定法律來禁止不公平的聘僱，市議會也更用心傾聽。改變從來不是一蹴可幾的。這需要堅韌又大膽的人付出許多年，而且他們之所以能成功，是因為生活在公民可以發聲的民主社會。
專題結束後，梅玲為家人做了一張簡單的表。每個人無論老少，都挑一項這週的工作。起初弟弟抱怨，但他很快承認家裡變得更乾淨了。她的父母說，他們應該一步一步來，讓工作分配得更公平。梅玲知道一張表不能解決所有問題。不過，她的學校在這方面做得不錯，她也很驕傲，因為家裡這個小改變是從一個問題開始的。

questions.stem: What did Mei-ling notice about her own family?
options: Her father did all the cooking and cleaning.
Her mother worked full time but still did most of the housework.
Her brother was not allowed to help at home.
Her parents never talked about fairness.
questions.explain: 第一段說母親全職工作卻仍做大部分家務，父親很少碰雜事，故選 (B)。(A) 與文意相反，做家事的主要是母親而非父親。
questions.evidence: Her mother works full time and still does most of the domestic work.

questions.stem: The word "bold" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: bold 在此形容願意為改變挺身而出的人，意思是「大膽的、勇敢的」，與 brave 最接近，故選 (A)。careless 是「粗心的」，不符文意。
questions.evidence: It took tough and bold people many years, and they could succeed only because they lived in a democratic society where citizens may speak up.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about changes in equal rights from paragraph 3?
options: They were easy for everyone to accept.
They needed a long time and a lot of courage.
They were only needed in one country.
questions.explain: 第三段說改變從不快速，需要堅韌又大膽的人努力多年，可推知平權改變需要時間與勇氣，故選 (C)。(A) 與 never quick 互相矛盾。
questions.evidence: Change was never quick.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a student found unfairness at home and tried to improve it
Why laws about hiring are too strict
How brothers and sisters can compete at school
Why housework is boring for most teenagers
questions.explain: 全文從梅玲發現家中家事分配不均，到調查同學、閱讀歷史，最後做出家事表，主軸是她發現不公平並嘗試改善，故選 (A)。(D) 只是文章的背景，並非重點。
questions.evidence: Mei-ling realized that a gender gap can exist even in a loving home.

vocab.stem: Everyone in the house must share the ______, such as washing the dishes and taking out the trash.
vocab.explain: 洗碗、倒垃圾屬於日常「雜事」，故選 chore。gap（差距）、council（議會）、ban（禁令）都不能接在 share the 後面表示這些工作。

vocab.stem: The ______ of voters supported the new park, so the city decided to build it.
vocab.explain: 支持的選民是「大多數」，所以市府決定興建，故選 majority。injustice（不公不義）與 chaos（混亂）都不合語意。

title: When Visitors Crowd the Town
connect: 課文談巴塞隆納的過度觀光，這篇換成一位台灣學生陪外婆回到山城，看見遊客太多對居民生活的影響。
paragraphs: Last spring, Hsin-yi took a bus with her grandmother to a small mountain town known for its old tea houses and lantern-lit stairs. They had visited when Hsin-yi was little, and her grandmother remembered a quiet place. This time, visitors [[flocked|L3-0329]] to the town in huge numbers. The [[narrow|T-0199]] stairs were so full that it took them twenty minutes to walk one short street.

Hsin-yi talked with a woman who sold vegetables near the market. The woman said the town had changed [[dramatically|T-0200]] in ten years. Many tourists took photos in front of people's doors and were [[thoughtless|T-0201]] about noise at night. Some local families were [[fed up with|P-0243]] the crowds, and the number of [[complaints|L3-0177]] to the town office kept rising. The problem became bad [[to such an extent that|P-0242]] some residents stopped going downtown on weekends.

Housing was another worry. A [[landlord|L5-0498]] can earn more by letting a flat to tourists for a few nights than by finding a long-term [[tenant|L6-0911]]. So many families could no longer afford to [[rent|T-0202]] a home in their own neighborhood, and the number of local residents began to [[decline|L5-0261]]. Hsin-yi realized that the tourism boom was good for some people but had a [[negative|T-0203]] effect on others.

Before leaving, Hsin-yi read a notice about new [[measures|L4-0621]]. The town was limiting the number of tour groups on busy days and asking visitors to be quiet after dark. For her, the best [[option|L4-0692]] was simple: travel in a small group and visit on a weekday. She also decided to [[strive|L4-0920]] to be a respectful guest by buying from local shops and keeping her voice low. 'The place in question is not a theme park,' she wrote in her journal. 'It is somebody's home.'
zh: 去年春天，欣怡陪外婆搭公車前往一座以老茶樓和點著燈籠的階梯聞名的山城。她們在欣怡小時候來過，外婆記得那是個安靜的地方。這一次，遊客大批湧向這座小鎮。狹窄的階梯擠得滿滿的，她們走一條短短的街竟花了二十分鐘。
欣怡和一位在市場附近賣菜的婦人聊天。婦人說，這座小鎮十年來變化極大。許多遊客在別人家門前拍照，夜裡也不顧慮噪音。有些當地家庭已受夠了人潮，向鎮公所提出的投訴也不斷增加。情況糟到一個地步，有些居民週末都不再去市區。
住房是另一個擔憂。房東把房子短租給遊客幾晚，賺的錢可能比找長期房客還多。於是許多家庭已負擔不起在自己社區租房子，當地居民的人數也開始減少。欣怡明白，觀光熱潮對有些人是好事，對另一些人卻有負面的影響。
離開前，欣怡讀到一張關於新措施的公告。小鎮在尖峰日限制旅行團的數量，並要求遊客天黑後保持安靜。對她來說，最好的選擇很簡單：小團體出遊，並選平日前往。她也決心努力當個有禮貌的客人，向在地商店購買東西，並壓低說話的音量。她在日記裡寫道：「這裡不是主題樂園，而是別人的家。」

questions.stem: Why did the walk along one short street take so long?
options: The narrow stairs were full of visitors.
They got lost in the market.
questions.explain: 第一段說狹窄的階梯擠滿遊客，所以走一條短街要二十分鐘，故選 (C)。(B) 文中並未提到外婆走得慢，是把原因錯推到人物身上。
questions.evidence: The narrow stairs were so full that it took them twenty minutes to walk one short street.

questions.stem: Why might a landlord choose to rent a flat to tourists?
options: Tourists can bring in more money in a short time.
Tourists take better care of the flat.
Local families refuse to rent any home.
The town office asks landlords to do so.
questions.explain: 第三段指出把房子短租給遊客幾晚，賺的可能比長期房客多，故選 (A)。文中沒說遊客較愛惜房子，(B) 是無中生有。
questions.evidence: A landlord can earn more by letting a flat to tourists for a few nights than by finding a long-term tenant.

questions.stem: The word "thoughtless" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: thoughtless 指「不為他人著想的」，文中遊客對別人家門前與夜間噪音毫不顧慮，與 careless about others 最接近，故選 (B)。
questions.evidence: Many tourists took photos in front of people's doors and were thoughtless about noise at night.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to find the cheapest hotel in a mountain town
Why a quiet town became a hard place to live in because of too many visitors
How tea houses make their drinks
Why grandmothers like to travel by bus
questions.explain: 全文以山城為例，說明遊客過多造成噪音、房價與居民減少等問題，故選 (B)。(A) 與住宿價格無關，文中沒有討論旅館。
questions.evidence: Hsin-yi realized that the tourism boom was good for some people but had a negative effect on others.

vocab.stem: Many students cannot afford to ______ an apartment near the university.
vocab.explain: 學生負擔不起「租」大學附近的公寓，故選 rent。decline（下降）與 flock（群聚）都無法直接接受詞 an apartment。

vocab.stem: The company took new safety ______ after the accident to protect its workers.
vocab.explain: 意外後公司採取新的安全「措施」，take measures 是常見搭配，故選 measures。tenants 與 landlords 是房客與房東，不能被「採取」。

title: The Mock Trial
connect: 課文介紹小說中律師為弱勢者挺身而出，這篇看一位高中生參加模擬法庭社，親身體會證據、陪審團與公平的意義。
paragraphs: Wen-hao joined the mock trial club at his school because he wanted to practice speaking. In the first meeting, the teacher gave the club a made-up case. A boy was [[accused|L4-0014]] of breaking a classmate's science project, but he said he had not done it. Wen-hao was [[appointed|L4-0049]] to defend the boy. He had never felt so nervous. All week he had practiced his opening lines in front of the mirror, but now his mind went blank for a few long seconds.

Eight students played the [[jury|L5-0494]]. Wen-hao carefully compared each [[version|L5-0963]] of the story told by the witnesses and found two small mistakes. [[Meanwhile|L3-0526]], the lawyer for the other side gave an emotional speech, trying to [[sway|L4-0931]] the jurors with their feelings instead of the facts. Wen-hao's heart beat fast.

Wen-hao stood up and spoke slowly. He asked the jurors to be [[sensible|L3-0777]] and to think about proof, not rumors. 'Anyone can say something about another person,' he said, 'but a fair decision must rest on evidence.' He tried to [[stand up for|P-0246]] the boy even though some classmates already thought he was guilty. When he finished, his hands were shaking, but he [[held his head up|P-0247]].

The [[verdict|L5-0962]] was not guilty, and the club cheered. But Wen-hao learned that winning a [[victory|T-0206]] was not the most important part. Some students offered [[criticism|L4-0238]], saying he should have looked at the jurors more. He [[definitely|T-0207]] agreed and wrote it down. Their teacher, who [[had high hopes|P-0250]] for the club, said that a good lawyer needs a strong [[moral|L3-0552]] sense, not just clever words. That night his mother brought him some warm soup, a small [[comfort|L3-0170]] after a tiring day.
zh: 文浩加入了學校的模擬法庭社，因為他想練習表達。第一次聚會，老師給社團一個虛構的案件。一名男孩被指控弄壞同學的科學作品，但他說自己沒有做。文浩被指派為這名男孩辯護，他從沒這麼緊張過。他整個星期都對著鏡子練習開場白，但此刻腦中卻有好幾秒鐘一片空白。
八位同學扮演陪審團。文浩仔細比較目擊者所說的每一個版本，找出兩處小錯誤。同時，對方的律師發表了一場很動人的演說，試圖用感情而不是事實來影響陪審員。文浩的心跳得很快。
文浩站起來，慢慢地說話。他請陪審員明智一點，要想想證據，而不是謠言。他說：「任何人都可以對別人說三道四，但公平的決定必須建立在證據上。」即使有些同學已經認為那個男孩有罪，他還是努力為他挺身而出。說完時，他的雙手在發抖，但他仍然昂首挺胸。
判決是無罪，社員們歡呼起來。但文浩明白，贏得勝利並不是最重要的部分。有些同學給了批評，說他應該多看看陪審員。他完全同意，並把它寫下來。老師對這個社團抱著很高的期望，她說一位好律師需要有強烈的道德感，而不只是巧妙的言詞。那天晚上，媽媽端來一碗熱湯，讓疲累的一天多了一點安慰。

options: Telling a lie to his teacher
questions.explain: 第一段說男孩被指控弄壞同學的科學作品，故選 (B)。他是否說謊並非案件內容，(A) 是無中生有。
questions.evidence: A boy was accused of breaking a classmate's science project, but he said he had not done it.

questions.stem: The word "sway" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: sway 在此指「影響、左右」，對方律師想用感情而非事實影響陪審員的看法，與 influence 最接近，故選 (B)。confuse 是「使困惑」，文中重點是影響判斷。
questions.evidence: Meanwhile, the lawyer for the other side gave an emotional speech, trying to sway the jurors with their feelings instead of the facts.

questions.stem: Why did Wen-hao ask the jurors to think about proof, not rumors?
options: He wanted them to finish quickly.
He believed a fair decision should be based on evidence.
He was afraid of the other lawyer.
He thought the boy was guilty.
questions.explain: 文浩說公平的決定必須建立在證據上，所以請陪審員重視證據而非謠言，故選 (B)。(D) 與他為男孩辯護的立場相反。
questions.evidence: He asked the jurors to be sensible and to think about proof, not rumors.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a student learned about fairness and courage through a mock trial
How to become a famous lawyer in Taiwan
How a jury chooses the best speaker
questions.explain: 全文講文浩在模擬法庭中為被指控的人辯護，並學到證據、公平與勇氣的意義，故選 (A)。(C) 科學作品只是案件背景。
questions.evidence: But Wen-hao learned that winning a victory was not the most important part.

vocab.stem: The ______ listened carefully to both sides before it made its decision.
vocab.explain: 聽取雙方說法後做決定的是「陪審團」，故選 jury。verdict 是判決結果，不能「聆聽」。

vocab.stem: The court is expected to announce its ______ tomorrow morning.
vocab.explain: 法庭宣布的是「判決」，故選 verdict。victory（勝利）、criticism（批評）都不是法庭宣布的內容。

title: A Week on a Flower Farm
connect: 課文介紹法國香水之都格拉斯，這篇換成台灣南部的花田，看一位高中生如何認識香氣背後的人與工作。
paragraphs: Yu-ting's aunt owns a small flower farm in southern Taiwan. Last summer Yu-ting helped there for a week. She had always thought of [[perfume|L4-0724]] as something made in big factories, but her aunt showed her a different side. The sweet [[scent|L5-0757]] of jasmine filled the whole field at sunrise, and the flowers had to be picked early.

The farm was in an [[ideal|L0-0171]] place for growing flowers. The soil was [[fertile|L4-0396]], the sun was strong, and there was enough rain. Her aunt explained that the weather in the area was [[more or less|P-0251]] the same for most of the year, so flowers could be grown for many months. She also said the farm had a good [[reputation|L4-0835]], and it sold flowers to [[professional|L4-0772]] makers of soap and tea.

The most [[remarkable|L4-0830]] part of the week was a visit to a [[specialized|T-0211]] workshop. A [[talented|T-0212]] young man there could [[identify|L4-0502]] dozens of smells with his eyes closed. He explained that being [[precise|L4-0754]] matters, because one extra drop can change a whole mixture. To make a small bottle of flower oil, workers [[soaked|L5-0801]] the petals in a liquid for hours. Yu-ting tried it and found it harder than it looked.

On the last morning, Yu-ting smelled a soft flower by the road [[by chance|P-0254]]. The scent made many happy memories [[come to mind|P-0252]]: her grandmother's garden, rainy afternoons, even her first school trip. She realized that a smell can carry feelings as strongly as a photograph. Back at home, she wrote in her notebook that every bottle of perfume starts as a field, and that behind it stand people who work with patience.
zh: 郁婷的阿姨在台灣南部有一座小花田。去年夏天，郁婷去那裡幫忙了一個星期。她一向以為香水是大工廠做出來的，但阿姨讓她看到不一樣的一面。日出時，茉莉花甜美的香氣瀰漫整片田野，花必須一早就採下來。
這座農場位在非常適合種花的地方。土壤肥沃，陽光強烈，雨水也充足。阿姨解釋，這一帶的天氣一年中大致上差不多，所以花可以種上好幾個月。她還說，這座農場名聲不錯，會把花賣給專業的香皂與茶品製造商。
這一週最了不起的部分，是參觀一間專門的工坊。那裡一位有才華的年輕人閉著眼睛就能辨認出幾十種氣味。他解釋說精確很重要，因為多一滴就可能改變整份混合物。要做出一小瓶花油，工人會把花瓣浸泡在液體裡好幾個小時。郁婷試著做做看，發現比看起來難多了。
最後一天早上，郁婷碰巧在路邊聞到一朵柔和的花香。這個香氣讓許多快樂的回憶浮現腦海：外婆的花園、下雨的午後，甚至是她第一次的校外旅行。她明白，氣味傳達感情的力量不輸給一張照片。回到家後，她在筆記本裡寫下：每一瓶香水都是從一片花田開始，而背後站著的是耐心工作的人。

questions.stem: Why was the farm in an ideal place for growing flowers?
options: It was close to a big factory.
It had good soil, strong sun and enough rain.
It was next to a busy road.
It had cold weather all year.
questions.explain: 第二段列出土壤肥沃、陽光強烈、雨水充足，這些就是適合種花的條件，故選 (B)。(D) 與「天氣一年中大致相同、可種好幾個月」不符。
questions.evidence: The soil was fertile, the sun was strong, and there was enough rain.

questions.stem: The word "precise" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: precise 是「精確的」，因為多一滴就會改變混合物，所以需要精準，與 exact 最接近，故選 (A)。
questions.evidence: He explained that being precise matters, because one extra drop can change a whole mixture.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the young man in the workshop?
options: He was new to the job.
He had a very good sense of smell and much practice.
questions.explain: 他能閉著眼睛分辨幾十種氣味，可推知他嗅覺靈敏又經驗豐富，故選 (B)。(A) 與 talented 的描述相反。
questions.evidence: A talented young man there could identify dozens of smells with his eyes closed.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to start a flower shop
How a student learned that perfume comes from flowers and the people who work with them
Why southern Taiwan gets a lot of rain
How to take good photographs of flowers
questions.explain: 全文描述郁婷在花田的一週，認識香水從花田到工坊背後的人與工作，故選 (B)。(C) 下雨只是環境條件之一。
questions.evidence: Back at home, she wrote in her notebook that every bottle of perfume starts as a field, and that behind it stand people who work with patience.

vocab.stem: Can you ______ the bird by looking at its bright blue feathers?
vocab.explain: 看羽毛辨認出是哪一種鳥，故選 identify。soak（浸泡）與 rent（租）不能用來辨認鳥。

vocab.stem: The restaurant has a good ______ for serving fresh food.
vocab.explain: 餐廳以供應新鮮食物而有好「名聲」，故選 reputation。scent（氣味）無法接 for serving fresh food 表示名聲。

title: Who Is Watching Me Online?
connect: 課文提醒網路世界的隱私與操弄風險，這篇看一位高中生發現帳號異常後，做調查學習保護自己。
paragraphs: Kai-wen spends hours online. He chats with friends in a [[virtual|L5-0973]] world, [[browses|L5-0106]] videos [[to his heart's content|P-0257]], and shops for game items. One evening, when he tried to [[log in|P-0259]] to his [[account|L0-0127]], he saw a message saying that someone had tried to use his password from another country. It was the first time he had thought about how much of his life was stored on a screen.

Kai-wen's older sister, who studies computers, told him to be careful. She explained that a data [[leak|L3-0481]] happens when a company fails to keep private information safe. If your password [[falls into the wrong hands|P-0258]], strangers can pretend to be you and read your messages. Kai-wen felt his face turn pale.

To understand more, Kai-wen did a small [[survey|L3-0872]] in his class. Most [[participants|L5-0602]] admitted that they used the same password for many sites. After a short [[analysis|L4-0038]], he found that students who changed their passwords often felt safer. He also learned that [[advertisers|T-0214]] collect information about what people click so they can show ads that fit each [[personality|L0-0147]]. Companies that [[violate|L4-0981]] users' privacy can be punished by law in many places.

[[Ultimately|T-0216]], Kai-wen decided that technology is neither good nor bad; what matters is how we use it. He now uses a different password for each site, helped two friends set up stronger ones, and turns on a second check when he signs in. His sister reminds him to [[watch out|P-0256]] for strange links. He also learned that some apps try to steer users toward certain choices, a kind of [[manipulation|T-0213]]. 'The more you know,' he says, 'the better you can protect yourself.'
zh: 凱文花很多時間上網。他在虛擬世界裡和朋友聊天，盡情地瀏覽影片，也買遊戲道具。有天晚上，他想登入自己的帳戶時，看到一則訊息，說有人試著從另一個國家使用他的密碼。這是他第一次想到，自己生活中有多少東西都存放在螢幕裡。
凱文就讀電腦相關科系的姊姊要他小心。她解釋，資料外洩是指公司沒能好好保護私人資訊。如果你的密碼落入壞人手中，陌生人就能假冒你，還可以讀你的訊息。凱文覺得自己臉色發白。
為了更了解這件事，凱文在班上做了一個小調查。大多數參與者都承認，他們在很多網站用同一組密碼。經過簡短的分析，他發現經常換密碼的同學覺得比較安全。他還知道，廣告商會蒐集人們點擊了什麼，好顯示適合每個人個性的廣告。侵犯用戶隱私的公司，在許多地方會受到法律的處罰。
最後，凱文認為科技本身沒有好壞，重要的是我們如何使用。他現在每個網站都用不同的密碼，還幫兩位朋友設了更安全的密碼，登入時也開啟第二道驗證。姊姊提醒他要小心奇怪的連結。他也學到，有些應用程式會設法把使用者引導到特定選擇，這是一種操弄。他說：「你知道得越多，就越能保護自己。」

questions.stem: What did Kai-wen see when he tried to log in to his account?
options: A message about someone using his password from another country
An ad for a new video game
questions.explain: 第一段說他登入時看到訊息，說有人試著從另一個國家使用他的密碼，故選 (A)。(B) 廣告在文中是講廣告商蒐集資料，與登入訊息無關。
questions.evidence: One evening, when he tried to log in to his account, he saw a message saying that someone had tried to use his password from another country.

questions.stem: The word "violate" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: violate 是「違反、侵犯」，侵犯用戶隱私的公司會被處罰，與 break（違反）最接近，故選 (A)。protect 意思正好相反。
questions.evidence: Companies that violate users' privacy can be punished by law in many places.

questions.stem: Why do advertisers collect information about what people click?
options: To teach people how to use computers
To show ads that fit each person
questions.explain: 第三段說廣告商蒐集點擊資訊，是為了顯示符合每個人個性的廣告，故選 (B)。(C) leak 是資料外洩，廣告商蒐集資料並非為了修補。
questions.evidence: He also learned that advertisers collect information about what people click so they can show ads that fit each personality.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a student learned why online privacy matters and how to protect himself
questions.explain: 全文從帳號異常談起，凱文做調查並學到保護隱私的方法，主旨是網路隱私與自我保護，故選 (B)。
questions.evidence: Kai-wen decided that technology is neither good nor bad; what matters is how we use it.

vocab.stem: The school ran a ______ to find out which lunch menu students liked best.
vocab.explain: 為了知道學生最喜歡哪種菜單而進行的是「調查」，故選 survey。leak（外洩）、account（帳戶）都不合語意。

vocab.stem: She forgot the password to her email ______ and could not read her messages.
vocab.explain: 忘記電子郵件「帳戶」的密碼，所以讀不到信，故選 account。其餘三個字都是人或特質，不能接在 email 後面。

title: My First Fun Run
connect: 課文談馬拉松的歷史與魅力，這篇看一位不愛運動的男孩如何訓練、飲食並完成人生第一場路跑。
paragraphs: Ming-han was not a sporty boy. He liked video games more than football. But after a health check showed that he needed to [[keep in shape|P-0263]], his uncle suggested a five-kilometer fun run in their city. Ming-han laughed at first, then decided to [[sign up|P-0266]] because his best friend promised to run with him. Soon he was reading everything he could about running.

The training plan was simple. Three days a week, they ran slowly, then a little farther each time. Ming-han learned that building [[endurance|L6-0304]] takes patience, and that rest days matter as much as running days. His uncle also taught him about food. Rice and noodles are rich in [[carbohydrate|T-0218]], which gives the body energy, while eggs, beans and fish supply [[protein|L4-0783]] to repair muscles. Before a long run, he should avoid [[greasy|L4-0463]] food, because it is harder to [[digest|L4-0284]]. He also learned to stay [[hydrated|T-0219]] by drinking small amounts of water through the day.

The night before the race, Ming-han almost [[got cold feet|P-0265]]. He felt so much [[stress|L0-0081]] that he could hardly eat dinner. His friend reminded him that their only real [[competitor|L4-0167]] was the person they had been last month. That thought gave him some [[confidence|L4-0180]].

On race morning, the [[atmosphere|L4-0071]] was cheerful, with music and children giving out cups of water. Ming-han did not run fast, but he crossed the finish line with a big smile. He did not become a [[legend|L4-0586]], of course, but he had proved something to himself. Now he wants to [[go the extra mile|P-0261]] and try a ten-kilometer race next year. His friends joke that he is now [[addicted|T-0217]] to running.
zh: 明翰不是個愛運動的男孩。比起足球，他更喜歡電動遊戲。但是一次健康檢查顯示他需要保持體態後，叔叔建議他參加城裡的五公里趣味路跑。明翰起初笑了笑，後來因為最好的朋友答應陪他一起跑，就決定報名。不久他就開始盡可能閱讀所有關於跑步的資料。
訓練計畫很簡單。每週三天，他們慢慢跑，然後每次多跑一點。明翰學到，培養耐力需要耐心，而且休息日和跑步日一樣重要。叔叔也教他飲食的知識。米飯和麵條富含碳水化合物，能給身體能量；蛋、豆類和魚則提供蛋白質，幫助修復肌肉。長跑之前應該避免油膩的食物，因為比較難消化。他也學會一整天少量多次喝水，保持水分充足。
比賽前一晚，明翰差點臨陣退縮。他的壓力大到幾乎吃不下晚餐。朋友提醒他，他們真正的對手只有上個月的自己。這個想法讓他多了一些信心。
比賽當天早上，現場氣氛很歡樂，有音樂，還有小朋友發水。明翰跑得不快，卻帶著大大的笑容跨過終點線。他當然沒有成為傳奇，但他向自己證明了一件事。現在他想多下功夫，明年試試十公里的比賽。朋友們開玩笑說，他現在迷上跑步了。

questions.stem: Why did Ming-han decide to sign up for the fun run?
options: His best friend promised to run with him.
He wanted to win a prize.
His uncle was one of the runners.
questions.explain: 第一段說他起初笑了笑，後來因為最好的朋友答應一起跑才決定報名，故選 (B)。(D) 叔叔只是提出建議，並未說他也參加。
questions.evidence: Ming-han laughed at first, then decided to sign up because his best friend promised to run with him.

questions.stem: The word "hydrated" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: having enough water in the body
questions.explain: hydrated 指「水分充足的」，文中說他透過一整天少量喝水來維持，故選 (A)。
questions.evidence: He also learned to stay hydrated by drinking small amounts of water through the day.

questions.stem: Why should a runner avoid greasy food before a long run?
options: It makes people drink more water.
questions.explain: 第二段說油膩食物比較難消化，所以長跑前應避免，故選 (A)。(B) 蛋白質是蛋、豆與魚提供的，不是油膩食物的問題。
questions.evidence: Before a long run, he should avoid greasy food, because it is harder to digest.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a boy who disliked sports trained for and finished his first fun run
Why football is better than running
How to cook healthy meals for a school trip
questions.explain: 全文從明翰報名、訓練與飲食、賽前緊張，到完成路跑，主旨是他完成第一場路跑的歷程，故選 (A)。(D) 文中沒有提到十公里比賽的勝者。
questions.evidence: Ming-han did not run fast, but he crossed the finish line with a big smile.

vocab.stem: Long-distance swimmers need great ______ to keep going for hours.
vocab.explain: 長泳選手要持續好幾個小時，需要很強的「耐力」，故選 endurance。atmosphere（氣氛）與 legend（傳說）都不合語意。

vocab.stem: After practicing the speech many times, she spoke with great ______.
vocab.explain: 練習多次後帶著很大的「信心」演講，故選 confidence。stress（壓力）與 chaos（混亂）不會是練習後的結果。

title: The Choice I Wrote About
connect: 課文談一首關於岔路與選擇的詩，這篇看一位台灣高中生怎麼把自己的一次選擇寫成作文，並理解選擇的意義。
paragraphs: Last spring, my English teacher gave us a [[plain|T-0221]] but difficult assignment: write about a choice that changed you. I thought it would be easy until I realized that my life did not seem [[outstanding|L4-0699]] enough for an essay. I had only chosen which club to join. To help us, she read a short poem by a [[renowned|L6-0754]] American poet about a traveler who stands in front of two paths in a forest. Some readers see it as a story about bravely taking the road few people walk. Others say the two paths were almost the same, and that the traveler simply told the story that way later.

That evening I asked my grandfather for advice. He has been a farmer, a bus driver, and a noodle cook, so people from every [[walk of life|P-0269]] stop to chat with him. He smiled and said that [[indecision|T-0223]] usually [[stems from|P-0271]] the fear of losing the road we do not take. "But no one can walk both," he said. "Afterward, we often [[justify|L5-0495]] our choice to ourselves with a good story."

So I wrote about the day I picked the erhu over the piano. Most of my classmates thought it was an [[unconventional|T-0225]] decision, and my first lessons were, honestly, a little painful. But my music teacher helped me [[compose|L4-0169]] a tiny piece for my grandfather's birthday, and I met students from other grades whom I would never have [[encountered|L4-0346]] otherwise. I also learned that a [[complicated|T-0220]] feeling can sit inside a simple choice: pride, worry, and curiosity all at the same time.

When I handed in the essay, I was not sure it was good. Two weeks later, my teacher returned it with one short [[comment|L4-0159]]: it had [[struck a chord|P-0273]] with her. She also wrote that the [[essence|L5-0345]] of a choice is not the road itself, but the way we keep walking afterward. I cannot know if the piano would have been better, and I no longer need to know. What I have is a [[compelling|T-0224]] story of my own, and I plan to keep telling it honestly.
zh: 去年春天，我的英文老師出了一份看似樸素卻很難的作業：寫一個改變過你的選擇。我本來以為很容易，直到發現自己的生活似乎沒有精采到可以寫成一篇作文。我只不過選過要加入哪個社團而已。為了幫助我們，她朗讀了一首由著名美國詩人寫的短詩，內容是一位旅人站在森林裡的兩條小徑前。有些讀者把它看成一個勇敢走上少有人走的路的故事；也有人說，那兩條路其實幾乎一樣，是旅人事後才把故事那樣說的。
那天晚上我向爺爺請教。他當過農夫、公車司機，也賣過麵，所以各行各業的人都喜歡停下來跟他聊天。他笑著說，猶豫不決通常源自害怕失去沒走的那條路。「可是沒有人能同時走兩條路，」他說，「事後我們常常用一個好故事來向自己證明當初的選擇是對的。」
於是我寫了自己選擇二胡而不選鋼琴的那一天。大多數同學都覺得這是個不尋常的決定，而我最初幾堂課說實話有點痛苦。但音樂老師幫我為爺爺的生日寫了一小段曲子，我也認識了其他年級的同學，要不是這個選擇，我絕不會遇到他們。我還學到，一個簡單的選擇裡可以藏著複雜的感受：驕傲、擔心和好奇同時存在。
交出作文時，我不確定寫得好不好。兩週後，老師把作文還給我，上面只有一句簡短的評語：這篇讓她很有共鳴。她還寫道，選擇的本質不在於路本身，而在於我們事後怎麼繼續走下去。我沒辦法知道選鋼琴會不會更好，而我也不再需要知道。我擁有的是一個屬於自己、引人入勝的故事，我打算誠實地一直說下去。

options: She did not know any famous poems.
She felt her life was not special enough to write about.
She had never chosen between two clubs.
She was afraid of reading in front of the class.

questions.stem: What can we infer from the two different readings of the poem?
options: Everyone agreed on what the poem means.
The poem was too short to discuss.
The poem can be understood in more than one way.
The teacher did not like the poem.
questions.explain: 有人覺得詩在讚美勇敢選少人走的路，也有人認為兩條路幾乎一樣，可見這首詩可以有不同解讀，故選 (C)。兩種讀法並存，所以 (A) 大家看法一致不合。

questions.stem: The phrase "stems from" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: stem from 是「源自、起因於」，爺爺說猶豫不決起因於害怕失去另一條路，與 comes from 最接近，故選 (A)。(D) happens before 只說時間先後，沒有「原因」的意思。

Why poems are harder to read than essays
How a grandfather became a famous cook
How a student came to see that a choice matters through what we do after it

vocab.stem: Her ______ performance in the final game made her the best player of the year.
vocab.explain: 「傑出的表現」讓她成為年度最佳球員，outstanding 最通順，故選 (C)。solitary（孤獨的）、plain（樸素的）、complicated（複雜的）都不能形容一場使她奪得榮譽的表現。

title: The Lunch Tray Rumor
connect: 課文談假新聞的定義與破解方法，這篇看一個高中新聞社如何一步步查證班級群組裡流傳的一張照片。
paragraphs: One Monday morning, a photo went around our class chat. It showed a tray of fried insects, and the message said that our school cafeteria would serve them from next week. Some students felt a wave of [[panic|L3-0609]]. Our school newspaper club decided to [[verify|T-0230]] the story. Our advisor, Mr. Chen, once worked as a reporter and now teaches [[journalism|L5-0490]] after school. He asked us a simple question first: how would you [[define|T-0226]] fake news? We realized it is not only a false story. A real photo can also be [[misleading|T-0227]] when it is used in the wrong way.

We began with the source. The photo had no name, no date, and no place. Using an image search tool, we found that [[prior to|P-0274]] the rumor, the same picture had appeared on a travel page about a street food festival in another country. It is easy to [[mistake|P-0276]] a festival snack for a school lunch when nobody tells you where the picture was taken. Whoever started the rumor had either made a careless error or wanted to [[deceive|L5-0258]] us.

Next, we checked what the school had really planned. The cafeteria manager showed us the monthly menu, which was made weeks ago, and there were no insects on it. We also had to [[evaluate|L4-0363]] the message itself. It was written in a hurry, and it asked everyone to "share it now." That kind of message is usually [[flawed|T-0228]] from the start, because honest writers give readers time to think. After an [[extensive|L5-0370]] search, we were sure. In the [[subsequent|L5-0861]] days, we posted our findings on the club page, and the rumor slowly disappeared.

At the end of our article, we gave readers a short checklist. First, ask who wrote it and whether the writer has [[credibility|L5-0241]]. Second, look for a date and a place. Third, search for the same story in other places. Last but not least, wait before you share. Many people [[fall for|P-0278]] stories like this because they are surprising, and surprising things feel important. We hope our small [[attempt|L0-0120]] will help our classmates stop and think before they press the button.
zh: 某個星期一早上，一張照片在我們班的群組裡傳開。照片裡是一盤炸昆蟲，訊息說我們學校的餐廳從下週起要供應這種餐點。有些同學感到一陣恐慌。我們學校的新聞社決定查證這件事。社團指導老師陳老師以前當過記者，現在課後教新聞學。他先問了我們一個簡單的問題：你們會怎麼為假新聞下定義？我們發現假新聞不只是假的故事，一張真的照片如果用錯方式，同樣會誤導人。
我們從來源開始查。這張照片沒有名字、沒有日期，也沒有地點。我們用圖片搜尋工具發現，在謠言出現之前，同一張照片就曾出現在一個介紹外國街頭美食節的旅遊頁面上。如果沒人告訴你照片是在哪裡拍的，很容易把節慶小吃誤認成學校午餐。散布謠言的人不是犯了粗心的錯誤，就是想欺騙我們。
接著，我們查了學校實際的規劃。餐廳經理給我們看好幾週前就訂好的月菜單，上面完全沒有昆蟲。我們也必須評估訊息本身。它寫得很倉促，還要求大家「現在就分享」。這種訊息通常從一開始就有缺陷，因為誠實的作者會給讀者思考的時間。經過廣泛搜尋後，我們確定了。在隨後幾天，我們把查證結果貼在社團頁面上，謠言慢慢就消失了。
在文章最後，我們給讀者一份簡短的檢查清單。第一，問問是誰寫的，這個作者有沒有可信度。第二，找找有沒有日期和地點。第三，到其他地方搜尋同一則消息。最後但同樣重要的是，分享之前先等一等。很多人會被這類消息騙，是因為它們令人驚訝，而令人驚訝的事感覺很重要。我們希望這小小的嘗試能幫助同學在按下按鈕之前先停下來想一想。

questions.stem: What can we infer about the message that asked everyone to "share it now"?

It was sent by the cafeteria manager.
