How a reporter became a teacher
Why travel pages often have wrong pictures
questions.explain: 全文描述新聞社如何查證照片、確認菜單，並提出檢查清單，主旨是查證謠言與避免假新聞的方法，故選 (B)。(D) 旅遊頁面只是來源之一，並不是說它們常常放錯照片。
questions.evidence: At the end of our article, we gave readers a short checklist.

vocab.stem: Before you share a story online, try to ______ where it came from.
vocab.explain: 分享網路消息前，要「查證」它的來源，verify 最通順，故選 (A)。deceive（欺騙）、panic（恐慌）、define（定義）都不符合「確認消息出處」的語意。

vocab.stem: The company hired a new writer because it wanted a more ______ report on the problem.
vocab.explain: 公司想要對問題做「更廣泛」的報告，extensive 最合，故選 (B)。misleading（誤導的）與 flawed（有缺陷的）是負面說法，公司不會刻意想要；subsequent（隨後的）則不能這樣形容報告的內容。

title: Two Days with My Cousin
connect: 課文介紹「福爾摩沙」之名與台灣多樣的地形與風貌，這篇看一位高中生帶加拿大表妹從城市走到山村，感受同一座島的兩種樣貌。
paragraphs: Last July, my cousin Emma flew in from Canada for her first visit to Taiwan. Before she came, she told me that she knew one thing about the island: long ago, [[sailors|T-0231]] from Europe had called it Formosa, which means "beautiful." I wanted to show her that the name still fit.

We started in Taipei. The streets were [[bustling|T-0237]] with scooters, bus riders, and people carrying bubble tea. The city is [[densely|T-0233]] populated, and Emma held her bag tightly as we walked through the night market. "Is it always this crowded?" she asked. I laughed and said that this was a quiet evening. She tried stinky tofu, made a face, and then asked for a second piece.

The next morning we took a bus to a small mountain village in Nantou. A large part of Taiwan is [[mountainous|L4-0655]], and as the road climbed, the buildings disappeared and the air became cool. Around us, [[majestic|L6-0538]] peaks stood behind one another, and a few black kites [[soar|L5-0802]]ed high above a deep [[valley|T-0234]]. We stopped at a clear [[stream|T-0235]], and Emma put her hands in the cold water. Tea fields covered the hills like green steps, and the forests were thick and [[lush|L6-0533]]. "This is [[gorgeous|L5-0412]]," she whispered.

That night, we sat on the farmhouse porch and [[took a look at|P-0279]] the stars. Emma said the city and the village [[were worlds apart|P-0280]], and I agreed. [[By contrast|P-0281]], her hometown looks about the same wherever you go. Yet it takes only a few hours to travel from one world to the other here. Hikers come [[from far and wide|P-0283]] to enjoy these mountains, and I think I understand why. The island is small, but its scenery can change [[considerably|T-0232]] in one day. Emma called it an [[exceptional|L5-0354]] place, and for the first time I saw my home through her eyes.
zh: 去年七月，我的表妹艾瑪從加拿大飛來，第一次造訪台灣。她來之前告訴我，關於這座島她只知道一件事：很久以前，歐洲的水手稱它為福爾摩沙，意思是「美麗」。我想讓她看到，這個名字至今仍然名副其實。
我們從台北開始。街上滿是熙熙攘攘的機車、搭公車的人，還有提著珍珠奶茶的路人。這座城市人口稠密，我們走過夜市時，艾瑪緊緊抓著她的包包。「這裡一直都這麼擠嗎？」她問。我笑著說，今晚算是安靜的了。她試吃了臭豆腐，皺了皺臉，然後又要了第二塊。
隔天早上，我們搭巴士前往南投的一個小山村。台灣有很大一部分是山地，隨著道路往上爬，建築物消失了，空氣也變涼。四周雄偉的山峰一座接著一座，幾隻黑鳶在深谷上方高高盤旋。我們在一條清澈的小溪旁停下，艾瑪把手伸進冰涼的水裡。茶園像綠色的階梯覆蓋著山坡，森林濃密而茂盛。「這裡美極了，」她輕聲說。
那天夜裡，我們坐在農舍的門廊上看星星。艾瑪說城市和山村簡直天差地遠，我也同意。相較之下，她的家鄉無論去哪裡看起來都差不多。但在這裡，只要幾個小時就能從一個世界來到另一個世界。登山客從四面八方趕來欣賞這些山，我想我明白為什麼。這座島很小，但風景在一天之內就能有很大的變化。艾瑪說這是個非凡的地方，而我也第一次透過她的眼睛看見自己的家。

options: Sailors once called it Formosa, meaning "beautiful."
Its mountains were the highest in the world.

It was smaller than her hometown.

questions.stem: The word "lush" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: lush 指植物「茂盛的」，句中形容森林濃密而茂盛，與 thick and green 最接近，故選 (B)。(A) dry 與茂盛的森林語意相反。
questions.evidence: Tea fields covered the hills like green steps, and the forests were thick and lush.

questions.stem: Why did the writer laugh when Emma asked, "Is it always this crowded?"
options: She thought Emma was afraid of the market.
She wanted to leave the night market.
She thought the crowd was small for a night market.
She did not understand the question.
questions.explain: 作者笑著說這晚算是安靜的，可見她認為這樣的人潮對夜市而言並不算多，故選 (C)。艾瑪還主動要了第二塊臭豆腐，並非害怕夜市，(A) 不合。
questions.evidence: I laughed and said that this was a quiet evening.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to take a bus to Nantou
Why Canada is more crowded than Taiwan
How the writer showed her cousin two very different sides of Taiwan
What kinds of food visitors can find in Taipei

questions.evidence: Yet it takes only a few hours to travel from one world to the other here.

vocab.stem: The train station was ______ with travelers on the first day of the holiday.
vocab.explain: 假期第一天車站擠滿旅客、熱鬧非凡，bustling with 最合，故選 (C)。majestic（雄偉的）、lush（茂盛的）、exceptional（傑出的）都不能用來形容擠滿旅客的車站。

vocab.stem: The weather in the mountains can change ______ within a few hours.
vocab.explain: 山區天氣幾小時內可能「大幅」改變，considerably 修飾動詞 change 最通順，故選 (B)。densely（密集地）只能形容人口或植物，不能修飾天氣變化。

title: Meat Without a Farm
connect: 課文談實驗室培養肉的優點與疑慮，這篇看一位高中生在大學開放日聽研究生說明，並學習不要太快下結論。
paragraphs: Last month my class visited a university open day. In the food science building, a graduate student showed us a small dish holding a thin, pale layer of [[tissue|L0-0250]]. "This is meat," she said, "but no animal was raised for it." Scientists take a few muscle cells from an animal and feed them inside a clean machine until they multiply. The idea is not [[primitive|L4-0764]] at all. It needs precise tools and exact timing, and it is still a very [[recent|L0-0052]] field of research.

Why would anyone go to so much trouble? She explained that raising [[livestock|L6-0516]] needs a great deal of land, water, and food for the animals. If we could grow meat from cells instead, some of that pressure might be lifted. Nobody can [[estimate|L4-0361]] exactly how much the environment would benefit, she added, because the technology is so new. Still, many scientists think it is worth trying.

She was also honest about the [[concerns|T-0239]]. At present, making this kind of meat on a large [[scale|L3-0759]] is very difficult. The machines are expensive, and the process uses [[substantial|L5-0863]] amounts of energy. Whole factories would have to be built, which means new [[infrastructure|L5-0461]] and a lot of money. "[[In theory|P-0289]], the price will fall when production grows," she said. "But in theory and in the supermarket are two different things." Meat also gives us protein and important [[minerals|L4-0638]], so a lab version must match real meat in nutrition, not just in taste.

A classmate asked whether the meat would be safe for people who are [[allergic|L5-0034]] to some foods. The graduate student said that researchers study such [[reactions|L3-0700]] carefully, and that governments must approve a new food before anyone can sell it. I left the building [[somewhat|L0-0243]] hopeful but not fully sure. We should not [[jump to conclusions|P-0291]], whether for or against this new food. Instead, we should [[keep a close eye on|P-0292]] the research and keep asking good questions.
zh: 上個月我們班參觀了一所大學的開放日。在食品科學大樓裡，一位研究生給我們看一個小培養皿，裡面有一層薄薄的淺色組織。「這是肉，」她說，「但沒有任何動物是為了它而被飼養的。」科學家從動物身上取下少量肌肉細胞，在乾淨的機器裡餵養它們，直到它們增生。這個想法一點也不原始，它需要精密的工具和準確的時間掌握，而且仍是一個非常新的研究領域。
為什麼有人要這麼費事？她解釋，飼養家畜需要大量的土地、水，以及給動物吃的飼料。如果我們改用細胞來培養肉，這些壓力也許能減輕一些。她補充說，因為這項技術太新，沒有人能準確估計環境到底能得到多少好處。儘管如此，許多科學家仍認為值得一試。
她也坦白說出了令人擔憂的地方。目前要大規模製造這種肉非常困難，機器價格昂貴，製程也要耗費大量能源。還必須蓋整座工廠，這代表要有新的基礎建設和很多錢。「理論上，產量變大後價格會下降，」她說，「但理論上和在超市裡是兩回事。」肉類還提供我們蛋白質和重要的礦物質，所以實驗室版本不能只在味道上，也要在營養上跟真正的肉相當。
一位同學問，這種肉對於對某些食物過敏的人是否安全。研究生說，研究人員會仔細研究這類反應，而且新食品必須經政府核准才能販售。我離開大樓時有點抱著希望，但並不完全確定。無論是贊成或反對這種新食物，我們都不該妄下結論。相反地，我們應該密切留意研究的進展，並持續提出好問題。

questions.stem: According to paragraph 1, how do scientists make this kind of meat?
options: They mix plants with water in a kitchen.
They raise animals in a very small space.
They grow a few muscle cells in a clean machine.
They cut meat into thin pieces and freeze it.
questions.explain: 第一段說科學家取下少量肌肉細胞，放進乾淨的機器裡餵養直到增生，故選 (C)。這種肉不是靠飼養動物取得，(B) 與文意相反。
questions.evidence: Scientists take a few muscle cells from an animal and feed them inside a clean machine until they multiply.

questions.stem: The phrase "in theory" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: according to an idea that may or may not work in real life
questions.explain: in theory 是「理論上」，指按想法應該如此，但實際不一定，所以研究生接著說理論和超市是兩回事，故選 (B)。(C) 與時間長短無關。
questions.evidence: "But in theory and in the supermarket are two different things."

questions.stem: What does the graduate student seem to think about lab-grown meat?
options: It will soon replace all other food.
It is dangerous and should be stopped.
It has not been studied by scientists.
It has promise, but it still faces real problems.
questions.explain: 她既說明可能減輕環境壓力，也坦白指出成本、能源與基礎建設等問題，可見她認為有潛力但仍有難題，故選 (D)。她沒有說會取代所有食物，(A) 太過誇大。
questions.evidence: She was also honest about the concerns.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Lab-grown meat is already sold in every supermarket.
Allergies are the biggest problem in modern food.
Farms will soon disappear from the world.
Lab-grown meat has benefits and problems, so we should learn more before judging it.
questions.explain: 全文介紹培養肉的做法、可能的好處、各種擔憂，最後建議不要妄下結論、持續關注，故選 (D)。過敏只是同學提出的一個問題，(B) 說是最大問題並不正確。
questions.evidence: We should not jump to conclusions, whether for or against this new food.

vocab.stem: Building a new subway line takes ______ amounts of money and time.
vocab.explain: 建造地鐵需要「大量」的金錢與時間，substantial amounts of 最合，故選 (D)。primitive（原始的）、allergic（過敏的）、recent（最近的）都不能修飾 amounts。

vocab.stem: The doctor asked if the patient had any bad ______ to the medicine.
vocab.explain: 醫生問病人對藥物有沒有不良「反應」，reactions to 為固定搭配，故選 (C)。scales（規模；秤）、tissues（組織）、estimates（估計）都不能與 bad ... to the medicine 搭配。

title: Water at Grandma's Door
connect: 課文談威尼斯因海水上升與地層下陷而面臨淹水，這篇看台灣西南沿海的一座小鎮如何面對同樣的問題。
paragraphs: My grandmother lives in a small town near the southwest coast of Taiwan. When my mother was young, it was a [[tranquil|T-0243]] place with [[vast|L4-0978]] fish ponds and narrow roads. Today, when the [[tide|L3-0910]] is high and a storm is near, sea water sometimes comes up through the drains and onto the street. Last summer I saw it myself. The water was [[literally|T-0244]] at my grandmother's front step, and she calmly moved her shoes onto a chair.

My science teacher told me that two things cause this. First, the sea is rising. As the Earth gets warmer, ice in [[polar|L6-0677]] regions begins to [[melt|L3-0530]], and the extra water flows into the oceans. Second, in some coastal areas the land itself is going down. For many years, farmers pumped [[excessive|L5-0355]] amounts of water from underground, and the ground slowly sank, just as a sponge becomes smaller when you squeeze it. [[Owing to|P-0298]] both problems, the sea now seems to climb higher every year. [[In consequence|P-0294]], my grandmother's town has to [[contend with|P-0295]] flooding more often than before.

The town is not waiting for help. The government built higher walls near the water, and farmers have been asked to use less underground water. Engineers measure the land every year to [[confirm|L3-0181]] how fast it is sinking. Because the [[elevation|T-0245]] of the town is only a few meters above the sea, even small changes matter. Everyone knows that the best way to [[curb|L6-0215]] the problem is to stop making it worse.

When I asked my grandmother whether she wanted to move, she shook her head. "This is my home," she said. The situation is [[far from|P-0299]] hopeless, but the [[outlook|L6-0626]] depends on what people decide to do now. I hope that when my own [[generation|L4-0439]] grows up, we will know how to live beside the sea without being afraid of it.
zh: 我的外婆住在台灣西南沿海附近的一座小鎮。我媽媽小時候，那裡是個寧靜的地方，有廣大的魚塭和狹窄的小路。如今，每逢漲潮又有風暴接近時，海水有時會從排水孔湧上來，漫到街上。去年夏天我親眼看到了。海水確確實實漫到外婆家的門階前，而她鎮定地把鞋子搬到椅子上。
我的自然老師告訴我，這是由兩件事造成的。第一，海平面正在上升。隨著地球變暖，極地地區的冰開始融化，多出來的水流進海洋。第二，在某些沿海地區，土地本身正在下沉。多年來，農民從地下抽取過量的水，地面慢慢下陷，就像海綿被擠壓後會變小一樣。由於這兩個問題，海水似乎一年比一年高。因此，外婆的小鎮必須比以前更常應付淹水。
小鎮並沒有坐等別人幫忙。政府在靠水的地方築起更高的堤牆，也要求農民少用地下水。工程師每年測量土地，以確認它下沉得有多快。因為小鎮的海拔只比海面高幾公尺，連小小的變化都很重要。大家都知道，抑制這個問題最好的方法，就是不要讓它變得更糟。
當我問外婆想不想搬家時，她搖搖頭。「這裡是我的家，」她說。情況絕非沒有希望，但前景要看人們現在做什麼決定。我希望等到我這個世代長大時，我們已經知道如何與海為鄰，而不再害怕它。

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, why is the land in some coastal areas going down?
options: Too much water was taken from underground.
Large ships make the ground weaker.
Farmers have planted too many trees.
The tide pulls the land into the sea.
questions.explain: 第二段說多年來農民抽取過量地下水，地面因此慢慢下陷，故選 (A)。文中沒有提到船隻或種樹，(B)(C) 都是無中生有。
questions.evidence: For many years, farmers pumped excessive amounts of water from underground, and the ground slowly sank, just as a sponge becomes smaller when you squeeze it.

questions.stem: The phrase "contend with" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: contend with 是「應付、對付」，指小鎮得面對更頻繁的淹水，與 deal with 最接近，故選 (B)。argue with（與人爭論）不能用來說面對淹水。
questions.evidence: In consequence, my grandmother's town has to contend with flooding more often than before.

questions.stem: What can we infer about the writer's grandmother?
options: She is angry at the government.
She does not understand why the water comes.
She plans to move to a big city soon.
She has learned to stay calm and she loves her home.
questions.explain: 外婆在水到門階時冷靜地把鞋子搬上椅子，又說這裡是她的家、不想搬走，可推論她很鎮定且愛她的家，故選 (D)。她沒有表現出生氣或要搬走，(A)(C) 皆與文意不符。
questions.evidence: "This is my home," she said.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why fish ponds are important to farmers
How a coastal town faces flooding caused by rising seas and sinking land
How scientists measure the temperature of the ocean
Why the writer wants to become an engineer
questions.explain: 全文從外婆家淹水談起，說明海平面上升與地層下陷兩個原因，以及小鎮的因應，主旨為 (B)。魚塭只在第一段作為背景提到，(A) 並非重點。
questions.evidence: The town is not waiting for help.

vocab.stem: When the snow began to ______, the river rose quickly.
vocab.explain: 雪開始「融化」，河水才會迅速上升，melt 最合，故選 (C)。curb（抑制）、confirm（確認）、contend（爭奪）都不能以 snow 作主詞表達這個語意。

vocab.stem: Doctors say that ______ use of a mobile phone can harm your eyes.
vocab.explain: 醫生說「過度」使用手機會傷害眼睛，excessive use 最合，故選 (D)。tranquil（寧靜的）、solid（堅固的）、vast（廣大的）與 use 的語意不搭。

title: Why a Speech Moves Us
connect: 課文是一篇追求平等的著名演講，這篇看一位台灣高中生在演講課研究它的修辭，並寫出自己的「夢想」講稿。
paragraphs: In our speech class, Ms. Wu played a recording from 1963. A huge crowd had gathered in front of a [[memorial|L4-0625]] in Washington, D.C., at the end of a long [[march|L3-0519]] for equal rights. A civil rights leader named Martin Luther King Jr. stood before them and spoke about a dream of equality. It was a [[decisive|L6-0222]] moment in American history. Even though the recording was old and the English was fast, I felt my skin tingle. Why does this speech still move people so many years later?

Ms. Wu asked us to study its [[rhetorical|T-0251]] skills. Our homework was to write an [[outline|L3-0596]] of the speech and mark the parts that worked best. I noticed that the speaker repeated key phrases again and again, so the speech sounded like music, almost like a [[symphony|L6-0902]]. His [[eloquence|T-0250]] did not come only from beautiful words. It also came from clear ideas. He spoke about [[racism|L5-0688]] and [[segregation|T-0248]], which kept people apart, and about the [[dignity|L4-0286]] that every person deserves. He appealed to the [[conscience|L4-0185]] of a whole nation, and the crowd listened.

Then Ms. Wu gave us a new task: write a short speech about a dream for our own school. I felt nervous, but I began to write. I dreamed of a campus where no student is laughed at for his accent or her family background. I dreamed of an old building where students with limited [[mobility|T-0249]] can reach every classroom, because our school has yet to build a ramp for the stairs. I also hoped that students and teachers would listen to one another, even when they disagree.

When I read my speech aloud, my voice shook at first. Afterward, my classmates clapped, and Ms. Wu smiled. She said that very few speeches [[go down in history|P-0300]], but every dream can start in a small place. "A dream will not [[live out|P-0303]] its own life," she told us. "You have to act on it." Now I plan to bring my idea to the student council. [[As long as|P-0301]] someone is willing to speak up, a school can change.
zh: 在我們的演講課上，吳老師播放了一段1963年的錄音。一大群人聚集在華盛頓特區的一座紀念館前，那是一場為了平等權利而走了很久的遊行的終點。一位名叫馬丁・路德・金恩的民權領袖站在他們面前，談起一個關於平等的夢想。那是美國歷史上具有決定性的一刻。儘管錄音很舊，英文又說得很快，我還是感到起了雞皮疙瘩。為什麼這篇演講在這麼多年後依然能感動人？
吳老師要我們研究它的修辭技巧。我們的作業是寫出演講的大綱，並標記出效果最好的部分。我注意到講者一次又一次重複關鍵的句子，所以整篇演講聽起來像音樂，幾乎像一首交響樂。他的口才不只來自優美的詞句，也來自清楚的想法。他談到使人們彼此隔開的種族歧視與隔離，也談到每個人都應享有的尊嚴。他訴諸整個國家的良心，而群眾專注地聆聽。
接著吳老師給我們一個新任務：為我們自己的學校寫一篇關於夢想的短講稿。我雖然緊張，還是動筆寫了。我夢想有一個校園，沒有學生會因為口音或家庭背景而被取笑。我夢想在一棟老建築裡，行動不便的學生也能到達每一間教室，因為我們學校的階梯還沒有蓋斜坡道。我也希望學生和老師即使意見不同，也能互相傾聽。
我大聲唸出講稿時，一開始聲音在發抖。唸完後，同學們鼓掌，吳老師也笑了。她說，很少有演講能名留青史，但每一個夢想都可以從一個小地方開始。「夢想不會自己活起來，」她對我們說，「你得採取行動。」現在我打算把我的想法帶到學生會去。只要有人願意站出來發聲，一所學校就能改變。

questions.stem: What was the homework Ms. Wu gave about the speech?
options: To learn the whole speech by heart
To write an outline and mark the best parts
To translate the speech into Chinese
To record a new version of it
questions.explain: 第二段說作業是寫出演講的大綱並標記效果最好的部分，故選 (B)。文中沒有要求背誦或翻譯，(A)(C) 都是無中生有。
questions.evidence: Our homework was to write an outline of the speech and mark the parts that worked best.

questions.stem: The word "decisive" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: important and able to change the result
questions.explain: decisive 指「具決定性的」，形容那一刻對美國歷史有重大影響，與 important and able to change the result 最接近，故選 (A)。(B) 輕鬆快速與重大的歷史時刻不符。
questions.evidence: It was a decisive moment in American history.

questions.stem: Why did the writer mention the old building without a ramp?
options: She wanted to show that the school has a problem worth fixing.
She thought the school should be torn down.
She wanted to praise the school's new design.
She was afraid of climbing the stairs.
questions.explain: 她在講稿中提到階梯沒有斜坡道，是要指出學校行動不便的學生遇到的困難，也是她想改變的地方，故選 (A)。文中並沒有說要拆掉學校或稱讚新設計，(B)(C) 不合。
questions.evidence: I dreamed of an old building where students with limited mobility can reach every classroom, because our school has yet to build a ramp for the stairs.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How speeches in America have changed over time
Why Ms. Wu is the best teacher in the school
What a student learned from a famous speech and how she turned it into a dream for her school
How to build a ramp for an old building
questions.explain: 全文從研究名演講的修辭，到寫出自己對學校的夢想並打算付諸行動，主旨為 (C)。(D) 斜坡道只是她夢想的一個例子，不是全文重點。
questions.evidence: Then Ms. Wu gave us a new task: write a short speech about a dream for our own school.

vocab.stem: The mayor placed flowers at the war ______ to remember the people who died long ago.
vocab.explain: 市長在戰爭「紀念碑」前獻花，war memorial 是固定說法，故選 (B)。outline（大綱）、symphony（交響樂）、conscience（良心）都不能與 war 組成合理的地點。

vocab.stem: Every person should be treated with ______, no matter where he or she comes from.
vocab.explain: 每個人都應受到有「尊嚴」的對待，with dignity 最通順，故選 (C)。racism（種族歧視）、segregation（隔離）、fatigue（疲勞）都是負面事物，不能放在 treated with 後作為應有的態度。
